0x1330c.purpose: The scrolling credits roll. 0x3CDF0 blacks the palette (fg_getdacs into 0xF8B40, fg_setdacs from a zeroed 0xF5D58); message.gif ([0xC19D0], cat_show(name, 3, [0xF40D8] = ACIV.CT2)) is drawn into the background buffer [0xF52CC] (byte [0xF52D0] = 0x15), copied to the back buffer and pasted to the screen; 0x3CE44("pal.pal") sets the palette (fg_gifpal into 0xF8B40, copy to 0xF5D58, fg_setdacs). Font 2, colour 13. For k = 0 .. count-11 (count = int32 [0xC8038] = 63, so 53 windows): the strip (0x50..0x22F, 0x5A..0x1A3) is restored from the background, then 11 lines i = 0..10 of record k+i are drawn at y = 0x5A + 30i: type 2 (the title "A D V A N C E D   C I V I L I Z A T I O N ~") through f3A18C(0x50, y, 0x1E0, colour 0x45) then font 2 and colour 13 again; types 0 and 1 centred with f3A0B0(0x50, y, 0x1E0); type 1 (the headings: Producer, Executive Producer, Program and AI Design, AI Design Nemesis, Game Programming, Ancillary Programming, Computer Graphics, Animations, Music, Sound Effects, Testing Coordination, Manual, Original Boardgame Design (Thank You!)) gets an underline fg_move/fg_draw at y + 0x15 from x 0x4E + (0x1E0 - w)/2 to + w + 2. Then 30 one-pixel steps: fg_vbpaste(0x50, 0x22F, 0x5A + j, 0x185 + j, 0x50, 0x185) from the back buffer, each after a clock wait.
0x1330c.globals: credit table 0xC7EFC + 5i {int8 type (read as dword [0xC7EF9 + 5i] sar 24), uint32 text at 0xC7EFD + 5i}, int32 count [0xC8038] (obj2, 63 records: 10 blank, title, 51 name/heading/blank rows, blanks); [0xC19D0] -> "message.gif"; [0xF40D8] ACIV.CT2 handle; [0xF52CC] background vb, [0xF52C8] back buffer; writes byte [0xF52D0] = 0x15; [0xBB3F4] wait divisor (10 with /C); 0xE1634/0xE1635 fg_intkey bytes; palette buffers 0xF8B40 / 0xF5D58 (inside 0x3CDF0/0x3CE44)
0x1330c.calls: 0x3CDF0 (unported: palette to black), fg_vbopen, fg_move, cat_show, fg_vbclose, fg_vbcopy, fg_vbpaste, 0x3CE44 (unported: palette from pal.pal), f39F90, fg_setcolor, clock 0x8A080, f3A0B0, f3A18C, fgf_width, fg_draw, fg_intkey
0x1330c.callers: main 0x1101D (after the intro, unless int16 [0xF40BE] or int16 [0xF52DC] is set), f14294 at 0x1464D (after Final Civilization Standings)
0x1330c.waits_for_input: Keyboard only: fg_intkey(0xE1634, 0xE1635) once per line; any key ends the roll. Otherwise clock-paced busy waits: each pixel step waits until clock() > start + (40 / [0xBB3F4]) / 10 (Watcom hundredths, about 4/100 s; 4/1000 with /C); no mouse.
0x1330c.risks: Busy-waits on clock (headless runs must not wait, as f78A20); type bytes read through the dword-sar-24 idiom; the two palette helpers 0x3CDF0/0x3CE44 are unported; the k loop runs while k < count - 10 (signed), so the last window starts at record 52; the title string ends in '~' (glyph to check in COGNAC19); the first step skips the wait only via a local flag ([ebp-0x2C]), the rest re-read clock() after each paste.

0x13d44.purpose: Census order of play. First f79270(100, int16 [0xF06B0] (the first entry of the current player list, read as dword [0xF06AE] sar 16), -200 (home view), "" (0xB0EC0), 0): a 100 ms redraw of the map at that nation's home view. Then int16 [0xF0698] = number of nations 1..9 in play (byte +0x9A != 0) and int16 0xF069A[] = those nations in ascending order, and qsort(0xF069A, count, 2, 0x13DE8). The comparator 0x13DE8 (address-taken, 104 bytes) sorts by nation byte +0x98 (tokens on the board, G: population) descending, ties by nation number ascending (it returns -1 for a <= b on the tie, never 0).
0x13d44.globals: reads nation byte +0x9A (0xF1566 + 199n), +0x98 (0xF1564 + 199n, in 0x13DE8); writes int16 [0xF0698] (count) and int16 0xF069A[10] (order); reads int16 [0xF06B0]
0x13d44.calls: 0x79270 (unported message/redraw routine: wait, nation, view, text, animation), qsort 0x8C331 with comparator 0x13DE8
0x13d44.callers: 0x5195C at 0x52F22 (G: PBEM), the game loop 0x54824 at 0x5497D
0x13d44.waits_for_input: No input; f79270 with 100 waits 100 ms (f78A20).
0x13d44.risks: qsort with a comparator that returns -1 for equal keys: keys are distinct (nation numbers), so any correct sort gives Watcom's order; the count is passed as dword [0xF0696] sar 16 (the int16 at 0xF0698); comparator is a function pointer (port as a C qsort callback).

0x14294.purpose: Final Civilization Standings. Builds a local array of {int16 score, int16 nation} for nations 1..9 in play (score = f147C4(n)), bubble-sorts it by score descending (strictly greater swaps whole dwords). With the continuous-test flag [0xF628C] == 0: background 0x17 (f3CD6C), copied to the back buffer; title "Final Civilization Standings" via f3A18C(2, 6, 0x280, colour 0xB0); font 2, colour 5; for row r < int32 [0xF40EC]: the nation's 35x35 token (sprite 0xF4A5C + 8n) at (0xDB, 49r + 0x2A) and (0x183, 49r + 0x2A), the name centred at y 49r + 0x28 (width 640) with an underline at y 49r + 0x3C, the score centred at y 49r + 0x3F (f3A148). The shared CONTINUE button 0x2A of dialog 0xBB800 is relabelled "EXIT" (font 1) and moved to x 0x109, y = 49R + 0x28 + (0x1DC - (49R + 0x28) - 0x13)/2 (R = rows). f3B05C(0xBB800), f3CC14, music f7B854("gcivil2_.xmi " [0xCAB1C], 0) and AIL_set_sequence_loop_count(1) when music is on; waits for EXIT; hides the mouse (f78884) and runs the credits f1330C. With [0xF628C] != 0 (the /C continuous test): appends to ctest.txt (fopen 0x7D8C8 mode "at") "End of game %d." ([0xBC8DC]), the memory statistics through 0x7762C (number formatting into 0xF5500), "Max WorldStack: %d Max MoveStack: %d Max RouteList: %d" ([0x112A8C], [0x112A90], [0x109E04]) and "RoutingMax: %d" ([0x10818C]), fclose (0x7D95E); [0xBC8DC] + 1; [0xF6290] cycles 0..[0xBC8E0]-1; then f3FB94(0x51) (START NEW GAME, a longjmp) as a tail call.
0x14294.globals: reads nation +0x9A; int32 [0xF40EC] (rows drawn); [0xF628C] continuous test; [0xF625D] music on, [0xF6284] sequence handle; writes dialog 0xBB800 record 0x2A label/x/y (permanent), [0xF8E78] (via f3B05C); ctest branch: [0xBC8DC], [0xBC8E0], [0xF6290], [0xF52D8] (FILE*), [0xF605C], [0xF6060], 0xF5500, [0x112A8C], [0x112A90], [0x109E04], [0x10818C]
0x14294.calls: f147C4, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, fg_vbopen, f3A18C, fg_setcolor, f39F90, f3AF8C, f3A0B0, fgf_width, fg_move, fg_draw, f3A148, f3C284, f3BB48, f3BC64, fg_vbclose, f3B05C, f3CC14, f7B854, AIL_set_sequence_loop_count 0x85BBF, f78BA4, f78884, 0x1330C (credits), fopen 0x7D8C8, fprintf, 0x7762C (unported number-to-text), fclose 0x7D95E, f3FB94(0x51)
0x14294.callers: 0x22F3C at 0x2309E, 0x230B8 at 0x23208 (G: eliminations ending the game), the game loop 0x54824 at 0x5522C (AST win)
0x14294.waits_for_input: Normal game: f78BA4(0xBB800, 0) until -1 (EXIT), -100 loops; then the credits' fg_intkey loop. Continuous test: none.
0x14294.risks: Rows are drawn for r < [0xF40EC] while the array only holds the nations in play: if [0xF40EC] exceeds that count it reads uninitialised stack entries (G: they are equal in practice); the EXIT label and the moved button are never restored in 0xBB800 (later CONTINUE dialogs inherit them unless they set them again); the /C branch ends in a longjmp (setjmp 0xF58D4); ctest.txt writes must stay in the game folder; music/AIL calls are port no-ops.

0x14a00.purpose: Loads the computer opening maps for every nation in play when a play-by-email game is created: for n = 1..9 with byte +0x9A != 0, f14C6C(local 16-byte buffer, n) picks the .BPM name; if the override flag int32 [0xF60E8 + 4n] is set the override name 0xF6064 + 13n is used instead; f15FE0(n, name) loads the three 160-byte tables. Then memcpy(0xEF3C4, 0xEED84, 0x640) (the base priorities).
0x14a00.globals: nation +0x9A; [0xF60E8 + 4n] override flags, 0xF6064 + 13n override names (dead developer switch, OVERVIEW egg 14); writes 0xEED84[10][160], 0xF0044, 0xEFA04 (through f15FE0) and 0xEF3C4[10][160]
0x14a00.callers: main 0x118B1, only when flags byte [0xE1624] has both 0x04 (new game) and 0x80 (PBEM); main then calls 0x4FE30, sets int16 [0xF408A] = -92 and jumps back to the title menu 0x11168
0x14a00.risks: PBEM-only path (dropped by Erik's ruling): only needed if PBEM is ever ported; local 16-byte stack buffer handed to f14C6C/f15FE0; the loop is laid out with the call in the middle (both branches jump to 0x14A38).

0x14aa4.purpose: For a restored game: for n = 1..9 in play whose override flag int32 [0xF60E8 + 4n] is set, reload the override opening map f15FE0(n, 0xF6064 + 13n); the normal tables come from the save. Then memcpy(0xEF3C4, 0xEED84, 0x640). The function is 0x92 bytes; the rest of the 456-byte range (0x14B38..0x14C6B) is 14C6C's jump tables.
0x14aa4.globals: nation +0x9A; [0xF60E8 + 4n], 0xF6064 + 13n; reads 0xEED84[10][160] (restored from the save), writes 0xEF3C4[10][160]
0x14aa4.callers: main 0x1189C, when byte [0xE1624] has neither 0x04 (new game) nor 0x80 (PBEM): every restored non-PBEM game, before the game loop
0x14aa4.risks: The override flags are always 0 (main clears them), so in practice only the copy runs. The copy takes the saved, already-adjusted priorities (f160EC adds +5) as the new base 0xEF3C4, which is not in the save (saveload.c reads only 0xEED84): G, a restore may make the +5 bonus cumulative; check against DOSBox-X. Size includes another function's jump tables (do not translate them here).

0x160ec.purpose: Refreshes nation n's (eax) territory priorities from the base copy: byte 0xF62A8[n] = 0, int32 [0xF62B4] = 0; for t = 0..159 with bit 0x04 of 0xF0044[160n + t]: 0xF62A8[n] = 1, t appended to the byte list 0xF62B8 + 5(n-1) + [0xF62B4]++, and 0xEED84[160n + t] = 0xEF3C4[160n + t] + 5 if nation n has tokens in the area of the canonical territory c = 0xC803C[t] (area record c + 1, int8 +0x0E + n > 0), else the base value. Territories without the 0x04 bit keep their current value.
0x160ec.globals: reads 0xF0044[10][160] (.bpm table 2), 0xEF3C4 (base), 0xC803C (canonical territory), area +0x0E+n (0xE31C7 + 69(c+1) + n-1, dword sar 24); writes 0xEED84[160n + t], byte 0xF62A8[n], int32 [0xF62B4], bytes 0xF62B8 + 5(n-1) + k
0x160ec.callers: 0x353C4 at 0x3546F, 0x461BC at 0x46230, 0x46BB8 at 0x46CAC (G: AI movement / expansion)
0x160ec.risks: The flagged-territory list has 5 bytes per nation but no bound: a 6th flagged territory writes into the next nation's list (G: the .bpm files flag few); [0xF62B4] is a single global reset per call; signed byte reads via movsx; the +5 is added to the base, so it never accumulates within a game (but see 0x14AA4).

0x162d0.category: phase: civilization advance acquisition (human UI + AI)
0x162d0.purpose: The Acquire Civilization Tools phase (debug tag "Acquire Civ"). Setup: player list 0xF06AE/0xF06B0 (nations in play), f783B8(0xF634C, [0xF5968]) labels, malloc(199) -> [0xEED78], int32 [0xF68AC] = fgf_width("Still needed"), RESTART 0x41 disabled (f3BFBC), background byte [0xEE168] = 0x12. For n = 1..9: the record is backed up into [0xEED78], the 9 discard stacks 0xF07B4 (25 bytes each) into a local copy, 0xF6D54 + 19n + 1..18 (cards spent) cleared, [0xF40F8] = n, [0xF68C8] (carry forward), [0xF6740], [0xF6744] = 0; Grain set aside for Famine (int16 0xF409A[n]) is subtracted from card count +0x08 and added back at the end. HUMAN (byte +0x9A == 3, or the PBEM local player): advance buttons 0x8E..0xA5 labelled 0xC7DC4[i], f194E4 (Mining list), f17EDC(n, -1, 1) (affordability, colours); if nothing is affordable the nation is skipped; else f1818C(n, 0), 0x6FBDC(n, 1) (REVEAL GOODS hot-seat prompt), 0x6D0C4(7, 0x196, 0x23A, n) (hand), POINTS = f195D8(n); then its own click loop on dialog 0xF634C. Codes (from f3FB94): -0x63 (id 0x41 RESTART): record and discard stacks restored, purchases cleared; -0x40/-0x41 (0xA7/0xA8): treasury used [0xF67E0] -1 / +1 (at most +0x3E), f18DD8, 150 ms; -0x43/-0x44 (0xAA/0xAB): Mining choice [0xF68B0] -/+; -0x3E (0x8E..0xA5, [0xF6758] = index): f1818C(n, 1), and f18DD8 if state 2; -0x3F (0xA6 ACQUIRE): byte +0x24+i = 1 ([0xF6740] = 1 for Mining), index appended to int16 0xF6E12 + 10n (count int16 0xF6E76 + 2n), label upper case 0xC7E24[i], colour 0x0F, RESTART enabled, carry forward = -still-needed if negative, treasury -= [0xF67E0], stock +0x99 += it, each goods card (0xF67E4[i]) moves to the spent list 0xF6D54 + 19n + i and to the discard pile (0x771F8) and leaves the hand; card states recomputed with f6DD98 + credits + carry + treasury (colours 0x0A or 0x90 with the alternate-colours toggle bit 0 of [0xF0981], 0x0C not affordable); -0x1D (id 0x75): a click in the hand strip moves one card from scratch record 0 to the goods 0xF67E4 (hit test with the hand spacing [0x11254C]/[0x112550] from x 7); -0x42 (0xA9): a click in the goods strip moves it back (spacing [0xF6738]/[0xF673C] from x 0x10A); after each, f18C68(0), f19170, f18DD8; -1 (0x2A FINISHED) ends the nation. COMPUTER (+0x9A == 2): up to three purchases: f17EDC(n, -1, 1), f1A888 (desirability), f177EC (choice) into 0xF6E12/14/16 + 10n, each tentatively owned and the remaining budget f176BC + f195D8 + treasury - costs passed to f17EDC(n, budget, 0); then the total still needed (costs - credits f176BC) goes to f1B59C(n, need); if it fails all purchases are undone (count 0); else the chosen cards (scratch record 0) are spent, treasury -= [0xF6750], stock += [0xF6750], advances owned, labels set, and a summary is drawn: f1818C(n, 0), f19170, "Goods toward purchase", "Applied Mining to" + IRON/BRONZE/SILVER/GEMS/GOLD (0xBDD44), "Credits Used", "Goods Used" (f193AC), "Treasury Used", token sprite 0xF49EC + 8n, treasury, then f19700(n, count, 0xF6E12 + 10n) ("%s has acquired ..." box). PBEM non-local humans: f17EDC(n, -1, 0) only. Every nation: +0x5E = f17760(n). After the loop: int16 [0xF409A + 2*10] = 0 (n is 10 here), free([0xEED78]), [0xEED78] = 0; if no nation could buy anything, f79270(100, int16 [0xF06B0], -200, "", 0).
0x162d0.globals: nation records (+0x01..+0x12 cards, +0x08 grain count, +0x24..+0x3B advances, +0x3E treasury, +0x5E advance points, +0x99 stock, +0x9A); scratch nation record 0 (0xF14CC, its cards); discard stacks 0xF07B4 + 25s; 0xF409A int16[10] grain used against Famine; [0xF40F8] current nation; dialog 0xF634C (BSS, count int16, records from 0xF634E); [0xF6758] selected advance, [0xF675C] previous; 0xF6764 int32[24] credits; [0xF6760] hand value; byte 0xF67C4[24] states (0 no, 1 owned, 2 affordable; read as dword [0xF67C1 + i] sar 24); 0xF67E4[19] goods toward purchase (+0x13 calamity count); [0xF67DC] still needed, [0xF67E0] treasury used, [0xF68C8] carry forward, [0xF6740] Mining bought, [0xF6744], [0xF6750] AI treasury, byte [0xF6754] Mining flag, [0xF68B0] Mining choice, [0xF68B4] Mining list count, 0xF68B8/0xF68C0 lists; 0xF6D54 + 19n spent cards; int16 0xF6E12 + 10n purchase list, int16 0xF6E76 + 2n count; [0xEED78] heap backup; [0xF68AC]; [0xF0981] bit 0; byte [0xEE168]; 0xE1624 bit 0x80 and byte 0xE1622 (PBEM local player); tables 0xC7DC4/0xC7E24 names, 0xBD480 costs, 0xBD4B0 prerequisites (Roadbuilding and Mining need Engineering, Democracy and Philosophy need Law, Monotheism and Theology need Enlightenment)
0x162d0.calls: f783B8, malloc 0x822B5, 0x78B0C (debug log no-op), fgf_width, f3BFBC, 0x3B914 (unported: set pressed byte), f3C284, f194E4, 0x17EDC, 0x1818C, 0x6FBDC (unported REVEAL GOODS), 0x6D0C4 (unported), fg_setcolor, f3A0B0, f195D8, itoa, f3CD6C, f775F0, fg_mousepos, f3C5D4, f3FB94, 0x18DD8, f78A20, 0x3BEA0 (unported: label colour), f3C314, 0x3C48C (unported: enable a button and redraw it on the active surface), 0x771F8 (unported: card to discard pile), f6DD98, 0x18C68, 0x19170, 0x1A888, 0x177EC, 0x176BC, 0x1B59C, f3A044, f3C9D0, f3A3A0, 0x193AC, f3AF8C, 0x19700, f17760, free, 0x79270
0x162d0.waits_for_input: Human nations: its own click loop: f775F0, fg_mousepos until [0xE1630] != 0, a manual hit test of dialog 0xF634C (enabled byte == 1, x <= [0xE1628] < x+w, y <= [0xE162C] < y+h), f3C5D4 + f3FB94(id); -100 polls again; -1 ends. 0x162d0.risks: 5100 bytes with a long if-chain on dispatcher codes; scratch nation record 0 is overwritten (other code reads record 0: f6DD98 callers 0x69B59/0x6A28E); [0xEED78] doubles as 0x7A4F0's nation snapshot pointer (G: no overlap in time); the final clear writes only index 10 of 0xF409A (harmless: 0x1E0A0 clears all 10 each calamity phase, G: meant per nation); the local 0xD8-byte copy of the discard stacks lives on the stack; hand hit tests depend on spacing globals set by unported drawing routines (0x71FB0 is ported, 0x19170 not); PBEM branches (dropped); the -0x3F path uses f6DD98 (no Mining bonus) where f17EDC uses f195D8 (G inconsistency, keep it).

0x176bc.purpose: Credit applied to computer nation n's purchase slot k (eax = n, edx = k): a = int16 0xF6E12 + 10n + 2k (the advance); returns min(cost int16 0xBD480[a], credit int32 0xF6764[a]).
0x176bc.globals: reads int16 0xF6E12 + 10n + 2k (via dword [0xF6E10 + ...] sar 16), 0xBD480 costs, 0xF6764 credits
0x176bc.risks: dword-sar-16 reads of int16 arrays; nothing else.

0x177ec.purpose: Chooses the advance computer nation n buys next, or -1. Candidates: i with state byte 0xF67C4[i] == 2 into 0xF7CA0 (count [0xF7C9C]). Group goal: the OR of the group masks (int16 0xBD510[i]: bit 0 crafts, 1 science, 2 arts, 3 civics, 4 religion) of owned advances, counted over 5 bits; if the AI table byte 0xBCCE2 + 85(n-1) + 5*pos (pos = AST square int8 +0x5C) exceeds that count, candidates whose mask adds no new group are dropped (if none is left, the full list is restored and a flag set). Points goal: need = 100 * byte 0xBCCE4 + 85(n-1) + 5*pos; if need > f17760(n), candidates with cost + points < need are dropped (same fallback, second flag). The list is bubble-sorted by desirability int32 0xF62EC[i] descending. If the nation [0xF52D4] is human (+0x9A == 3), owns Military (+0x35) and int32 0xF52E0 + 40n + 4*[0xF52D4] > 500, the top candidate is taken. Otherwise the list is cut to 4 and weighted (jump table 0x177CC by count: 1: s0; 2: 2*s0, s1; 3: s0 + 66 s0/100, s1 + 33 s1/100, s2; 4: s0 + 50%, s1 + 30%, s2 + 20%, s3), r = game_rand() * total >> 15, and the candidate is picked by cumulative weight (jump table 0x177DC). The choice stands only if f76F14(n) > 8 (G: cards in hand), or f1B538(n), or either fallback flag, or f1B45C(choice), or f1B4D4(n); otherwise -1 (wait and save).
0x177ec.globals: reads 0xF67C4 states, nation +0x24.. advances, +0x5C AST square, +0x9A; AI tables 0xBCCE2..0xBCFD9 (9 nations x 17 squares x 5 bytes, obj2), 0xBD510 group masks, 0xBD480 costs, 0xF62EC int32[24] desirability, [0xF52D4] (G: the leading nation), 0xF52E0 int32[10][10] (G: AI attitude matrix); writes [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0 (the shared candidate list)
0x177ec.risks: Two jump tables (0x177CC, 0x177DC, 4 entries each) sit in the byte range of the preceding f17760, not in this function; table reads by the dword-sar-24 idiom; the special-case branch reads int32 [0xF7CA0] after the sort; game_rand is drawn only on the weighted path (the order of draws matters for replay); entries set to -1 are compacted in place.

0x17edc.purpose: Which advances nation n (eax) can buy with budget edx, drawing if ebx == 1. With budget -1: [0xF6760] = f195D8(n) (hand value incl. Mining), credits int32 0xF6764[i] = sum over owned advances j of int8 0xBD240 + 25j + i (credit table, 25-byte rows), and budget = [0xF68C8] + hand + treasury (+0x3E); otherwise the budget as given and no credits. For each i 0..23: label 0x8E+i = 0xC7DC4[i]; owned: state 1, label upper case 0xC7E24[i], colour 0x0E if drawing; budget + credit < cost: state 0, colour 0x0C; prerequisite int16 0xBD4B0[i] == 0 or owned: state 2, colour 0x90 when bit 0 of [0xF0981] (Alternate Tool Acquisition Colors) else 0x0A; else state 0, colour 0x0C. Returns 1 if any advance is in state 2, and then sets int16 [0xF4092] = 1.
0x17edc.globals: nation +0x24.., +0x3E; 0xBD240 credit table, 0xBD480 costs, 0xBD4B0 prerequisites, 0xC7DC4/0xC7E24 names; [0xF68C8]; [0xF0981] bit 0; writes [0xF6760], 0xF6764[24], 0xF67C4[24], int16 [0xF4092], dialog 0xF634C labels and label colours
0x17edc.risks: The credit table row stride 25 (24 used) read by dword sar 24; the ebx draw flag only selects colour calls, labels are always set.

0x1818c.purpose: Draws the Acquire Civilization Tools screen for nation n (eax), mode edx (0 hand face down f71F2C, 1 face up f71FB0 + POINTS and hand value). Background int8 [0xEE168] copied to the back buffer; hand box int16 0x11158C..0x111592 = (7, 0x196, 0x23A, 0x2E); title "Acquire Civilization Tools" and the nation name (f3A18C); token sprite 0xF49EC + 8n and treasury (+0x3E); a coloured frame around each advance button (geometry from 0x3BBD8/0x3BCF4/0x3BA30/0x3BABC, colours int16 0xBD4E0[i], two-tone when the high byte is set). If [0xF6758] >= 0: button states (0x3B914), the name underlined at (0x115, 0x9C) and the description 0xC7E9C[i] wrapped (f3A42C, 0x104, 0xAB, 0xD1); if that advance is affordable (state 2): nation record n copied into scratch record 0, goods 0xF67E4 cleared (19 bytes), "Goods toward purchase", arrows 0xF51AC/0xF51B4, boxes "Carry Forward" ([0xF68C8]), "Credits" (0xF6764[sel]), "Goods" (f193AC), "From Treas." ([0xF67E0]), still needed/excess (f18AEC -> [0xF67DC], shown as absolute value), and with Mining "Apply Mining to" + 0xBDD44 name. If int16 0xF409A[n] != 0: "Already used to reduce Famine losses." and that many sprites 0xF4C5C, else that strip is restored. Buttons 0xA9, 0x75, 0xA7, 0xA8, 0xA6, 0xAA, 0xAB disabled, then enabled for an affordable selection (0xAA/0xAB only with Mining); f3B05C, f3CC14; with [0xF67DC] >= 0 ACQUIRE 0xA6 is disabled (0x3C530) and FINISHED 0x2A enabled (0x3C48C), else the reverse (D 0x18A9B).

If treasury is in use and need < 0, [0xF67E0] is reduced by the excess (not below 0), need recomputed and the From Treas. box (0x239, 0x10C) redrawn. 0x19448.risks: Duplicate of 0x193AC with another base (translate both).

0x19700.purpose:
Announces a computer purchase: sprintf(stack buffer, "%s has acquired 
", name[n]) then the names 0xC7DC4 of the count (edx) advances in the int16 list (ebx), joined by ", 
" or " and 
", then ".". The box width is the text width + 10, at least 180 and at most 350 (+20 test), height from f3A42C + 45, centred on the screen. The pressed bytes of the current dialog [0xF8E78] are saved into 0xF8E44 and cleared (records with ids 0x8E..0xA5 skipped), redrawn; the screen under the box is saved to the GIF file "junk" (fg_makegif); buttons 5, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 0x2A, 0x41, 0xA6 of [0xF8E78] shown up (0x3C530); box f3C9D0(flags 3), text, CONTINUE of dialog 0xBBBEC moved to the centre and labelled "CONTINUE"; then the wait; then [0xF8E78] restored with the saved pressed bytes, [0xF52D0] = 0, the "junk" GIF shown back at the box (fg_showgif flags 3), f3CCBC.

Scratch record 0 cleared (199 bytes); background 0x19; title "Tool Acquisition Wrapup" (sprintf into a stack buffer, f3A18C(0, 6, 0x280, 0xB0)); headings "Acquired" (0x3D, 0x1A) and "Using" (0xBE, 0x1A). One 49-px row per nation in play: separator line (0x3D..0x259 at 49r + 0x23) from the second row, token sprite 0xF4ACC + 8n centred in 51 px at x 5, name below in colour 15; the bought advances (upper case 0xC7E24) in colour 13 spread over the row (step 51/(count+1)); the cards spent (0xF6D54 + 19n) copied into record 0 and drawn face up by f71FB0(0xA0, 49r + 0x26, 0x1CC, 0). Dialog 0xBD940 (8 invisible full-width row buttons 0xB2..0xB9 and CONTINUE 0x2A) drawn, [0xF8E78] = 0xBD940, f3CC14, then the wait.

0x1a888.purpose: Scores the advances computer nation n might buy: 0xF62EC int32[24] cleared; m = max over nations k in play of int32 0xF52E0 + 40n + 4k (from -5000), its k kept; a = the LAST read value / [0xF40EC]. For each advance i not owned and in state 2 a case of jump table 0x1A828 (24 entries) sets 0xF62EC[i]: base values Pottery 45 (+50 if n is [0xF52D4] and m < -200), Clothmaking 45 (+30/+10/-10/+50/-20 by nation through table 0x1A7BC, +10 with +0x2B), Metalworking 80 (+80 if a nation j with byte 0x109E24 + 9n + j has Metalworking, +40 for contested territories, +20 per nation without Military, +30 Mining, +10 Agriculture...), Agriculture 110 (nation table 0x1A7E0, +30 if byte 0xF5934 + n > 0), Roadbuilding 140 (by nation, + (a-200)*8/300 + 60 capped at 100 when a > 200, +100 if tokens on board > 75% of [0xF4898], +25 if a neighbour flag is set), Mining 180 (+40 with Coinage +0x2C), Engineering 140 (+50 Egypt n 9, +35 Babylon n 8), Astronomy 80, Coinage 110 (+40 Mining, +40 if 0x1C2DC(n) > 0 i.e. short of tokens), Medicine 140, Mathematics 180 (+50 if credit >= 100), Drama & Poetry and Music 60 (stored at 0xF62EC + 4i), Architecture 120 (+8 per own territory below 9 with terr flag 0x40), Literacy 70, Law 140, Democracy 160, Military 180, Philosophy 160 (+80 if its credit >= 120), Mysticism 50, Deism 80, Enlightenment 150, Monotheism 220, Theology 250, each with adjustments by owned advances (+0x26 Metalworking, +0x28 Roadbuilding, +0x2B, +0x35 Military, +0x37..+0x3A) and by other nations' advances (+0x29..+0x2B of others: 0xF1505/06/07 + 199k).
0x1a888.globals: nation records (+0x24.. advances, +0x5D/+0x60 territory count (dword sar 24 = +0x60), +0x61.. territories, +0x98, +0x9A); area records (+0x01 nation count via dword [0xE31B6 + 69r] sar 24); land adjacency [0xF8E78 + 4r] (= 0xF8E7C + 4(r-1)); territory flags 0xE1639 + 35t; 0xF52E0 int32[10][10], [0xF52D4], [0xF40EC], [0xF4898], [0xF40F0], 0x109E24 + 9n + j, byte 0xF5934 + n, credits 0xF678C/0xF67A4/0xF67AC (0xF6764[10], [16], [18]), 0xF67C4 states; writes 0xF62EC[24]
0x1a888.risks: Four jump tables placed before the function (0x1A7BC, 0x1A7E0, 0x1A804: 9 entries by nation; 0x1A828: 24 by advance); per-case stores to fixed addresses except cases 11/12. BUG(1995) candidates (D reading, G intent): (1) the 'other nation present' test computes the ADDRESS 0xE31B8 + 69r + 2 and tests it for zero (0x1AAF5, 0x1AB59), so it is always true; (2) the average a takes the last value, not a sum (mov, 0x1A914); (3) the Metalworking neighbour loop reads nation record j for j 0..8 (record 0 and never nation 9) where the next loop uses j+1. A literal port must keep all three.

0x1b45c.purpose: Buy-anyway test for advance i: if cost(i) < score 0xF62EC[i], returns (game_rand() * 100 >> 15) < score - cost; else 0 (no draw).
0x1b45c.risks: The random draw is conditional; the multiply is done as 25*4 (shifts).

0x1b4d4.purpose: Returns 1 if nation n's stock (int8 +0x99) is smaller than cities (+0x51) times tax rate (+0x3F, 2 by default): G, cannot pay taxes.

0x1b538.purpose: Returns 1 if for some commodity i 1..18 nation n holds exactly int8 0xBD540[i] cards (the full set size: 7 7 7 8 8 9 7 8 6 7 5 6 5 6 4 5 4 5, obj2), else 0.

0x1b59c.purpose: Chooses which cards computer nation n pays for 'need' points (edx). Copies nation n's record into scratch record 0; [0xF6748] = min(0x1C2DC(n) (token shortfall), treasury), [0xF674C] = treasury. Then an 18-digit odometer over record 0's card counts (each digit counts down from the full count to 1, then wraps back and carries to the next commodity; the tolerance [ebp-0x1C] starts at 3 and grows by 3 the first time digits 3, 5, 7, ... 17 move): at each step 0x1BE08 evaluates the current reduced hand; an exact fit (1) applies its mask and returns 1; else the smallest excess so far (with its mask, the Mining choice, and a copy of the 32-byte candidate list 0xF68CC -> 0xF6B0C, count [0xF6D50]) is kept; when best < tolerance, the best mask is applied (record 0's cards zeroed, then the masked list entries' counts written back), [0xF6750] = max(0, need - f19448()) (treasury to add) and 1 is returned. When the odometer completes: 0.
0x1b59c.globals: scratch record 0 (written), nation n (read), [0xF6748], [0xF674C], [0xF6750] (written), [0xF68B0] (Mining choice), 0xF68CC/0xF6B0C candidate lists (32-byte entries), [0xF6D4C]/[0xF6D50] counts, 0xBC800 int32 bit masks (1 << k)
0x1b59c.risks: Hand-unrolled 18-level odometer with registers and stack flags interleaved (translate as a loop but keep the exact visiting order and the tolerance steps); possibly very many iterations (product of the card counts); passes stack pointers and two stack arguments to 0x1BE08 (ret 8); digits are compared through the dword-sar-24 idiom at shifted offsets.

0x1be08.purpose: Evaluates scratch record 0's hand for payment (eax n, edx need, ebx &excess, ecx &mask, stack: &exact_mask, first-call flag; ret 8). Builds the list 0xF68CC (count [0xF6D4C]) of 32-byte entries per held commodity i: +0x00 value used, +0x04 count, +0x08 id i, +0x10 Mining-eligible (ids 4, 11, 12, 16, 18), +0x14 face value (i+1)>>1, +0x18 c*c*v, +0x1C (c+1)^2*v (Mining). With Mining (+0x29) the eligible entries are tried in turn with the bonus value ([0xF68B0] set to the matching list index). Prefix sums over the list until sum + treasury >= need; if sum + [0xF6748] <= need the prefix mask is exact (returns 1); otherwise walks back dropping entries to find the smallest excess (masks of bit k per entry), writing *excess and *mask; returns 0, or 1 with *exact_mask on an exact fit.
0x1be08.globals: scratch record 0 (+1..+18, +0x29 Mining), 0xF68CC.. list, [0xF6D4C], [0xF68B0], [0xF68B4], 0xF68B8 (dword [0xF68B5 + k] sar 24), [0xF6748], [0xF674C], 0xBC800 masks
0x1be08.risks: Callee-pops two stack arguments (ret 8); out-pointers into the caller's frame; bit masks over up to 18 entries (int32); entries indexed by shl 5.

0x1c2dc.purpose: Token shortfall of nation n: need = cities (+0x51) * tax rate (+0x3F) + for each territory in its list (+0x60 count, +0x61.. territory+1): +1 if it has 1 token there, +2 if 2 or more (G: population growth); returns need - stock (+0x99) if the stock is smaller, else 0.

0x1c3d0.purpose: Runs the Barbarian Hordes for victim n (eax; edx passed on to 0x1D234). [0xF6F60] = 0, picture byte [0xEE168] = 3. "%s falls victim to the Barbarian Hordes." (f79270(-500 = CONTINUE wait, n, -200, text, 2)); "The Barbarians consider their destination." (-550: no wait); mouse hidden; 0x1C9FC(n) picks the landing; at least 1.5 s since that message (clock loop 1500/[0xBB3F4]/10); 0x1D234(n, edx, 15, &t). Then while the barbarians in t (area +0x19, nation 11) exceed the territory's limit (terr byte +1 bits 3..5): snapshot (0x7A4F0), visited 0xF6EBC[160] cleared and 157..159 set, the destination message, 0x1D858(n, t, remaining, route 0xF6E94, 0xF6EBC) (depth search), 1.5 s; the equal-best routes (same territory byte +2 and +0 low nibble as the first) go to 0xF7CA0; restore (0x7AB24). If no route (byte [0xF6E96] == 0xFF): [0xF6F60] = 1, message area moved (y 0x14C, h 0x7B), "The next destination has been referred to the BRPC (Barbarian Ravaging and Plundering Committee). Please wait. This could take several minutes." with the BRPC picture (anim -299), brpc.wav (sound on: f7B504, AIL volume = music volume*127/9, at least 1, loop forever), a deeper search (depth 20) under a snapshot, at least 4 s, sample stopped; still no route: the excess barbarians removed (f57CE8(t, 11, 0, excess)) and "The BRPC is deadlocked. They decide to settle in %s." Otherwise 0x1D234 moves on; when nation n has no cities (+0x95 = +0x98? read as dword [0xF1561] sar 24) and no tokens (dword [0xF151A] sar 24 = +0x51 cities) the excess is removed and "%s has been wiped out by the Barbarians. Satisfied with a job well done they settle in %s." Final message with CONTINUE.
0x1c3d0.globals: area +0x19 (barbarian tokens, dword [0xE31CE + 69r] sar 24), terr byte +1 bits 3..5 (0xE1639 + 35t), 0xC768C/0xC77D8 names; [0xF6F60] BRPC mode, byte [0xEE168]; route buffer 0xF6E94 (4-byte entries, territory at +2), 0xF6EBC[160] visited (+0x9D..+0x9F set), [0xF6E8C] depth, [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0; message area int16 0xBB3FA..0xBB400 (saved/restored); [0xF097C] bit 0 sound, [0xF625C], [0xF6278] sample handle, int16 [0xF097E] volume; [0xCAB6C] -> "brpc.wav"; [0xBB3F4]
0x1c3d0.calls: sprintf, 0x79270 (5x), clock (6x), f78884, f788AC, 0x1C9FC, 0x1D234 (2x), 0x7A4F0 (unported: snapshot areas/territory state/nations into [0xEED74]/[0xEED7C]/[0xEED78]), memset, 0x1D858 (2x), 0x7AB24 (unported: restore snapshot), f7B504, AIL_set_sample_volume, AIL_start_sample, AIL_set_sample_loop_count, AIL_end_sample, f57CE8
0x1c3d0.callers: 0x217A0 at 0x218CE (the Barbarian Hordes calamity entry: "Crete can not be the Victim of Barbarian...")
0x1c3d0.waits_for_input: CONTINUE in f79270(-500) for the first and last messages (f7BA64/f78BA4 inside 0x79270); clock busy-waits of 1.5 s and 4 s scaled by [0xBB3F4]; no keyboard.
0x1c3d0.risks: Busy waits on clock (headless); the barbarians are nation 11 (records past the 9 nations); the route search can be long (the BRPC message admits 'several minutes'); search snapshots on the heap; AIL sample calls are port no-ops but the volume arithmetic writes nothing; the barbarian-count test is redone with the dword-sar idiom several times; the same-route grouping loop has no bound but stops at the first different entry.

0x1c9fc.purpose: Chooses where the Barbarians land for victim n. A local int16[6] gets the territories t < 157 whose terrflag byte +0 high nibble equals n (the nation's barbarian landing zones). Candidates: those where n has tokens (area +0x0E+n) or n's city stands (0xE2C1A bit 0, owner 0xE2C18 == n) into 0xF7CA0. None: a second rule (G: nearest own territories through adjacency, also with snapshots). One: taken. Several: each is tried under the snapshot buffers [0xEED74]/[0xEED7C]/[0xEED78] (0x7A4F0): visited cleared, 0x1D858 search, and the resulting route entries sorted by 0x1DEAC; the best (lowest +2, then +0 nibble) wins, ties kept in the list. Then the barbarians are placed: f57E28(t, 11, k) after 0xF547C/0xF548C cleared, and conflict/city handling 0x5B224/0x5B588 when n's city is there.
0x1c9fc.globals: terr byte +0 (0xE1638 + 35t) high nibble, +1; area +0x0E+n, +0x19; territory state 0xE2C18/0xE2C1A; heap snapshot pointers [0xEED74], [0xEED78], [0xEED7C]; 0xF547C/0xF548C (per-nation losses, cleared); route 0xF6E94, 0xF6EBC visited, 0xF6F59..0xF6F5B, [0xF6E8C]; [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0
0x1c9fc.risks: The local int16[6] landing list is filled without a bound: a nation with more than 6 marked territories would overwrite other locals (G: check terrflag.dat); copies through heap snapshot pointers (port handles); shared candidate list 0xF7C9C/0xF7CA0 reused by the callee.

0x1d234.purpose: One barbarian step for victim n (eax; edx = a second nation passed through, ebx = barbarians, ecx = &t). If t == -1 or the route's first entry has a destination: the route entries are bubble-sorted and the equal-best destinations listed (0xF7CA0). If the first entry's high nibble is 0 (no damage possible): the barbarians in t are reduced to the limit (f57CE8(t, 11, 0, excess)), "The Barbarian Hordes can no longer do any damage to %s units in adjacent territories." (adjective 0xC76C4[n]) with CONTINUE, and area +0x3B+n = 2 if n still has tokens there. Otherwise the barbarians leave t (f57CE8), a destination is drawn (game_rand * count >> 15 if several), f57E28 moves them in, "The Barbarians finally settle in %s." or "%s is invaded." (with conflict: 0xF547C/0xF548C cleared, 0x5B224/0x5B588 for cities, area +0x3B+n = 2, and if 0x1DFFC() != 0 the screen "BARBARIAN CONFLICT - UNITS REMOVED": background 3, f7876C, dialog 0xC5214 (FINISHED) appended, 0x5CDE8 table, removed). A human victim in a hot-seat game (+0x9A == 3, not PBEM) chooses the invaded city through 0x207B4(n, edx, 0x1A) (the Treachery 'REPLACE CITY' chooser, G); computers by game_rand.
0x1d234.globals: route 0xF6E94.. (+0 nibbles, +1, +2 territory, +3), [0xF6E90] (swap temp), [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0; area +0x19 (barbarians), +0x0E+n, +0x3B+n (written 2), terr +1 limit bits; territory state; 0xF547C/0xF548C; 0xC76C4 adjectives, 0xC77D8 territory names; flags 0xE1624 bit 0x80; int16 [0xBB400]; dialog 0xC5214

0x1d858.purpose: Recursive depth-limited search of the barbarians' next destination from territory t for victim n (eax n, edx t, ebx remaining depth, ecx route out, stack: visited buffer; ret 4). In BRPC mode ([0xF6F60]) every 250th call ([0xF6F5C]) prints "%s %s" = the BRPC message + a spinner character from 0xBB404 ('|', '/', '-', '\\') into 0xF5500 and shows it (f3A990, f3A9F4, f3CBBC). For each land (0xF8E7C) and coast (0xF90FC) neighbour not visited: the world state is copied into fresh heap blocks (0x2A51 bytes of areas 1..157 from 0xE31FD, 0x88D bytes of nations from 0xF1593, 0x1D7 bytes of territory state), the move simulated (f57E28, 0x5B224 / 0x5B588 when a city of n is hit), and an entry recorded in a local 4-byte table: +0 = (3 * cities lost 0xF548C[n] + tokens lost 0xF547C[n]) & 0x0F with the high nibble kept, +1 = 0x1DFFC() (barbarians left), +2 = depth [0xF6E8C], +3 = territory; recursion with depth + 1 while barbarians remain; the state copied back and the blocks freed. The local table is sorted (0x1DEAC) and the best entries copied to the route.
0x1d858.globals: [0xF6F60], [0xF6F5C] (call counter), 0xBB404 spinner pointers, 0xF5500; adjacency 0xF8E7C/0xF90FC; areas 0xE31FD.. (+0x0E+n, +0x19), territory state 0xE2C18, nations 0xF1593.. (copied/restored); 0xF547C/0xF548C; [0xF6E8C] depth

0x1d858.risks: Recursion with heap snapshots per level (depth up to 20: exponential work, as the game's own text warns); callee-pops one stack argument (ret 4); the snapshot sizes (157 areas) differ from the World State Stack's (160); a local route table on the stack; the result depends on the exact sort (0x1DEAC) and visiting order.

0x1deac.purpose: Sorts count (eax) 4-byte route entries at edx: first an exchange sort by the low nibble of byte +0 ascending, then a bubble pass from the end by byte +2 ascending (so the final order is by +2, ties by the +0 nibble). Swaps go through the global dword [0xF6E90].
0x1deac.risks: Two different sorting passes whose combined order must be kept exactly (stable bubble on the second key); unsigned byte compares (jbe).

0x1dffc.purpose: Returns the sum of int8 0xF547C[1..10] plus only the FIRST non-zero int8 of 0xF548C[1..10] (the second loop falls out after its first add).
0x1dffc.risks: BUG(1995) candidate (D: no jump back after the add in the second loop; G: meant to sum both tables); the 48-byte jump table at 0x1E070 in this range belongs to 0x1E0A0.

0x1e0a0.purpose: The calamity phase. int16 0xF409A[10] (Grain used against Famine) cleared. If no nation 1..9 holds a calamity (0x1E340): f79270(100, int16 [0xF06B0], -200, "", 0) and return. Otherwise: phase music 0x553C0, message area (0xA9, 0x154, 0x12C, 0x23); Zeus 0x1E388 unless bit 0x10 of [0xE1624]; 0x1E5B8 builds the list; player list 0xF06AE/0xF06B0 and f783B8(0xF596C, [0xF5940]); 0x7A4A0 ([0xCAC60] = [0xCAC64] = -1). For each calamity k < [0xF7808] whose victim (byte 0xF77E6 + 3k) is in play: int32 0xF4204[n] = (tokens on board +0x98 * 100 / [0xF4898] > 75), 0x7C960 (AI attitude recompute), [0xF783C] = card id, and jump table 0x1E070 by id - 0x13: Volcano/Earthquake 0x1E7A0, Treachery 0x20564, Famine 0x25A38, Superstition 0x23230, Civil War 0x29E34, Slave Revolt 0x235E4, Flood 0x2D4F0, Barbarian Hordes 0x217A0, Epidemic 0x2E59C, Civil Disorder 0x237A8, Iconoclasm & Heresy 0x23ACC, Piracy 0x241D8; after each (also skipped ones) 0x22B00 (elimination check, "%s has been eliminated from the game.") and 0x5E7B4 (an empty function).
0x1e0a0.globals: 0xF409A (cleared, 20 bytes), nation +0x13 (via 0x1E340), +0x98, +0x9A; [0xE1624] bit 0x10; message area int16 0xBB3FA..0xBB400 (written); [0xF5940]; calamity list 0xF77E4 + 3k {id, giver, victim}, [0xF7808]; writes 0xF4204[n], [0xF783C]; [0xF4898]
0x1e0a0.waits_for_input: Only inside the calamity handlers it calls.
0x1e0a0.risks: Jump table 0x1E070 (12 entries, stored inside 0x1DFFC's range); an id outside 0x13..0x1E falls through silently; 0x5E7B4 is an empty stub (G: a removed autosave or PBEM hook) that must still be called in order; the victim byte is read via dword sar 24.

0x1e340.purpose: Returns 1 if any nation 1..9 has a non-zero calamity count (byte +0x13), else 0.
0x1e340.risks: Does not test +0x9A (nations not in play have count 0).

0x1e388.purpose: For each nation n 1..9 in play holding more than two calamities (+0x13 > 2): discards count - 2 of them at random: idx = game_rand() * count >> 15, card = +0x14 + idx, discarded to its stack (0x771F8), the list +0x14.. shifted down, count - 1, the freed slot zeroed; names (0xC775C[id], e.g. "FAMINE") joined as "A", ", B", " and C" after "Zeus takes pity upon %s and discards ", then "."; shown by f79270(-500 CONTINUE, n, -200 home view, text, -298 = the Zeus animation/sound).
0x1e388.calls: sprintf (2 per name), game_rand (once per discard), 0x771F8 (unported: card to its discard stack), 0x79270
0x1e388.callers: 0x1E0A0 at 0x1E113 (skipped when bit 0x10 of [0xE1624] is set)
0x1e388.waits_for_input: CONTINUE in f79270 (-500), or the unattended timer.
0x1e388.risks: BUG(1995) candidate (D): unlike 0x1E69C it does not shift the parallel 'traded by' list +0x1C..+0x23, so after a Zeus discard the givers no longer line up with the remaining calamities (0x1E5B8 copies +0x1C+j as the giver; G: affects tradable calamities with a secondary victim). Two stack buffers (0x6C and 0x12C bytes) with strcat-like inline copies; one game_rand per discarded card.

0x1e5b8.purpose: Builds the calamity list in resolution order: [0xF7808] = 0; for id 0x13..0x1E, for nations 1..9 with +0x13 != 0, for slot j 0..7 with +0x14+j == id: record k = 0xF77E4 + 3k: +0 id, +1 giver (+0x1C+j), +2 nation n.
0x1e5b8.risks: No bound on the list (at most 9 x 8 entries; 0xF7808 sits 36 bytes after 0xF77E4, i.e. 12 records: more than 12 calamities in a round would overwrite the count, G); slot reads via dword [+0x11 + j] sar 24.

0x1e69c.purpose: Removes calamity k's card from its victim: int16 [0xF4094] = 1; finds slot j with +0x14+j == id, shifts both lists +0x14.. and +0x1C.. down, count +0x13 - 1, the last slot set to 0 / 0xFF, and the card discarded (0x771F8).
0x1e69c.risks: Uninitialised local: if the card is not found, the start index [ebp-0x14] is never set (D) and the shift starts from stack garbage; must not happen if the list is consistent (but see the Zeus misalignment above, which only touches +0x1C).

0x1e7a0.purpose: Calamity k (card 0x13) for victim n = byte 0xF77E6 + 3k. No cities (+0x51 == 0): "%s has no cities to be affected by volcanos or earthquakes." (CONTINUE, anim 1). Otherwise the three volcanoes of table int16 0xBDE18[3][2] (Mt. Vesuvius: 52 CAMPANIA, 127 NEAPOLIS; Mt. Etna: 76 MILAZZO, 78 SYRACUSE; Mt. Thera: 83 THERA, -1) are candidates if one of their territories holds a city of n (tested by hand on 0xE2CB4..0xE2D97). None: the earthquake 0x1F524(n). One: that volcano. Several: each scored (+6 per territory with a city whose owner is not 10, else the tokens of nations 1..9 there); a unique maximum wins; ties: a human victim in a hot-seat game (not PBEM, +0x9A == 3) chooses among the tied volcanoes (list 0xF7CA0) through 0x1EAEC(n, 0x13), a computer through 0x1EF28(n, scores). Then the eruption 0x1F25C(volcano, n) and 0x1E69C(k).
0x1e7a0.globals: 0xF77E4 + 3k; nation +0x51, +0x9A; territory state 0xE2C18/0xE2C1A (hard-coded addresses for territories 52, 127, 76, 78, 83); area +0x0E+1..9; volcano table 0xBDE18; [0xE1624] bit 0x80; [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0
0x1e7a0.waits_for_input: CONTINUE (f79270 -500) for the no-city message; the human choice in 0x1EAEC.
0x1e7a0.risks: Hard-coded territory addresses (must match the table); owner 10 excluded from the city score (G: a non-nation owner such as pirates); local score arrays on the stack passed to 0x1EF28; PBEM test.

0x1eaec.purpose: Lets a human victim n choose among the candidates in 0xF7CA0 (count [0xF7C9C]): type edx 0x13 volcano ("%s is about to undergo a Volcanic Eruption. Choose which volcano will erupt.", button "ERUPT HERE"), 0x12 earthquake ("... hit by an Earthquake. Choose which territory will be hit.", "STRIKE HERE"), 0x19 flood ("... Flooded. Choose which river will flood.", "FLOOD HERE"). Background 3, arrow sprites, panel f459E4(n), the message (f3A9F4), dialog 0xBE21C (arrows 0x39/0x3A, button 0x2A relabelled) appended to 0xF596C. Loop: the current candidate's name in a sunken box (volcano 0xBDE24, territory, or river 0xBEE0C), its territories highlighted (f3F624), the map centred (f3DA60), the animation hook 0x7A4C4(-600) after a change, then f78BA4(0xF596C, 1): a map click on a candidate (code >= 0) selects it, -9/-10 previous/next, -1 (the HERE button) returns 0xF7CA0[idx] after removing the dialog.
0x1eaec.globals: [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0; tables 0xBDE16/0xBDE18 (volcanoes), 0xBDE24 volcano names, 0xBEE08..0xBEE0E (rivers: territory lists and names), 0xC77D8 territory names; dialogs 0xBE21C, 0xF596C; byte [0xEE168]

0x1eaec.risks: A type other than the three leaves the message buffer uninitialised (stack); the candidate index is not clamped for map codes (they are list indices from f78BA4); relabels button 0x2A of 0xBE21C each call; f78BA4's map branch returns indices into 0xF7CA0.

0x1ef28.purpose: Computer choice among tied volcanoes for victim n (eax; edx -> int32 scores[3]). First a sum over v = 1..2 and territory j of the word pair at 0xBDE14 + 4v + 2j (volcanoes 0 and 1 only) of v when area record t (not t+1) holds tokens of another nation, or territory t-1 holds a city of another owner than n and 10; sum 1 -> 0, 2 -> 1. Otherwise compares the scores: all three equal -> 1 if n == 5 (Crete) (0 if n == 1), else 2; scores[0] == scores[1] -> sums tokens of other nations in hard-coded area records 34, 35, 54, 76 and returns 1 or 0; scores[0] == scores[2] -> 0 for n == 5, else 2; else 1 for n == 5, else 2.
0x1ef28.globals: 0xBDE14.. volcano table (read 2 bytes early), area records via 0xE31C4 + 69t and hard-coded 0xE3AEE/0xE3B33/0xE4052/0xE4640 (+3 bytes) groups, territory state 0xE2C18/0xE2C1A at t-1
0x1ef28.risks: Off-by-one indexing (D): area record t and territory state t-1 for a volcano territory t, unlike 0x1E7A0/0x1F25C; volcano 2 (Thera) never examined in the first loop; byte-sized locals and sums (int8 arithmetic). Keep literally; G: likely 1995 bugs.

0x1f25c.purpose: Volcano v (eax) erupts on victim n's turn (edx): message area h 0x14; 0xF547C/0xF548C cleared (14 bytes each). For each territory of the volcano: a city is destroyed (0xF548C[owner] + 1, 0x78F04(t, owner)); otherwise every nation 1..9's tokens there are lost (0xF547C[k] += tokens, stock +0x99 += tokens, board +0x98 -= tokens, area +0x0E+k = 0, f581C4(t, k)). Then background 3, f7876C, dialog 0xC5214 (FINISHED) appended, f3B05C(0xF596C), highlights cleared, panel f459E4(n), the volcano's territories highlighted in colour 15, map centred on the first, sprintf "%s eruption casualties" (0xBDE24[v]: Mt. Vesuvius, Mt. Etna, Mt. Thera), 0x7D5E8 (G: strupr), 0x5CDE8(2000) (the casualty table), dialog removed, int16 [0xBB400] = 0x23.
0x1f25c.globals: volcano table 0xBDE18, names 0xBDE24; territory state 0xE2C18/0xE2C1A; area +0x0E+k; nation +0x98, +0x99; 0xF547C/0xF548C (written); byte [0xEE168] = 3; int16 [0xBB400]; dialogs 0xC5214, 0xF596C
0x1f25c.calls: memset (2), 0x78F04 (unported: remove a city, G), f581C4, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, f7876C, f7853C, f3B05C, f3F670, f459E4, f3F624 (2), f3DA60, f3CBBC, sprintf, 0x7D5E8, 0x5CDE8 (unported casualty screen), f78664
0x1f25c.risks: Tokens are only removed where there is no city (the two branches are exclusive); the per-nation loss tables are global and read later by 0x5CDE8.

0x1f524.purpose: Earthquake for victim n (when no volcano touches its cities): [0xF783C] = 0x12. For each city i of n (+0x51 count, +0x52+i territory+1) a candidate block 0xF6F68 + 100i of 10-byte entries {int16 city, int16 neighbour, int16 score 6, int16 0xF52E0 attitude, int16 .bpm priority 0xEED84} for its land and coast neighbours (duplicates skipped; count int16 0xF72EC + 2i). Scores: +6 for a neighbouring city of another nation without Engineering (+0x2A), owner 10 gets -9000 values; the maximum and its ties are found. Maximum 0 (no neighbouring city to damage): only own cities qualify, listed in 0xF7CA0; a human in a hot-seat game chooses with 0x1EAEC(n, 0x12), a computer through 0x201B8; then 0x203B4. Unique maximum: 0x203B4 directly. Ties: the tied pairs into 0xF72FC + 8k; a human chooses through 0x1FDDC ("%s is about to be hit by an Earthquake ..."), a computer through 0x20068; int16 [0xF77E0] = the choice; 0x203B4 resolves ("Earthquake strikes %s! The city in %s w...", reduction of the neighbouring city).
0x1f524.globals: nation +0x51, +0x52.., +0x9A, others' +0x2A; adjacency 0xF8E7C/0xF90FC; territory state; 0xF52E0; 0xEED84; candidate blocks 0xF6F66..0xF72EB, counts 0xF72EC, tie list 0xF72FC.. (8-byte), [0xF7C9C]/0xF7CA0, int16 [0xF77DE]/[0xF77E0], [0xF783C]; [0xE1624] bit 0x80
0x1f524.risks: Fixed-size tables: 9 cities x 10 entries of 10 bytes (0xF6F68..0xF72EB); a 10th city or an 11th neighbour would run into the next block / the counts (G: check the maps); long index arithmetic (lea/shl chains) for the 100-byte stride; PBEM test.

0x1fddc.purpose: Earthquake target choice for a human victim n (eax). Called by the Earthquake resolver 0x1F524 only when not PBEM (byte [0xE1624] & 0x80 clear) and nation +0x9A == 3; returns an index into the candidate PAIR list 0xF7300 (stored by the caller in int16 [0xF77E0]). Screen: f3CD6C(3), [0xEE168]=3, fg_vbcopy whole screen [0xF52CC]->[0xF52C8]; in the back buffer the arrow sprites 0xF51AC at (0xC4,0x195) and 0xF51B4 at (0x1AF,0x195); f459E4(n); sprintf(local 0x74-byte buf, "%s is about to be hit by an Earthquake. Choose which territories will be hit.", name 0xC768C[n]) shown by f3A9F4; f7853C(0xBE608) appends dialog 0xBE608 (ids 0x39 left -> -9, 0x3A right -> -10, 0x2A 'STRIKE HERE' -> -1) to 0xF596C, f3B05C. Loop: frame f3C9D0(0xD2,0x195,0xDC,0x13,5), colour 5, sprintf "%s/%s" of the two territory names 0xC77D8[int16 rec+0] and 0xC77D8[int16 rec+2] of pair idx, centred f3A0B0(0xD2,0x199,0xDC); f3F670, both territories highlighted 15 (f3F624); if redraw: f3DA60(rec+0); f3CBBC; if redraw: f7A4C4 (calamity animation) and redraw=0. r = f78BA4(0xF596C,1): -100 loop; r>=0 -> idx = r, redraw; -9 idx-- if >0; -10 idx++ if < [0xF7C9C]-1; -1 ends. Then f78664(0xBE21C) and return idx.
0x1fddc.globals: reads [0xF52C8]/[0xF52CC] vb handles, 0xF7300 pair records (8 bytes: int16 +0 own city territory, +2 neighbouring city territory, +4/+6 scores written by 0x1F524), int32 [0xF7C9C] count, name tables 0xC768C (nations) and 0xC77D8 (territories); writes byte [0xEE168]=3, the dialog list 0xF596C (append/remove), border highlights 0xFFB60 via f3F624/f3F670; f78BA4 compares map clicks with 0xF7CA0[0..[0xF7C9C])
0x1fddc.calls: f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, fg_vbopen, f3AF8C, fg_vbclose, f459E4, sprintf 0x7DB3D, f3A9F4, fg_setcolor, f7853C, f3B05C, f3C9D0, f3A0B0, f3F670, f3F624, f3DA60, f3CBBC, 0x7A4C4 (unported: animation if 0xF097C&4), f78BA4, f78664
0x1fddc.waits_for_input: yes: f78BA4(0xF596C, 1) loop (buttons and map clicks) until STRIKE HERE (-1)
0x1fddc.risks: Map clicks: f78BA4 matches the clicked territory against 0xF7CA0, but the pair branch of 0x1F524 fills only 0xF7300, so a map click returns an index from a stale list (D for the code, G for the effect). Removes dialog 0xBE21C (Volcano's ERUPT HERE) instead of its own 0xBE608 (copy-paste; harmless only because both have 3 records starting with id 0x39). 0xF7300 records are read as dword sar 16 (int16). Animation path may draw game_rand inside 0x7A0A0 (indirect).

0x20068.purpose: AI ordering of the Earthquake candidate pairs (argument eax unused): two bubble sorts over the 8-byte records 0xF7300[0..[0xF7C9C]) through the temp 0xF77D8: first descending by int16 +6, then (stable) descending by int16 +4; so the order is +4 desc, ties +6 desc. Does nothing if count <= 1. The caller 0x1F524 then takes pair 0 ([0xF77E0]=0).
0x20068.globals: rw 0xF7300 records (8 bytes), reads int32 [0xF7C9C]; writes the 8-byte temp 0xF77D8
0x20068.risks: 16-bit signed compares (mov ax/dx, cmp ax, dx); record swaps by movsd through a global temp; keep the two-pass order exactly (stability matters for ties).

0x201b8.purpose: AI choice of the city of nation n (eax) hit by an Earthquake when 0x1F524 found no pairs (list 0xF7CA0 of n's city territories, count [0xF7C9C]). score[i] (int16[90] on the stack, cleared) = sum over the land neighbours (list [0xF8E7C+4t]: int16 count, int16 ids) of n's tokens there (int8 area +0x0E+n). dups = number of ordered pairs i!=j with equal scores. If dups == 0: the LAST i with score 0 wins; if none, the first i with the highest score (> 0). If dups != 0: the first i with the highest score (> 0), else index 0. Returns the territory 0xF7CA0[idx].
0x201b8.globals: reads 0xF7CA0/[0xF7C9C], land adjacency pointers 0xF8E7C, area records 0xE31B8+69(t+1) byte +0x0E+n
0x201b8.risks: Stack array short[90]; reads score[i] once as dword [ebp+2i-0xD2] sar 16 (same value); best kept as a dword loaded from a 16-bit mov (upper bits stale, compared as 16-bit). Empty list returns the stale 0xF7CA0[0]. Odd preference (zero-neighbour city only when all scores distinct) must be kept literally.

0x203b4.purpose: Applies the Earthquake: f203B4(t = own city, t2 = neighbouring city or -1, n = victim). Text: sprintf(buf 0x144-? local, "Earthquake strikes %s!  The city in %s was %s.", nation name, territory name t, "reduced" if n has Engineering (byte +0x2A, 0xF14F6+199n) else "eliminated"). If t2 != -1: appends " The neighboring %s city in %s was reduced." (adjective 0xC76C4[owner], name t2) or, owner 10, " The neighboring Pirate city in %s was eliminated.". Then t: Engineering -> f78FEC(t,n) (city replaced by tokens) else f78F04(t,n) (city removed). t2: owner 10 -> f78F04, else f78FEC (always reduced, the neighbour's Engineering is not tested); t2 highlighted 15. f79270(-500 (wait for CONTINUE), n, -t (highlight t without clearing), buf, anim 2).
0x203b4.globals: reads nation +0x2A (Engineering) and tstate owner 0xE2C18[3t]; writes through f78F04/f78FEC: tstate 0xE2C18..0xE2C1A, nation +0x51/+0x52.. city list, tokens; 0xFFB60
0x203b4.calls: sprintf 0x7DB3D, strcat (inline), 0x78FEC, 0x78F04 (unported city helpers), f3F624, 0x79270 (unported message helper)
0x203b4.waits_for_input: yes: through 0x79270(-500): CONTINUE (f78BA4 loop) unless unattended (f7BA64)
0x203b4.risks: ebx = -t: for t == 0 the helper sees 0 (>=0) and clears all highlights, dropping t2's highlight (G). Inline strcat into a stack buffer. anim argument 2 (not 1).

0x20564.purpose: Treachery resolution for calamity record i (eax) of 0xF77E4 (3-byte records {card, trader, victim}). v = victim (byte 0xF77E6+3i). If v has no cities (+0x51 == 0): "%s has no cities and cannot be affected by Treachery." via 0x79270(-500, v, -200 home view, text, 1), discard. Else it finds the Treachery card (id 0x14) among v's held calamities (+0x14..+0x1B, first match), its giver p = byte +0x1C+idx (-1 = drawn: p = v). Human p (not PBEM, +0x9A==3): t = f207B4(p, v, 0x14). Otherwise text "%s is a victim of Treachery by %s." or "%s is a victim of his own Treachery.", 0x79270(-500, v, -200, text, 1), t = f20C70(p, v) - 1. If p != v and p has < 9 cities: byte area(t)+0x3B+v = 1 (G: 'lost to another nation' mark). Then f3A990, f3CBBC, f20FC4(t, p, v), and 0x1E69C(i) discards the card.
0x20564.globals: reads 0xF77E4 records, nation +0x14..+0x1B (calamity cards), +0x1C..+0x23 (who gave each), +0x3D (number), +0x4E-derived +0x51 (cities), +0x9A; byte [0xE1624]&0x80 (PBEM); writes area +0x3B+v
0x20564.calls: f207B4, f20C70, f20FC4, 0x79270, f3A990, f3CBBC, 0x1E69C (unported: remove calamity i from the holder, discard via 0x771F8), sprintf
0x20564.waits_for_input: via 0x79270(-500) CONTINUE; via f207B4 for a human beneficiary

0x207b4.category: calamity UI: choose a territory (Treachery / Flood / Barbarians)
0x207b4.purpose: Human chooses a territory: f207B4(p chooser, v victim, kind). Kind 0x14 Treachery: p != v: "%s is a victim of Treachery by %s.  %s select the city to be %s." (v, p, p, "replaced" if p has < 9 cities else "eliminated") with button 0x58 of dialog 0xBDE30 relabelled "REPLACE CITY"/"ELIMINATE CITY"; p == v: "%s is a victim of his own Treachery. Select the city to be reduced." / "REDUCE CITY". Kind 0x1A Barbarians: "%s, choose territory for Barbarians to invade." / "INVADE HERE" (list prepared by the caller). Kind 0x19 Flood: "%s select your coastal city to be %s due to Flooding." (reduced/eliminated by v's Engineering +0x2A), REDUCE/ELIMINATE CITY. For kinds other than 0x1A the list 0xF7CA0 is rebuilt (157 entries -1, count 0): v's cities (owner byte 0xE2C18[3t]==v, city bit 0xE2C1A&1), for Flood also territory byte +0 bit 0x02 (G: coastal). Screen: background 3, arrows at (0xFB,0x195)/(0x178,0x195), f3A9F4(text), f7876C phase name, f3B05C; [0xF40F8] = v. Loop: frame (0x109,0x195,0x6E,0x13) with the territory name, f459E4(p), highlight, f3CBBC, on redraw f3DA60 + 0x7A4C4; r = f78BA4(0xF596C,1): r>=0 idx, -9/-10 arrows, -16 (button 0x58) returns 0xF7CA0[idx]. f78664(0xBDE30). Returns the territory.

0x20c70.purpose: AI choice of the victim's city taken by Treachery: f20C70(p beneficiary, v victim) returns territory+1. p == v: returns f213C0(v). If p has < 9 cities (replace): scanning v's city list +0x52+i from i = 9 down to 0: (1) first city with a land neighbour (0xF8E78[c] = list of territory c-1) where p has tokens (area +1+p != 0); (2) same with coastal adjacency 0xF90F8[c]; (3) first city whose territory byte +0 has bit 0x02; (4) the last city +0x51+count. If p has 9 cities (eliminate): if v's AST square (+0x5C) > p's: first city (ascending) whose territory byte +1 lacks bit 0x40, else last city (descending) with bit 0x40; fallback the last city.
0x20c70.globals: reads nation +0x3D, +0x4E/+0x51, +0x52..+0x5B city list, +0x5C AST square; adjacency 0xF8E7C/0xF90FC (indexed as 0xF8E78/0xF90F8 with t+1); area +1+n; territory bytes +0 (0x02) and +1 (0x40)
0x20c70.risks: Scans index 9 = byte +0x5B, one past the 9-entry list (0 by 0x45D30, so skipped). Signed byte compare of +0x5C. Return value is t+1 (callers subtract 1).

0x20fc4.purpose: Applies Treachery: f20FC4(t, p, v). Text "%s %s city in %s was " with "An"/"A" chosen by 0x789EC(v) (0 for Thrace 4, Crete 5, Babylon 8: 'A'), adjective 0xC76C4[v], territory name. f3F670, highlight t, f3DA60(t), f78A20(500). p != v and p has < 9 cities: 0x78F04(t,v), 0x78E74(t,p) (city changes owner), tstate +0 = p, +1 = int16 [0xF40FC] (round); if PBEM or p computer (+0x9A==2) appends "replaced by %s %s city." (a/an, p's adjective). p has 9 cities: appends "eliminated.", 0x78F04(t,v). p == v (own Treachery): inline city removal (bit cleared, owner 0, +1 = 0xFF, t+1 taken out of v's list), then k = min(pop limit (territory byte +1 bits 3..5) + Agriculture (+0x27), stock +0x99) tokens placed by f57E28(t,v,1) k times, stock -= k, board +0x98 += k, text "reduced.". Shown by 0x79270(2000, v, t, text, 1) for PBEM/computer p, else only f3DA60(t), f459E4(p), f3CBBC (a human chooser sees no message).
0x20fc4.globals: rw tstate 0xE2C18..0xE2C1A[3t], nation +0x51/+0x52.. lists, +0x98/+0x99, area tokens; reads +0x27, +0x9A, territory byte +1, int16 [0xF40FC], byte [0xE1624]
0x20fc4.waits_for_input: 0x79270(2000): a timed 2 s wait, no click
0x20fc4.risks: Own-Treachery reduction adds the Agriculture bonus unconditionally, while the shared helper 0x78FEC adds it only when no other nation's tokens are there (D difference, keep both). The inline list removal leaves its index uninitialised if t+1 is not in the list. Duplicate owner/round writes after 0x78E74.

0x213c0.category: calamity AI: which own city to reduce
0x213c0.purpose: AI's choice of one of nation n's (al, signed byte) own cities to reduce; returns territory+1. city[9] and lim[9] (stack) from the list +0x52+i and the pop limit (territory byte +1 bits 3..5); bubble sort descending by limit. If lim0 > lim1 and city0's territory has byte+1 bit 0x40: city0. Else if city0 lacks 0x40 and city1 exists with 0x40: compare pair (1,2) the same way (lim1 > lim2 -> city1). Only one city: city0. Otherwise for the two candidates sum n's tokens (byte area +0x0E+n) in land neighbours and 'coastal neighbours'; return the first candidate if its sum is larger (signed byte), else the second.
0x213c0.globals: reads nation +0x3D, +0x52..+0x5A, territory byte +1 (bits 3..5, 0x40), adjacency 0xF8E7C/0xF90FC, area tokens
0x213c0.risks: BUG(1995) D: the coastal-neighbour loop (0x216E3) tests j < list[j] instead of j < count and starts at j = 0, so it adds the tokens in territory 'count', then runs while j < the j-th id, reading past the list into following heap data: the coastal sum is garbage. Unusual frame (sub ebp,0x82, positive offsets); sums are int8 and wrap; argument is a signed byte.

0x217a0.purpose: Barbarian Hordes for calamity record i: v = victim; the director = the record's trader (byte 0xF77E5+3i) if not -1, else the nation k (1..9 in play, k != v) with the highest 5*(9 - cities +0x51) + tokens in stock +0x99 (int16 compare, strictly greater than the best, best starts 0). If v == 5 (Crete): "Crete can not be the Victim of Barbarian Hordes." via 0x79270(-500, 5, -200, text, 1); else 0x1C3D0(v, director). Then 0x1E69C(i).
0x217a0.risks: The director is uninitialised when no nation scores above 0. Loop counter compared as int16.

0x21914.purpose: Monotheism phase driver called from the game loop 0x54824 (case at 0x55096; the loop then sets phase byte 0x11). Message area 0xBB3FA..0xBB400 = (0xA9, 0x154, 0x12C, 0x23). int16 [0xF06AE] = count of nations in play and 0xF06B0[] their numbers; f783B8(0xF596C, [0xF5940]) labels the player buttons. For n 1..9 in play holding Monotheism (+0x3A): f227B0(n) builds the candidates; if any: flag=0, 0x553C0 (civil music), then human (+0x9A==3, not PBEM) f21A70(n) else f21E8C(n). If nobody had candidates: 0x79270(100, first nation in 0xF06B0, -200, "" (0xB1E9E), 0): home view, no text, 0.1 s.
0x21914.risks: The 'no conversion' redraw passes the empty string at 0xB1E9E (the NUL ending the Crete text). In PBEM a human is played by f21E8C.

0x21a70.purpose: Human Monotheism conversion for n: "%s, possession of Monotheism allows conversion of a neighboring territory."; dialog 0xBE9F4 (arrows -9/-10, 0x58 'CONVERT TERRITORY' -> -16, 0x2A 'FINISHED' -> -1) appended; background 3; arrows at (0xFB,0x181)/(0x178,0x181); f7876C; [0xF40F8] = n. Loop over the list 0xF7CA0 from f227B0: frame (0x109,0x181,0x6E,0x13) + name, highlight; on redraw f459E4(n), f3DA60(t); f3CBBC; r = f78BA4(0xF596C,1). CONVERT on t: a city -> area +0x3B+owner = 1, 0x78F04(t, owner), 0x78E74(t, n). No city -> for each nation k with tokens x there: area +0x3B+k = 1, f57CE8(t,k,0,x), k board -= x, stock += x; f57E28(t,n,x), n stock -= x, board += x. Then f459E4, f3D52C(0,0), f3CBBC, f78A20(1000) and the loop ends (one conversion). FINISHED ends without converting. f78664(0xBE9F4).

0x21e8c.purpose: AI Monotheism for n over the candidates 0xF7CA0 (from f227B0). Records of 12 bytes on the stack {t, nation, count} (about 170). If n has < 9 cities and board tokens/2 >= cities+1: candidate cities only; bubble sort descending by int8 priority 0xEED84[160n+t] (the opening-map table), then by int32 0xF52E0[10n+owner]; take the first: "%s converts %s by Montheism!" shown by 0x79270(-550 no wait), f78A20(300), area +0x3B+owner = 1, 0x78F04(t,owner), 0x78E74(t,n), then 0x79270(-500, n, t, text, 0) waits for CONTINUE. Otherwise (or no city candidates) the non-city candidates with their largest foreign token stack (nation, count); sorts by 0xEED84, 0xF52E0[10n+nation], count (all descending); converts every nation's tokens in the first territory into n's (as f21A70) with the same two messages.

0x21e8c.risks: If every candidate is a city but the city branch is not taken (9 cities or too few tokens), the unit branch has 0 records and reads the uninitialised stack record 0 as the territory (G: wild index). 2 KB stack array of 12-byte records swapped by movsd. Text slip 'Montheism'.

0x227b0.purpose: Builds the Monotheism candidate list for n: 0xF7CA0[157] = -1, [0xF7C9C] = 0; own[] (stack) = territories with n's city or n's tokens; adj[157] (stack, memset 0xFF) = 1 for every land neighbour of an own territory, then -1 for the own territories. For each t with adj[t] != -1: added if n can take a city (cities != 9) and t holds a city whose owner is not 10 (Pirates) and who has neither Monotheism (+0x3A) nor Theology (+0x3B); otherwise added if the foreign tokens there (nations 1..9 except n) total > 0 and <= n's stock (+0x99) and none of those nations has Monotheism or Theology.
0x227b0.globals: writes 0xF7CA0, [0xF7C9C]; reads tstate, area tokens +0x0E+n/+0x0F+k, adjacency 0xF8E7C, nation +0x3A, +0x3B, +0x51, +0x99
0x227b0.risks: Stack arrays int32[157] x2 (0x524 bytes); the memset fills bytes with 0xFF (dwords -1). Barbarian tokens (nation 11) are not counted.

0x22b00.purpose: After calamities and every phase: for n 1..9 in play with no tokens on the board (+0x98 == 0) and no cities: computer -> int8 [0xE1621] -1, "%s has been eliminated from the game." via 0x79270(-500, n, -200, text, 0). Human: not PBEM and humans [0xE1620] > 1 -> [0xE1620] -1, same message; PBEM -> system("del *.pl? >NUL") and f230B8(n); last human (not PBEM) -> f22DCC(n) (does not return). Then +0x9A = 0; PBEM: the 32-byte player record of n (0xF4104+32p) removed by shifting; [0xF40EC] players -1, == 1 -> f22F3C (winner, does not return). n's commodity cards go back with 0x771F8 one by one (+1..+0x12 to 0), its calamity cards (+0x14.., count +0x13) are discarded too; in the other nations' calamity lists a giver byte (+0x1C+j) equal to n becomes -1. Finally 0x7784C([0xF40EC]).
0x22b00.globals: rw nation +0x01..+0x12, +0x9A; reads +0x13/+0x14.., +0x98, +0x51; writes other nations' +0x1C..; int8 [0xE1620] humans, [0xE1621] computers, [0xF40EC] players, player records 0xF4104+32p (PBEM), discard piles 0xF07B4 (via 0x771F8)
