0x32214.waits_for_input: Human: f78BA4(0xF596C, 1) loop (map clicks pick a site) until FINISHED or no candidates left; computer: busy-wait on clock() (inline f78A20 arithmetic from the turn's start time) and 300 ms highlights
0x32214.risks: Jump table at 0x32200 (5 entries, codes -0xD..-9). 0x5B8-byte frame with two local 160-int arrays. The human paths inline the city creation instead of calling 0x78E74 and do not clear city-state bits 0x02.. that 0x333E8 clears (D). Inline busy wait on clock() with signed idiv by [0xBB3F4]. PBEM branches (0xE1622, [0xF408E]) to drop. The AI's Architecture build has no 3/6 cap (relies on the candidate list).

0x333e8.purpose: Builds a city for the computer: f333E8(t = eax, n = edx, k = ebx tokens used, arch = ecx). 0x78E74(t, n), f57CE8(t, n, 0, k), city state +2 &= ~2 then &= 3; message '%s builds a city in %s.' or '%s builds a city in %s using Architecture.' shown with 0x79270(ms, n, t, text, 0): -500 with toggle 0xF0980 & 1, else 2000 (attended) or 500/1500 (unattended, [0xF40BA]).
0x333e8.waits_for_input: 0x79270 with -500 when 'City Construction AI Pause' is on (G: waits for CONTINUE)
0x333e8.risks: Stock/board counters are adjusted by the caller, not here.

0x334f4.purpose: Candidate city sites of nation n (edx) into int32 0xF7CA0[] / need 0xF7F20[] (count [0xF7C9C]; the 157 entries of 0xF7CA0 first set to -1). Costs 6 / 12 (or 1 / 2 when int16 [0xF40B2] != 0). For t < 157 without a city: with arch (eax) and only one nation in the area: city site (terrflag +1 bit 0x40) with tokens >= 3 and tokens + treasury >= 6 -> need 6; non-site with tokens >= 6 and tokens + treasury >= 12 -> need 12. Otherwise: site with tokens >= cost6 -> need cost6; non-site with tokens >= cost12 -> need cost12.
0x334f4.globals: writes 0xF7CA0[157], 0xF7F20[], [0xF7C9C]; reads int16 [0xF40B2] (never written by any store in the listing, D), terrflag 0xE1639 + 35t bit 0x40, city state bit 0, area +0x01, +0x0E+n, nation +0x3E treasury
0x334f4.risks: The Architecture branch hard-codes 3/6/12 and ignores the [0xF40B2] costs. Leaf prologue.

0x337c8.purpose: How many new cities computer nation n (eax) should aim for. lim = [0xF4898]/2 (stock size; -2 for Crete); if AI-table roll int16 0x112A94[4][n-1] / 300 < (AI level ((word 0xE1624 >> 10) & 3) + 1) * 10: lim -= 5. If tokens on board < lim: returns 1 if tokens > 21 or any of n's token areas is shared, else 0. Else k = cities; while 2k <= tokens and tokens > 18: tokens -= 6, k++; e = min(k - cities, 3); if e == 3 and roll 0x112A94[5][n-1] / 300 < 25: e = 2; capped so cities + e <= 9.
0x337c8.globals: [0xF4898] stock size; AI random table int16 0x112A94[30][10] (rows 4 and 5, filled by f7BCD4); flags word 0xE1624 bits 10..11 (AI level); nation +0x51, +0x60, +0x61.., +0x98; area +0x01
0x337c8.risks: 16-bit bit-field extraction (shl eax,4; shr ax,14). Leaf prologue.

0x33964.category: AI (plan city sites and gather tokens)
0x33964.purpose: Plans up to goal (eax) cities for computer nation n (ebx), adding to *count (edx). rem = goal - *count; planned = n's areas with city-state bit 0x02 (planned) and >= 3 tokens. Candidates from 0x33ECC(&cnt, local list {t, priority}, n, mode ecx). For each candidate not in the failure cache 0xF8558[n-1][t] while done < rem and cities + done + planned < 9: s = 0x3433C(t, n) (tokens still needed; < 0 -> cache 99); else push the World State Stack (f7A940), save move-log count [0x1079B4] and [0x107D3C], nation +0x5D -= min(tokens at t, 0x78D08(t, n)), r = 0x3580C(s, t, n, 0, [s]); accept if r == 0, or r == 1 with [0xF488C+n] set, a city site and >= 6 tokens: for r == 1 a move-log record {0xC8, t} is appended at 0x107694 + 4*count, city state bit 0x02 and owner n set and int16 area +0x37 = tokens; 0x7AD24 (G: drop the saved state), done++; >= 12 tokens there sets byte [0x107ED8] = 1. Rejected: pop (f7AC60), counters restored, cache = r. Then, if short, [0x107EE0] == 0 and Architecture: budget = treasury - 2*(flags bit 5 ? 7 : 9) clamped to 0..3 (or the treasury when negative); for every t with 0 < cache <= budget: retried with need s - cache; success commits and counts.
0x33964.globals: int8 0xF8558[9][160] (failure cache, 0x63 = impossible); move log records 0x107694 + 4i ({from, to, count, code}) and count [0x1079B4], [0x107D3C]; flags [0x107ED8], [0x107EE0]; byte 0xF488C[n]; city state 0xE2C18 bits; int16 area +0x37; nation +0x3E, +0x51, +0x5D, +0x60/+0x61, +0x31
0x33964.risks: Trial moves under the World State Stack (push/pop around each try) and save/restore of the move-log counters: a literal port needs the stack and 0x7AD24/0x7AE14 semantics exact. The {0xC8, t} record leaves bytes +2/+3 stale (D). The Architecture retry loop marks nothing as planned and is not limited by rem or the budget count (D). 0x1A4-byte frame with a 0x198-byte list passed to 0x33ECC.

0x33ecc.purpose: Fills list (edx, 2-byte entries {t, priority}) and *cnt (eax) for nation n (ebx), mode (ecx). For t < 157 in play (0xEE16C) with no city and not planned: city site (terrflag +1 bit 0x40): if n has tokens there -> modes 0/2 add {t, 0xEFA04[n][t] + 10}, mode 1 only if terrflag +2 bit 0; if n has no tokens -> mode 0 adds when 0x49934(t, n, 0) != 0. Non-site, mode 0: population limit v = terrflag +1 bits 3..5; v == 1 (or Thrace and t == 1), or v == 2 for Illyria/Thrace, and n alone there -> {t, 9 - v}. Bubble sort descending by priority; each run of equal priority is reordered by 0x7701C(len, buf, n) (order from the AI random table column n-1, not game_rand).
0x33ecc.globals: 0xEE16C in-play flags; terrflag 0xE1638 + 35t (+1 bits, +2 bit 0); city state bits 0/1; AI table int8 0xEFA04[n][160]; areas +0x01, +0x01+n, +0x0E+n
0x33ecc.risks: Writes through the caller's stack buffer; 2-byte entries read as bytes, swapped as words. Thrace/Illyria special cases hard-coded by nation number. Ties ordered by 0x7701C, which always starts at row 0 of 0x112A94 (deterministic per call).

0x3433c.category: AI (tokens needed to build at t)
0x3433c.purpose: How many more tokens computer nation n (edx) needs at t (eax) to build a city, or < 0 if not feasible (-1 default, -999 for an unsafe non-site). archBudget = Architecture and [0x107EE0] == 0 ? clamp(treasury - 2*(flags bit 5 ? 7 : 9), 0..6) : 0. Areas with 2 nations are considered only if n is one of them. Threat x = 0x348B0(t, n, &enemy, &maxB). If another nation holds t: enemy = 0x7C7C4(t, n), e = its tokens. If x + e > 0 and the enemy is not the Barbarians (11): with relation int32 0xF52E0[enemy][n] < 0, rolls from the AI table (row t%4 + 9) against 0xF52E0[n][enemy] adjusted by AI level and whether the enemy is human decide whether to expect a fight; a computer enemy that will not fight -> no-threat path; when a fight is expected x is capped at 2 (+1 if the enemy has Metalworking and n not). City site: if x + e > 3*[0xF488C+n] + 4 - mb: -(x+e); else need = 6 + x + e - 1 + mb - tokens; with Architecture (budget > 2, flags clear) need is cut so tokens + need <= 7 and [0x107EDC] = 1. No-threat path: site -> (e ? e-1 : 0) + 6 - tokens; non-site with maxB == 0 and e == 0 -> 12 - archBudget - tokens (archBudget > 0 sets [0x107EE0] = 1); else -1.
0x3433c.globals: relations int32 0xF52E0[10][10]; AI table 0x112A94 rows 9..12; flags word 0xE1624 (AI level bits 10..11, bit 5); [0x107EDC], [0x107EE0] (Architecture reserved, written); byte 0xF488C[n]; nations +0x26 Metalworking, +0x31, +0x3E, +0x9A; areas +0x01, +0x01+n, +0x0E+n; terrflag +1 bit 0x40
0x3433c.risks: Local ebp-0x3c is a constant 0 subtracted in every formula (dead variable, keep or fold). Many signed divisions (200 / ((human?2:1)*(5-level)), rel / (5-level)). Out-parameters of 0x348B0 are only written when a maximum > 0 is found (enemy pre-set to 0 here).

0x348b0.purpose: Estimates how many enemy units can reach t (eax) against nation n (edx); returns the threat, *enemy (ebx) = the strongest nation, *maxB (ecx) = largest raw count. Push World State Stack + 0x7AA1C; restores predicted positions (0x3566C) of every nation moving after n (rank byte 0xF06C0[k] > rank[n]). Land reach list 0x48028(&c1, l1, t, n, [11]) and two-step list 0x4892C(t, &c2, l2, c1, [l1, n, 11]); per nation k after n: A[k], B[k] += movable tokens (area +0x24+k) on l1, and on l2 for nations with Roadbuilding (A gets count - 1). If max A < 5 and t is coastal: per later nation with ships, each ship (territory +0x45+2j, points +0x41+j) that 0x5843C says can reach t is expanded by 0x58888 into the list 0x108820 (16-byte records, count [0x109E00]); 0x374E0 scores each into +8 (with [0xF5908] cleared around it); sorted descending (bubble sort below 20 records, else qsort with comparator 0x3530C); best +8 into a local; C[k] = max, divided by (4 - AI level) when n is short of cities for its AST step (byte 0xBCCDC[n-1][ast][0] > cities). Threat = max A + C. Pop + 0x7AE14. If 0: repeated for human nations only (their +0x5D set to 99 inside the pushed state), result capped at 1 or 2 (Metalworking).
0x348b0.globals: rank bytes 0xF06C0[n]; areas +0x01, +0x24+k; nations +0x28, +0x40 ships, +0x41.., +0x45.., +0x51, +0x5C AST, +0x5D, +0x9A, +0x26; ship search list 0x108820 + 16i, count [0x109E00]; scratch 0xF8418, 0xF84B8, 0xF8194 (memset -1); [0xF5908] (saved/cleared/restored); AST table 0xBCCDC; terrflag +0 bit 2
0x348b0.risks: qsort with a code pointer (0x3530C: descending by signed byte +8); Watcom's qsort is not stable, so the order left in the global list 0x108820 depends on its exact algorithm (only record 0's +8 is used here, but the list stays in the data object). Simulation inside push/pop of the World State Stack; writes to human nations' +0x5D are undone only if the stack covers the nation records. 0x5FC-byte frame with large local lists passed to unported routines. [0xF5908] save/clear/restore around 0x374E0.

0x353c4.purpose: Predicts the positions of the nations that move after n (eax) and stores them in shadow tables. Push + 0x7AA1C. For k 1..9 with rank[k] > rank[n] and ships (+0x40) > 0: 0x460C0(k), 0x46158(k), +0x5D = 99, [0xF5908] cleared, 0x160EC(k), 0x7BD5C(k), failure cache 0xF8558[k-1] cleared, goal = 0x337C8(k), 0x33964(goal, &done, k, 2), 0x46BB8(k), [0xF5908] restored; nation k copied to 0xF09E8 + 199k; for every area r 1..160 and nation column j 0..8 the bytes +0x02+j, +0x0F+j, +0x1C+j, +0x2E+j, +0x25+j, +0x3C+j are copied to the shadow areas at 0xEB3F0 + 69r. Pop + 0x7AE14.
0x353c4.globals: shadow nations 0xF09E8 + 199k, shadow areas 0xEB3F0 + 69r (written); rank 0xF06C0; 0xF8558; [0xF5908]; nations +0x40, +0x5D
0x353c4.risks: The whole-column copy runs once per simulated nation (cumulative state). Only nations with ships are simulated (D; G whether intended). Deep simulation through many unported AI routines under one World State Stack level.

0x3566c.category: AI (restore predicted state of one nation)
0x3566c.purpose: Copies nation k's (eax) predicted record back from 0xF09E8 + 199k to 0xF14CC + 199k and its area columns (+0x02+j, +0x0F+j, +0x1C+j, +0x2E+j, +0x25+j, +0x3C+j with j = k-1) from the shadow areas 0xEB3F0 + 69r for r 1..160.
0x3566c.globals: reads shadow tables 0xF09E8, 0xEB3F0; writes nation k and area records
0x3566c.risks: Only valid inside a pushed World State Stack level (0x348B0 pops afterwards). Leaf prologue.

0x3580c.purpose: Moves computer nation n's (ebx) tokens toward t (edx) until need (eax) is met; returns the remaining need (0 = done). mode (ecx) 0/1/2, stack arg s (ret 4). Every move is 0x57CA4(from, to, n, k, [1]) plus a move-log record {from, to, 1, code} at 0x107694 + 4*[0x1079B4]. Stages: (mode 0) areas from 0x48028(.., 0x15) sorted by 0x48D44 whose tokens 0x7C838 releases, code 0x20; adjacent areas (0x48028(.., 9)) keeping Agriculture + population limit, code 0 / 0x1B; two sweeps (10 tries) one token per visit keeping 0x49790(0x495C0(..)) or 1 (codes 1/0x1C, 2/0x1D, +0x5D -= 1); a guarded sweep inside push + 0x7AA1C/0x7A688/0x7A7E8 that re-runs with the areas reachable by later nations (0x460C0, 0x46158, 0x648C8 simulations) marked used, accepting when 0x49A1C(a, n, 1, t) or the 0xF3580 bit allows (codes 3/0x1E); with Roadbuilding two-step moves via 0x79128's middle area (records +2 = 0x33 and 0x4C, codes 0x12/0x1F); by sea 0x36918(n, t, &need, mode) when t is coastal and int16 [0xBB3F0] != 0; a second guarded sweep. Ends: mode 0: need = -1 if >= 12 tokens and byte [0x107ED8] == 1; need 0 -> record {0xC8, t, 0}, city state bit 0x02 + owner n, int16 area +0x37 = tokens, return 0; else clears those and returns need. mode 1: 0 when done or when (start - need) >= 2 (or >= 1 with tokens there) and no city, a weak lone enemy; else need. mode 2: done or (start - need) >= s -> record {0xC9, ?, 0, owner of t}, 0.
0x3580c.globals: move log 0x107694 + 4i and [0x1079B4]; [0x107ED8]; city state 0xE2C18; int16 area +0x37; areas +0x01, +0x0E+n, +0x24+n; terrflag (+1 bits 3..5, +0 bit 2, +2 bit 2); nation +0x27, +0x28, +0x5D; int16 0xF3580[9][157]; [0xF5908]; int16 [0xBB3F0]; rank 0xF06C0
0x3580c.risks: BUG(1995) candidate (D): the mode-2 success record writes its +0 (0xC9) and +2 (0) bytes at 0x107694 + count and 0x107696 + count (unscaled index, 0x36887/0x368D8) instead of 4*count, corrupting earlier records, while +1 goes to the right record. Very long function with seven near-identical sweep blocks (copy-paste; keep each code byte). Two nested World State Stack levels with seven unported stack helpers. 0x628-byte frame with 160- and 0x280-byte local lists passed to callees. ecx (mode == 1) reused as the constant 1 in address arithmetic.

0x36918.purpose: f36918(n = eax, t = edx target land territory, int *need = ebx, int8 code = cl). The computer carries up to *need tokens of nation n by ship to t. Pushes the World State Stack (f7A940). For each ship k < n.+0x40 while the remaining count > 0: s = word +0x45+2k - 1, c = 0xC803C[s] (alias table, identity except 157..159 -> 57/13/135); if 0x5843C(s, t, n, mp +0x41+k) == 1 (t reachable, Astronomy +0x2B picks one of two route routines), it pushes the Move List Stack (0x7AA1C) and either (A) direct: if *need+1 <= area[c].+0x24+n (movable), land matrix 0xF95FC[157c+t] == 0, s != t and !(0xE2C1A[3c] & 2): count = min(*need, 5), 0x57CA4(c, t, n, 1, count) (tokens c -> t), 0x58888(c, t, n, mp) and route 0 copied; or (B) multi-stop: 0x58888 fills the route table 0x108820 (16-byte records, count [0x109E00]: +0..5 stops (0xFF pad), +6 moves left, +7 tokens, +8..13 per-stop pickups), memsets 0xF8418, 0xF84B8 (uint8[160]) and 0xF8194 (int32[160]) to -1, sets each route's +7 = min(f374E0(j, t, n, remaining, 0), remaining), sorts by +7 descending (bubble when count < 20, else qsort(0x108820, n, 16, cmp 0x35368)), counts the routes tied with route 0 on +6 (idx), picks r = AI table int16 [0x112B0A+2n] (= 0x112A94 row 6 col n-1) / (30000 / min(idx, 30000)), clamped to idx-1, and if route r carries tokens moves them stop by stop (0x57CA4 per stop, ship mp - 1 per hop) into a local 28-byte plan record (+4 ship, +8 stops, +0xC tokens, +0x10 pickups[6], +0x16 stops[6]; up to 4 on the stack). Each ship pops the Move List Stack (0x7AE14). Then pops the World State (f7AC60: all trial moves undone), sorts the plans by stop count (bubble) and replays them for real: per stop q tokens 0x57CA4(alias(stop), t, n, 1, q), *need -= q, and appends 6-byte ship-move records to 0x1079B8 + 6*[0x107D3C] {+0 from, +1 to, +2 count, +3 ship, +4 type 3 embark / 0x0A sail / 5 disembark, +5 0xC1938[code]}; the ship's word +0x45+2k = t+1 and +0x41+k decremented per hop.
0x36918.globals: reads nation n +0x40, +0x41+k, +0x45+2k (writes +0x41+k, +0x45+2k), area 0xE31B8+69(c+1) +0x24+n, 0xF95FC land matrix, 0xE2C1A[3c] bit 1, 0xC803C, AI table 0x112A94 (int16 at 0x112B0A+2n), 0xC1938[5] (byte codes 4,0x23,0x28,0x0F,0x27); writes 0xF8418/0xF84B8/0xF8194 caches (-1), route table 0x108820 (+7), ship move list 0x1079B8 / [0x107D3C]; *need (caller's int)
0x36918.calls: f7A940 (push world), f7AC60 (pop world), 0x7AA1C / 0x7AE14 (Move List Stack push / pop-restore, unported), 0x5843C (ship can reach), 0x58888 (enumerate ship routes into 0x108820), f374E0, 0x57CA4 (f57CE8 + f57E28: k tokens a -> b), qsort (0x8C331, comparator 0x35368 unported), memset 0x7D5D0
0x36918.callers: 0x3580C at 0x36350 (code = its mode byte, an index 0..4), f37CF8 at 0x384DF (code 0x0F), f396FC at 0x39B4E (code 0x27)
0x36918.risks: (1) qsort for 20+ routes: tie order of Watcom's qsort must be reproduced bit-exactly (comparator 0x35368). (2) The tie scan 'while route[0].+6 == route[idx].+6 idx++' has no bound: it relies on 0x58888's 0xFF fill after the last route. (3) BUG(1995) G: f37CF8 and f396FC pass the code values 0x0F / 0x27 where 0x3580C passes an index 0..4 into the 5-byte table 0xC1938, so their records get byte +5 = [0xC1947] / [0xC195F] (0 in practice: f3A748's buffer neighbour and the button label offset table). Keep the out-of-table read. (4) Random choice uses the pre-rolled table, entry 0x112B0A+2n (row 6 col n-1 via an odd base). (5) Plan records live in a 4x28-byte stack array, exactly the 4 ships. (6) Two stacks pushed/popped in strict pairs; the replay depends on the trial-state undo.

0x374e0.purpose: f374E0(j = eax route index, t = edx target, n = ebx, max = ecx, a = stack, ret 4): how many tokens (<= 5, <= max) route j (0x108820 + 16j) can collect along its stops for nation n, trying the pickups on the live state and undoing them. Copies nation record n (199 bytes) to the stack, zeroes route bytes +8..+13. Pass 1 over stops m (c = 0xC803C[stop]): if cache 0xF84B8[c] == -1 and movable(c) > 0 and n.+0x5D > 0 and c != t and !(0xE2C1A[3c] & 2) and land matrix[c][t] == 0: keep = 0xF8418[c] (computed once as f49790(f495C0(c, n, a, &e), c, n, e): defenders to leave); if movable < tokens take one at a time while movable > keep, else (keep 0 and !(F3580[n-1][c] & 0x80) -> keep 1) while tokens > keep: each take saves area record c once (69 bytes in a local 73-byte slot, index in 0xF8194[c]), taken++, n.+0x5D--, route +8+m ++, f57CE8(c, n, 1, 1), [0xF8414] = 1. If the cache is already set and c not yet visited in this call, it adds 0xF84B8[c] pickups. Pass 2 (taken < max, < 5, first stop uncached): stops whose tokens == 1 give one more if f49A1C(c, n, 1, -1) != 0 or (n.+0x5D > 0 and F3580 bit 0x80). Pass 3 stores the per-stop pickups into the cache 0xF84B8. Restores the nation record and every saved area record (0xF8194 entries back to -1). Returns min(taken, 5).
0x374e0.globals: reads/writes route table 0x108820 (+8..+13), caches 0xF8418[160], 0xF84B8[160] (int8), 0xF8194 int32[160], flag [0xF8414] = 1; reads area +0x0E+n, +0x24+n, nation +0x5D (budget, restored), 0xE2C1A[3c] bit 1, land matrix 0xF95FC, F3580 (int16 [9][157] at 0xF3580 + 314(n-1) + 2c, bit 0x80), 0xC803C
0x374e0.calls: f495C0, f49790, f49A1C, f57CE8 (one token off), memset 0x7D5D0
0x374e0.risks: Trial-and-undo by raw memcpy of 69-byte area records into a 6-slot stack buffer and of the 199-byte nation record; the caches are global and persist between routes of one f36918 call (filled only by the caller's memset). f49790/f49A1C use the AI table rolls. f49A1C recursion guard [0x1082DC]. Sign: bytes read as dword sar 24.

0x37cf8.category: AI movement: attacks on enemy territories
0x37cf8.purpose: f37CF8(n = eax, x = edx; x = 1 first round, 0 second). Mode = 1; with L = AI level (word [0xE1624] bits 10..11: 0 Stronger, 1 Normal, 2 Weaker): if table[7][n-1]/300 < 80 + 10(2-L) mode = 2, and if then table[8][n-1]/300 < 3L mode = 3 (aggressiveness). For every territory t < 157 in play where f387C8(t, n, mode, &need, &victim, x) says attack: add {t, need, victim} (12-byte records, stack) if n has tokens in a land neighbour, else if 0x4D29C(t, n) (reachable by sea, G). If any: skip all when table[9][n-1]/300 < 2L+1. Bubble-sort by attitude F52E0[n][victim] descending, then non-city-sites before city sites (terr +1 bit 0x40). A dead loop marks a 9-byte local for contested territories over their limit (never read). For each candidate until one succeeds: if F52E0[n][victim] < 0 it attacks only if table[9 + t%4][n-1]/300 > (F52E0 - 200) / ((5-L) * (victim human ? 2 : 1)). Attack: push World State and Move List; f48028(&c, list, t, n, 9) and f48D44(&c, list, n, t, 1) give the source territories; pass A: from each source while tokens > population limit (f78D08) one token at a time 0x57CA4(s, t, n, 1, 1), move record type 0x0C; pass B (10 sweeps): tokens > 1, type 0x0D; pass C (10 sweeps, [0xF5908] cleared around it): if f49A1C(s, n, 1, t) or (t not a city site and the other nation in t lacks Architecture +0x31), type 0x0E; then ships f36918(n, t, &need, 0x0F) if terr[t]+0 bit 2 and word [0xBB3F0]. If need still > 0: pop both stacks (undone). Else: append record {0xC9, victim (0x7C7C4(t, n)), 0, -} to the move list, drop both stack levels (0x7AD24, 0x7AD7C: keep the moves), stop.
0x37cf8.globals: reads AI table 0x112A94 rows 7, 8, 9, 9..12; word [0xE1624] AI level; F52E0 int32 attitude [n][m] at 0xF52E0 + 40n + 4m; nation +0x60/+0x61 list, +0x31 (Architecture) of the other nation, +0x9A of the victim; area +0x0E+n, +0x24+n; terr 0xE1638+35t (+0 bit 2, +1 bit 0x40, +1 bits 3..5); word [0xBB3F0]; [0xF5908] saved/cleared/restored; writes move list 0x107694 + 4*[0x1079B4] {from, to, count, type}
0x37cf8.calls: f387C8, 0x4D29C, f48028, f48D44, f78D08 (0x78D08 population limit, unported), 0x57CA4, f49A1C, 0x7C7C4 (other nation present), f36918, f7A940, f7AC60, 0x7AA1C, 0x7AE14, 0x7AD24 (drop world level), 0x7AD7C (drop move-list level), memset
0x37cf8.risks: Uses the pre-rolled AI table, not game_rand: rows 7..12 by nation. Big stack arrays (0x1214 bytes). Attack threshold for negative attitude: (F52E0-200)/x is negative, so the roll nearly always passes (kept literal). Dead 9-byte local marking. Stack push/pop pairing must be exact; 'success' path drops levels instead of popping.

0x387c8.purpose: f387C8(t = eax, n = edx, mode = ebx, int *need = ecx, int *victim = [ebp+8], x = [ebp+0xC], ret 8): 1 if n should attack territory t, with *need tokens. Requires exactly one nation in t (area +1 == 1); 0 if t has tstate bit 1 and n is the one there. victim o = 0x7C760(t) (first nation present), *victim = o; bonus = 1 if n has Metalworking (+0x26) and o not. 0 if o.+0x51 (cities) >= 9. City site (terr +1 bit 0x40) without a city (tstate bit 0) and x == 0: if o has Architecture (+0x31): o's tokens > limit (f78D08(t, o)), turn order 0xF06C0[n] > 0xF06C0[o], tokens 3..mode+3+bonus and tokens + o.treasury (+0x3E) >= 6 -> *need = tokens - 1 - bonus. Else: tokens >= 6 and n moves later, or (tokens >= 4, F52E0[n][o] > 300, era of n's AST square (0xBCCE0 + 85(n-1) + 5*n.+0x5C) is 3 or 4, tokens >= f78D08(t, o), n moves earlier, 0x337C8(o) > 0); then tokens > mode+6+bonus -> 0; if tokens >= 4, >= limit and n moves earlier: f48028(&c, l, t, o, 0xC), r = 0x4D110(t, &c, l, o, 1), *need = max(min(r + tokens, 9) - 6, 0) + 2 - bonus; else *need = tokens - 4 - bonus. Otherwise (no site / city / x != 0): o with Architecture: x == 0, tokens >= 6, cities < 9, n moves later, tokens <= mode+6+bonus, tokens + treasury >= 12 -> tokens - 4 - bonus; without: tokens >= 12, n moves later, tokens <= mode+12+bonus -> tokens - 10 - bonus. Returns 1 with *need set, else 0.
0x387c8.globals: reads area 0xE31B8+69(t+1) +1, +1+n, +0x0E+o; tstate 0xE2C1A[3t] bits 0/1; terr +1 bit 0x40; nation +0x26, +0x31, +0x3E, +0x51, +0x5C; 0xF06C0[n] turn order; F52E0[n][o]; AST era table 0xBCCE0 (uint8 [9][17] in 5-byte records)
0x387c8.calls: 0x7C760 (first nation present), f78D08 (population limit), 0x337C8 (G: n's city/token situation), f48028, 0x4D110
0x387c8.risks: Long nested condition chain with several near-duplicate branches (city vs no city, Architecture or not); 'tokens' always means the victim's tokens +0x0E+o read signed; returns via ret 8 (two stack args).

0x38e54.purpose: f38E54(n). Only if n.+0x98 (tokens on board) >= 14 and f39C08(n) < 9 (city sites held). For each territory s in n's list (+0x61.., count +0x60) without tstate bit 1: f48028(&c, list, s, n, 0x14) (city sites with AI flags where n moves earlier than the other nation) and f48D44(&c, list, n, s, 0x201) (sort by opening-map score, cities dropped). For each target u: k = 0x4CC5C(u, n, 3) (G: tokens needed there); if k > 0 and movable(s) >= k: counter++, and if table[11 + counter%9][n-1]/300 < 95 - 15L: 0x57CA4(s, u, n, 1, k), area[u] +0x3B+n = 0, move record {s, u, k, type 0x19}.
0x38e54.globals: reads nation +0x98, +0x60/+0x61; area +0x24+n; tstate bit 1; AI table rows 11..19; AI level; writes area +0x3B+n (G: target flag) and the move list 0x107694/[0x1079B4]
0x38e54.risks: Local counter starts at 0 per call (rows depend on candidate order). Pre-rolled table only.

0x39068.category: AI movement: attack on an enemy city
0x39068.purpose: f39068(n = eax, x = edx). Returns at once if n.+0x51 >= 9. Score = 10 if n has Engineering (+0x2A), + 15 - 5L, + 5 * (n.+0x98 - 6x - [0xF4898]/2) when positive, + 20 if treasury +0x3E is 15..17. Finds the most disliked nation (max F52E0[n][m], m 1..9 in play, start -9999) and adds 10*(max/50 + 1) if max > 0. thresh = score * min(max AST square of all nations, 12) / 13; no attack if table[24][n-1]/300 >= thresh. Candidates: every city t < 157 (tstate bit 0) of owner o != n, o != 10, empty or held only by o, F52E0[n][o] >= -200 and f49934(t, n, 0): record {t, value = F52E0[n][o] * 0xC2864[era(o)][L] / 100, a, b}, with a = 0x4CEE4(t, n, &b) for the most disliked nation, else a = b = 99999. Bubble-sorts by a ascending then by value descending. Tries each until one succeeds: a = 0x4CEE4 if still 99999; if a != -1: push World State and Move List; 0x3580C(a, t, n, 2, b) (G: the attack plan; 0 = success): non-zero -> pop both; zero -> drop both levels, area[t].+0x3B = n's tokens there (+0x0E+n), done.
0x39068.globals: reads nation +0x2A, +0x3E, +0x51, +0x5C, +0x98, +0x9A; [0xF4898] token supply; F52E0; AST era table 0xBCCE0; 0xC2864 int32[6][3] (era x AI level: 0/0/0, 50/25/10, 100/80/60, 150/110/90, 200/150/100, 225/175/125); AI table row 24; tstate +0 owner / bit 0; area +1, +1+o; writes area +0x3B
0x39068.risks: 16-byte candidate records on the stack (0xA60 frame, up to ~160). Two bubble sorts whose combined order must be kept exactly (stable). 0x3580C returns 0 on success (inverted sense). Owner 10 excluded by number (G: pirates/barbarians).

0x396fc.category: AI movement: relieve besieged own cities
0x396fc.purpose: f396FC(n). For each own city (area index +0x52+k, k < n.+0x51) with any nation's tokens in it (area +1 != 0): o = 0x7C7C4(t, n) (the intruder). Base = 8 if n has Engineering (+0x2A) and o not, 6 if o has it and n not, else 7; bonus = 1 if n has Metalworking and o not; need = o's tokens - base + 2 - bonus. Push World State and Move List; sources f48028(&c, l, t, n, 9), f48D44(.., 1); pass A: tokens above the population limit, one at a time, type 0x24; pass B (10 sweeps): tokens > 1, type 0x25; pass C (10 sweeps, [0xF5908] cleared): f49A1C(s, n, 1, t) or (t not a city site and o lacks Architecture), type 0x26; then ships f36918(n, t, &need, 0x27) if terr[t]+0 bit 2 and word [0xBB3F0]. need != 0: pop both (undone); else drop both levels (kept).
0x396fc.globals: reads nation +0x2A, +0x26, +0x31 (of o), +0x51, +0x52..; area +1, +0x0E+o, +0x0E+n, +0x24+n; terr bits; word [0xBB3F0]; [0xF5908] saved and restored; writes the move list 0x107694
0x396fc.risks: Engineering/Metalworking rule encoded as nested tests on bytes read through dword sar 24 at +0x27/+0x26 offsets (n's +0x2A read via [rec+0x27] sar 24). Passes code 0x27 to f36918 (see the 0xC1938 out-of-table read there).

0x39c08.category: AI helper: count held city sites
0x39c08.purpose: f39C08(n): counts territories t < 157 in play that n has or will keep: a city of n (tstate bit 0 and owner == n); otherwise only city sites (terr +1 bit 0x40): F3580[n-1][t] bit 0x04, or n alone there; contested sites (count > 1, n has tokens): counted if the other nation 0x7C7C4(t, n) is > 9; else a silent conflict is simulated (area record saved, nations saved 0x7A778, byte [0xBB3F8] = 0, 0x5B588(t+1), [0xBB3F8] = 1, nations restored 0x7A7B0), the area record is restored, and then 'n alone' is tested on the restored record.
0x39c08.globals: reads 0xEE16C in-play, tstate 0xE2C18+3t, terr +1 bit 0x40, F3580 bit 0x04, area +1/+1+n/+0x0E+n; writes byte [0xBB3F8] (0 then 1), area record (restored), nation records 1..11 via 0x116FFC (restored)
0x39c08.calls: 0x7C7C4, 0x7A778 / 0x7A7B0 (save/restore nations 0xF1593..+0x88D to 0x116FFC), 0x5B588 (conflict resolution of one area)
0x39c08.risks: BUG(1995) G: the test after the simulated conflict reads the area record AFTER it was copied back, so a contested site is never counted; the 0x5B588 call is wasted work. Keep it literal (0x5B588 may change other state, e.g. tstate or [0xBB3F8]-dependent output).

0x39f50.purpose: f39F50(i): release Fastgraph/Fonts font i: 0x8E0F8(int16 [0xF8B2C + 2i]) (read as dword [2i + 0xF8B2A] sar 16), or 0x8E0F8(-1) for i == -1 (all fonts).
0x39f50.calls: 0x8E0F8 (Fastgraph/Fonts release, not yet in LIBRARY_CALLS.md; G: fgf_release(handle), -1 = all)
0x39f50.callers: main 0x118D3 (after the game loop 0x54824 returns: fonts released, fg_mousefin, video mode restored by 0x80A33([0xF6058])), 0x5055C (PBEM host file) and 0x50D08 (PBEM trade session), both right before f44CAC
0x39f50.risks: Library call not catalogued; port can no-op it or free its font tables.

0x3b728.purpose: Redraw the button with id edx of dialog eax in its current state, in the back buffer: first record whose int16 id (rec+0x0E, 16-bit compare) matches; fg_vbopen([0xF52C8]); f3B4E0(dlg + 2 + 20i); fg_vbclose. No match: message box "Button not found" (0xB3C14) through f3A7B0.
0x3b728.callers: 0x7399C at 0x73A5B (trade offers: REJECT ALL OFFERS / ACCEPT PREFERRED ORDER)
0x3b728.risks: none (pattern of the ported by-id helpers)

0x3b914.purpose: Set the pressed byte rec+0x12 of button id (edx) of dialog (eax) to (int8)bl, no redraw. "Button not found" (0xB3C47) if none.

0x3ba30.purpose: Return the width (int16 rec+0x04) of button id edx in dialog eax: mov ax, word [dlg+20i+6]. Not found: "Button not found" (0xB3C69) and 0.
0x3ba30.risks: eax's upper half on success is the upper half of the record address (only ax loaded); the only caller reads the low word (movsx), so return int16.

0x3babc.purpose: Return the height (int16 rec+0x06) of button id edx in dialog eax (ax only). Not found: "Button not found" (0xB3C7A) and 0.
0x3babc.risks: as 0x3BA30: upper 16 bits of eax are address bits; caller uses the word

0x3bbd8.purpose: Return the x (int16 rec+0x00) of button id edx in dialog eax (ax only). Not found: "Button not found" (0xB3C9C) and 0.
0x3bbd8.risks: upper half of eax is garbage; return int16

0x3bcf4.purpose: Return the y (int16 rec+0x02) of button id edx in dialog eax (ax only). Not found: "Button not found" (0xB3CBE) and 0.
0x3bcf4.risks: upper half of eax is garbage; return int16

0x3bea0.purpose: Set the label colour byte rec+0x0C of button id edx (dialog eax) to (int8)bl, no redraw (0 = default colours with shadow). "Button not found" (0xB3CF1).

0x3c1f4.purpose: Set the no-flash byte rec+0x0D of button id edx (dialog eax) to (int8)bl (1 = f3C5D4 does not flash it on a click). "Button not found" (0xB3D57).

0x3c48c.purpose: Enable button id edx of dialog eax (rec+0x10 = 1) and redraw it with f3B4E0 on the ACTIVE surface (no fg_vbopen, unlike f3C314). "Button not found" (0xB3D9B).
0x3c48c.risks: draws on whatever surface is active (caller decides)

0x3c530.purpose: Disable button id edx of dialog eax (rec+0x10 = 0) and redraw it on the active surface (f3B4E0). "Button not found" (0xB3DAC).

0x3c6a0.purpose: Enable every button of dialog eax: fg_vbopen([0xF52C8]); for i < int16 [dlg]: rec+0x10 = 1, f3B4E0(rec); fg_vbclose. No state saved (unlike f3C7A0/f3C8C4).

0x3c720.purpose: Disable every button of dialog eax in the back buffer: fg_vbopen([0xF52C8]); rec+0x10 = 0 and f3B4E0 for each; fg_vbclose. No state saved.

0x3cdf0.purpose: Black-out before a fade: fg_getdacs(0, 256, 0xF8B40) saves the current palette, memset(0xF5D58, 0, 768), fg_setdacs(0, 256, 0xF5D58).
0x3cdf0.globals: writes 0xF8B40[768] (target palette, used by f3CFE4), 0xF5D58[768] (fade work buffer)
0x3cdf0.risks: start-up path, not M6; port: palette.c equivalents

0x3ce44.purpose: Set a GIF's palette at once: if name (eax) is non-empty fg_gifpal(name, 0xF8B40); copy 0xF8B40 to 0xF5D58 (768 bytes); fg_setdacs(0, 256, 0xF5D58). With an empty name it re-applies the saved palette.

0x3f6e4.purpose: Clear every token box colour: memset(0xFFC00, 0, 0xA0) (the companion of f3F698).

0x3f758.purpose: Clear every ship box colour: memset(0xFFCA0, 0, 0xA0) (companion of f3F70C). functions.txt's 1084 bytes include the dispatcher 0x3FB94's jump table at 0x3F780..0x3FB93 (data); the code is 40 bytes.
0x3f758.risks: the size in functions.txt is wrong (table data counted)

0x448ec.purpose: f448EC(x, y, w, h): recolour a rectangle on the active surface through the table 0xC2720: for each column x..x+w-1, each row y..y+h-1: fg_setcolor(0xC2720[fg_getpixel(x, y)]), fg_point(x, y) (G: darkens/tints a card area, like f44800 with 0xC2620).
0x448ec.risks: pixel-by-pixel read-modify-write; order irrelevant for the result

0x460c0.purpose: f460C0(n): for area records r = 1..160: movable +0x24+n = tokens +0x0E+n if the marker +1+n is non-zero, else 0 (start of a movement: every token may move).
0x460c0.risks: the 0 store uses ah (the zero marker byte), i.e. 0

0x46158.purpose: f46158(n): every ship k < +0x40 of nation n gets movement points +0x41+k = 4, or 5 with Clothmaking (+0x25 != 0).

0x461bc.category: AI movement: top level for one computer nation
0x461bc.purpose: f461BC(n): the computer's whole movement plan for nation n, also run (as a planning step) by ship maintenance and ship construction. If [0xF5908] (G: AI moves shown) start = clock(). Pushes n on 0x107D48[[0x107D44]++]. 0x7BD5C(n), f46998(n), 0x160EC(n), clears token/ship boxes (f3F6E4, f3F758), ship points (f46158); for areas 1..160: +0x3B = 0, int16 +0x37 = 0, movable +0x24+n = tokens or 0, and f3F698(r-1, 15) where n is present. reserve = 99. Push World State; c = 0x337C8(n); push, 0x5AAA4(0) + 0x5C238(0) (silent conflict and city checks), reserve = 0 if cities + c >= (tokens-1)/2 else tokens - 2 - 2(cities + c); pop. Loop: clear the move lists ([0x1079B4], [0x107D3C]), counters [0x108194], [0x107EE0], [0x107EDC], byte [0x107ED8], [0x108164+4n], memset(0xF8558 + 160(n-1), 0, 160), 0x7AF28(); n.+0x5D = reserve; f37CF8(n, 1); f396FC(n); if +0x5D == 0: f4A088(n, 0, 1), 0x4C074(n), recompute reserve (floor 0), flag. +0x5D = reserve; most disliked nation m (max F52E0[n][m], start -99999; any negative -> flag); era = 0xBCCE0[n-1][m.+0x5C] (+1 and attitude +200 if m is human); if (any negative and attitude * 0xC2864[era][L] / 100 > 500) or f468EC(): [0x107D40] = 0, f39068(n, cnt), 0x33964(c, &cnt, n, 0); else 0x33964 first, then f39068. 0x4C9B8(n, 1); f38E54(n); f46BB8(n) (if it changed nothing, n has no ships, no cities and >= 12 tokens: 0x33964(c+1, ..)); 0x4C9B8(n, 2); f37CF8(n, 0); 0x4C6E4(n); f478D8; if cnt < 4 f47A44; if !f46B34(n): L != 2 -> 0x643C8(n) else 0x648C8(n, 0). Push both stacks; f4A088(n,0,0), f49E04(n), v = f46A4C(n); if v > 0 a second variant is tried (0x7A688, 0x7A7E8, 0x7AF28, 0x7AFB8, f49E04, f4A088) and kept unless its excess is not smaller (then 0x7A700, 0x7A85C restore); drop both levels. 0x4C074(n); [0xC28AC] = 0, f46BB8(n), [0xC28AC] = 1; [0xC28B0] = 3, f4A088(n, 0, 1), [0xC28B0] = 4; 0x648C8(n, 0); 0x4BBDC(n); 0x65CB0(n) if [0xF5908]. If cnt > 0: k = own territories with tstate bit 1; 0x5AAA4(0), 0x5C238(0); if tokens - 2 < 2*cities + 2k: c-- and loop again. Finally pop the World State (all trial moves undone; the plan stays in the move lists), wait until clock() >= start + (500/[0xBB3F4])/10 if shown, 0x4D518(n, [0xF5908] != 0) ('%s is moving.': G executes the move lists), [0x107D44]--.
0x461bc.globals: [0xF5908], [0xBB3F4], 0x107D44/0x107D48 nation stack, area +0x37, +0x3B, +0x24+n; token boxes 0xFFC00; nation +0x5D, +0x51, +0x98, +0x60/+0x61, +0x40, +0x9A, +0x5C; F52E0; 0xBCCE0; 0xC2864 (6 era rows incl. 225/175/125); AI level; [0x107D40], [0x108194], [0x107EDC], [0x107EE0], [0x107ED8], [0x108164+4n], 0xF8558[9][160]; [0xC28AC] byte, [0xC28B0] recursion depth of f4A2E0; move lists 0x107694/0x1079B8
0x461bc.callers: 0x55574 (movement phase) at 0x55A5F; ship maintenance 0x60BD8 ('Maintenance housekeeping for %s'), 0x61254 (2, '%s considers ship maintenance.'); 0x61940 DoShipContruction; 0x62840 (2, '%s considers building ships.'); 0x680DC ('%s cannot fully populate...')
0x461bc.waits_for_input: no click wait; a clock() busy wait (500 ms / [0xBB3F4]) before executing when [0xF5908] is set. The callee 0x5C238 has a click-wait path (0x79270 -> f78BA4) only for a non-zero argument; this function passes 0
0x461bc.risks: The central AI routine: ~40 callees, most unported; three nested stack disciplines (World State push/pop/drop, Move List push/pop/drop, nation stack 0x107D44). Port order matters: everything is trial-and-undo on the live globals. Timing uses clock(); keep it outside comparisons. Era index can reach 5 (human bump): 0xC2864 has that row, in-table. Random decisions come from the pre-rolled table 0x112A94 (saved in the save file) and the free-running counter [0x108198] (see f474A0).

0x468ec.purpose: f468EC(): 1 only when the AI level is 0 (Stronger) and some nation m 1..9 is human (+0x9A == 3) with stock +0x99 < 4, cities +0x51 > 0, ships +0x40 < 4, and [0xF5470] >= 3 (G: round number); else 0.

0x46998.purpose: f46998(n): for t = 0..157 (inclusive): if F3580[n-1][t] high byte bit 0x08 and the opening-map score 0xEED84[n][t] > 0 and area[t+1] +0x3B+n != 1: set area +0x3B+n = 1 (G: an expansion target).
0x46998.globals: F3580 (+1 byte, bit 0x08); 0xEED84 + 160n (.BPM scores); writes area +0x3B+n
0x46998.risks: Loop bound jg 0x9D: t = 157 included, reading F3580 entry 157 (one past the 157-entry row, i.e. the next nation's entry 0) and area record 158 (G off-by-one; keep).

0x46a4c.purpose: f46A4C(n): sum over n's territories (list +0x61, count +0x60) without tstate bit 1 where n is alone (area +1 == 1) of max(0, tokens - f78D08(s, n)): the tokens that population limits would cost.

0x46b34.category: AI helper: room for all tokens
0x46b34.purpose: f46B34(n): 1 if the population limits (f78D08) of all n's territories add up to at least the token supply [0xF4898] (47 or 55), else 0.

0x46bb8.purpose: f46BB8(n): unless f46B34(n): memset(0x10819C, 0, 160), memset([0xC2860] = 0x107EE4, 0, 4), memset(0x10823C, 0, 160); repeat until a pass changes nothing: f47BA0(&c, list, n, 3, 1) (n's territories with movable tokens, by score); on the first pass, if byte [0xC28AC], f471CC(&c, list, n) reorders; for each s: if f46CBC(s, n) == 1 -> changed, [0x108164 + 4n] = 1. Then 0x160EC(n).
0x46bb8.globals: 0x10819C[160], 0x10823C[160] (per-territory done flags), int32 array 0x107EE4 via the pointer [0xC2860], byte [0xC28AC], [0x108164+4n]
0x46bb8.risks: BUG(1995) G: memset(*(int**)0xC2860, 0, 4) clears only entry 0 of the int32[160] array 0x107EE4 (sizeof pointer slip); f471CC then reads flags left by other users of 0x107EE4 (ship routines 0x58630.., 0x4AC50, 0x64Bxx, 0x65Dxx). Keep literal: the order of the AI's moves depends on it.

0x46cbc.category: AI movement: spread from one territory
0x46cbc.purpose: f46CBC(s, n): move n's spare tokens from s into neighbours. List: f48028(&c, l, s, n, 0) (empty land), f4876C(.., 0x16) (lone weak neighbours worth attacking), f48D44(&c, l, n, s, [0xF488C+n] ? 0x436 : 0x36). avail = movable(s); keep = f49790(f495C0(s, n, 0, &e), s, n, e) if the .BPM flag 0xF0044[n][s] bit 0 or f49A1C(s, n, keep, -1) == 0; if nothing has moved from s yet avail -= keep; ret = 1 if avail > 0. With [0xC28AC]: f474A0(s, n, &avail, &ret, c, l). For each target u while avail > 0: if score 0xEED84[n][u] > score[n][s], 0x10823C[s] == 0 and F3580[n-1][u] bit 0x80 or 0x04: avail -= f49C88(s, n), 0x10823C[s] = 1. Else k: .BPM flag bit 1 and n alone... (area +1 == 1): k = min(avail, limit bits of u); bit 1 and contested: the first nation there o (0x7C760) has ot tokens; k = ot if ot <= avail, else avail when avail + ot <= limit, else 0; else if F3580 hi bit 0x04 or lo 0x20/0x40: k = f495C0 threat (1 if none) capped by the limit, then by avail; else k = 1. Moves k: 0x57CA4(s, u, n, 1, k), area[u] +0x3B+n = 0 if alone, record type 5, avail -= k. If avail changed and [0xC28B4]: 0x10819C[s] = 1. Returns ret.
0x46cbc.globals: area +1, +0x0E, +0x24+n, +0x3B+n; terr +1 limit bits; 0xEED84 / 0xF0044 .BPM tables; F3580; 0xF488C[n]; 0x10823C, 0x10819C; [0xC28AC], [0xC28B4]; move list
0x46cbc.risks: Mutual recursion with f49A1C (guard byte [0x1082DC]); the 'k' branch chain is long and uses signed byte compares; limit read as (b << 2) >> 5 of terr +1.

0x471cc.purpose: f471CC(int *cnt, int list[], n): for each s in list: neighbours (f48028 0, f4876C 0x16, f48D44 0x36), spare as in f46CBC; if spare > 0, F3580[n-1][s] bit 0x20 and 0x10819C[s] <= 0: if some neighbour has .BPM flag bit 1, or there is at most one neighbour, set int32 [0x107EE4 + 4s] = 1. Then rebuilds the list: entries with that flag first, then the rest (stable).
0x471cc.risks: Reads flags never fully cleared (see f46BB8). Stack copy of the list (0x2CC bytes).

0x474a0.purpose: f474A0(s, n, int *avail, int *ret, cnt, list) (ret 8): if *avail > 0, F3580[n-1][s] bit 0x20 and 0x10819C[s] <= 0 (and a neighbour has .BPM flag bit 1, or <= 1 neighbour): f48028(&c, l, s, n, 0xB) (all), f48D44(.., 1). Pass 1 over targets u with F3580 hi bit 0x02, pass 2 with lo bit 0x10: k = 0x4CC5C(u, n, 3); if k > 0, movable(s) >= k, f78D08(u, n) >= k and 0x7C838(u, n, k, &x) == 0: r = table[10 + c%10][n-1] with c = [0x108198]++; if r/300 < 90 - 20L: 0x57CA4(s, u, n, 1, k), area[u] +0x3B+n = 0, record type 0x13 (pass 1) / 0x15 (pass 2), *avail -= k, 0x10819C[s] = 1 if [0xC28B4], *ret = 1.
0x474a0.globals: [0x108198] global counter (incremented per roll), AI table rows 10..19, F3580, 0x10819C, [0xC28B4], area, move list
0x474a0.calls: f48028, f48D44, 0x4CC5C, f78D08, 0x7C838 (G: simulated conflict result), 0x57CA4
0x474a0.risks: [0x108198] is written only here, never reset (not by f461BC, not by new game or restore) and not in the save file: the AI's rolls after a restore depend on how often this ran earlier in the session. A port must keep it as a process-lifetime static (0 at start) to match DOSBox-X runs from a fresh start.

0x478d8.purpose: f478D8(c, int *cnt, n, int *flag): if cities + *cnt < 9: spare = tokens(+0x98) - 4 - 2(cities + *cnt) measured after a silent 0x5AAA4(0)/0x5C238(0) under a World State push/pop; if spare <= 0 and !*flag: *flag = 1, f4A088(n, 0, 1), 0x4C074(n), measure again. If spare > 0: n.+0x5D = spare; f47BA0(&c2, l, n, 0x0E, 0) (sites ready for a city); if any: old = *cnt; 0x33964(c+1, cnt, n, 1); if *cnt changed [0x108194] = 1.
0x478d8.risks: state pushed/popped around the measurement only

0x47a44.purpose: f47A44(c, int *cnt, n, int *flag): if tokens(+0x98) >= 20, f46A4C(n) != 0 and cities + *cnt < 9: same spare measure as f478D8 (with f4A088(n, 0, 1) and 0x4C074 once if needed); if spare > 0: +0x5D = spare, 0x33964(c + [0x108194] + 1, cnt, n, 0).

0x47ba0.purpose: f47BA0(int *cnt, int list[], n, mode, flags) (ret 4): t < 157 in play. mode 3: no tstate bit 1, movable > 0, and n alone or (contested and .BPM flag bit 1). mode 0x0E: no tstate bit 1, city site (+1 bit 0x40), terr +2 bit 0x01, n alone, tokens > limit + Agriculture (+0x27). Other modes: empty list. flags bit 0x01: bubble sort by score 0xEED84[n][t] ascending; bit 0x08: those over their limit (f78D08) first. functions.txt's 1160 bytes include f48028's jump table (0x47FC4..0x48027, 25 dwords).
0x47ba0.risks: jb/jbe dispatch on mode; size includes data

0x48028.purpose: f48028(int *cnt, int list[], t, n, filter) (ret 4): the land neighbours u of t (list [0xF8E7C + 4t]: int16 count, ids) that pass filter 0..0x18 (25-entry jump table at 0x47FC4): 0 empty and no city; 1 n alone with tokens < limit (+1 Agriculture); 2 movable > 0; 7 n alone, not a city site; 8 n alone; 9 n alone, no tstate bit 1; 0x0A movable > 0, no tstate bit 1; 0x0B all; 0x0C n has tokens; 0x0F n alone, terr +0 bit 2 clear, no tstate bit 1; 0x11 n alone with tokens > limit; 0x12 F3580 bit 0x80; 0x13 empty, no city, 0xF4234[n-1][u] set; 0x14 city site with F3580 lo 0x10 or hi 0x02 and n moves later than the nation there (0xF06C0); 0x15 contested with n present; 0x17 as 0x14 plus empty of n and one nation there; 0x18 one other nation there, n absent; 3..6, 0x0D, 0x0E, 0x10, 0x16 none.
0x48028.globals: adjacency [0xF8E7C+4t]; area +1, +1+n, +0x0E+n, +0x24+n; tstate; terr +0/+1; F3580; 0xF4234 uint8[9][160]; 0xF06C0
0x48028.risks: Jump table (25 entries, unsigned ja for > 0x18): translate as a switch with the same empty cases; registers pre-computed before the jump (69(u+1), 35u, 314(n-1)+2u) are shared by the cases.

0x4876c.purpose: f4876C(int *cnt, int list[], t, n, filter) (ret 4), filter 0x16 only: appends neighbours u held by one other nation o (0x7C7C4) with .BPM flag bit 1 for n, when F52E0[n][o] >= 0, or when table[25 + u%3][n-1]/300 > F52E0[o][n] - 200/((5-L)(1 + o human)).
0x4876c.globals: F52E0 (both directions), nation +0x9A, AI table rows 25..27, AI level, 0xF0044
0x4876c.risks: Other filter values append nothing. Note the asymmetric attitude indices.

0x4892c.purpose: f4892C(start, int *cnt, out[], count, list[], n, filter) (ret 0xC): if [0xF09E4] != 0: for each t in list that is n's city, empty land, or held by n alone: its land neighbours u that are not start, not in list and not yet in out, passing filter 0 (empty, no city), 9 (n alone, no tstate bit 1), 0x0B (all), 0x14 or 0x17 (as f48028), are appended to out.
0x4892c.globals: [0xF09E4] (set in the game loop, 0x55118/0x557C9), tstate, area, terr, F3580, 0xF06C0, adjacency
0x4892c.risks: filter dispatched by a jb/jbe chain; three stack arguments

0x48d44.category: AI helper: sort/filter a territory list
0x48d44.purpose: f48D44(int *cnt, int list[], n, t, flags) (ret 4), list of territories, steps in this order: 0x80 city sites first; always bubble sort by score 0xEED84[n][u] descending (signed bytes); 0x10 keep the entries with score >= 0; 0x20 drop entries with 0xF4234[n-1][u] set (byte [0x108190] = 1 when one is dropped); 0x200 drop cities; 0x02 score <= score(t) first, then higher; 0x04 .BPM flag bit 1 first; 0x400 keep score > 105; 0x100 cities first; 0x40 F3580 hi bit 0x04 first. Each partition is stable through a stack copy.
0x48d44.risks: Order of steps and the bubble sort's tie behaviour must be kept; score(t) computed even where unused.

0x495c0.category: AI helper: threat next to a territory
0x495c0.purpose: f495C0(t, n, mode, int *enemy): the largest stack of another nation in a land neighbour of t; *enemy = that nation. Contested neighbours are first resolved silently (area record and nation records saved, [0xBB3F8] = 0, 0x5B588(u+1), [0xBB3F8] = 1, nations restored; the area record restored after the scan). mode 1 counts only nations that move after n (0xF06C0).
0x495c0.globals: adjacency, area +1, +0x0E+m, 0xF06C0, byte [0xBB3F8], nation records via 0x116FFC
0x495c0.risks: Raw 69-byte save/restore of the area record around a full conflict resolution (0x5B588) must not leak other side effects (tstate, cities).

0x49790.purpose: f49790(r, t, n, enemy): 0 if r == 0. thr = max(limit bits(t) - 1, 1) + 1 + Metalworking(n) - Metalworking(enemy); 1 if r < thr; else if table[12 + t%8][n-1]/300 < 95 - 10L: min(tokens of n in t, limit bits(t)); else 1.
0x49790.globals: terr +1 limit bits, nation +0x26, area +0x0E+n, AI table rows 12..19, AI level

0x49934.category: AI helper: can n reach t
0x49934.purpose: f49934(t, n, mode): 1 if n has tokens in a land neighbour of t; else, unless mode == 1, 1 if any ship k of n can reach t (0x5843C(word +0x45+2k - 1, t, n, +0x41+k) == 1); else 0.

0x49a1c.category: AI helper: would t be refilled
0x49a1c.purpose: f49A1C(t, n, k, exclude): guarded by byte [0x1082DC] (returns 0 if set). Pushes the World State, saves [0x1079B4]; sources f48028(&c, l, t, n, 0x0A) minus exclude; empties t of n (count +1 = 0, marker, tokens = 0), forces .BPM flag bit 1 at t; [0xC28B4] = 0; the first neighbour for which f46CBC(u, n) == 1 puts tokens back into t -> found; [0xC28B4] = 1. Result: found and (table[12 + t%8][n-1]/300 < 90 - 15L ? tokens(t) >= k : tokens(t) != 0). Restores the flag byte and [0x1079B4], pops the World State, clears the guard.
0x49a1c.globals: [0x1082DC] guard, [0x1079B4], [0xC28B4], 0xF0044[n][t], area record t, AI table rows 12..19
0x49a1c.risks: Recursion f46CBC <-> f49A1C via the guard; move records written during the trial stay in memory past the restored count.

0x49c88.purpose: f49C88(s, n): surplus = tokens(s) - f78D08(s, n); one token each to neighbours u with F3580 lo bit 0x20, without hi bit 0x02 and exactly one below their limit bits (limit - tokens == 1): 0x57CA4(s, u, n, 1, 1), record type 0x17. Returns the number moved.

0x49e04.category: AI movement: fill marked empty lands
0x49e04.purpose: f49E04(n): copies n's territory list to 0xF7CA0 (count [0xF7C9C]); for each s held by n alone with movable > 0 and no tstate bit 1: spare = tokens - min(f78D08(s, n), 2); targets f48028(.., 0x13) + f48D44(.., 0x12); then the first target u gets one token at a time (type 0x18) while spare > 0, movable > 0 and tokens(u) < its limit.
0x49e04.globals: 0xF7C9C/0xF7CA0 (shared scratch, also the nation choice's list), area, move list
0x49e04.risks: BUG(1995) G: the target u and its limit are read once (list[0]); the loop index advances but u is never reloaded, so only the first target is filled. Keep literal.

0x4a088.purpose: f4A088(n, a, b): for each territory s of n (local copy of the list), unless it has tstate bit 1 and owner n: if n alone with tokens > limit, excess = tokens - limit (when movable > 0); if contested with n's tokens == 0x7C838(s, n, 0, &x) (G: n would lose them all), excess = that value when movable equals it. Then f4A2E0(excess, s, n, 0, &s, 1, a, b).
0x4a088.risks: [ebp-0x38] read only after the branch that sets it (checked); the visited list is a one-entry stack variable

0x4a2e0.purpose: f4A2E0(k, s, n, depth, visited[], nvisited, mode, conquer) (ret 0x10): returns tokens moved out of s. Stops at depth >= [0xC28B0] (3 or 4). Pass 1: neighbours not visited, empty (no city) or n alone below its limit, sorted f48D44(.., 6); fills them one token at a time (type depth+7: 7..10). If mode != 1 and s is coastal (terr +0 bit 2): moved += 0x4AC50(s, &k, n, depth) (ship). If conquer == 1: neighbours held by one weaker nation o (0x7C760) below the limit: tokens up to the limit, type 0x22. Then onward relay: neighbours of n with spare movable tokens (alone: movable > tokens - limit; contested: movable > 0) sorted, with the visited list appended: x = min(movable(u), k, limit(u)), r = f4A2E0(x, u, n, depth+1, newlist, ..), room from r, the area int16 +0x37 or the limit; tokens s -> u one at a time.
0x4a2e0.globals: [0xC28B0], area +1, +0x0E, +0x24, +0x37, terr limit bits and +0 bit 2, tstate bit 0, adjacency, move list
0x4a2e0.risks: Recursion depth bounded by [0xC28B0] (globals set around calls by f461BC); visited list grows on each level's stack (0x2D4 frame); record type encodes depth (depth+7 after the increment).

0x4ac50.purpose: AI: ship nation n's tokens from territory t to free land elsewhere. Args eax = t, edx = n, ebx = int *cnt (tokens to ship), ecx = mode; returns the number of tokens landed ([ebp-0x50]). If mode > 1, f57E28(t, n, *cnt) first puts the tokens on t, and at the end f57CE8(t, n, 0, original *cnt) takes them off again. For each ship k < nation +0x40, while *cnt > 0: s = int16 +0x45+2k - 1. Only ships that f5843C(s, t, n, points +0x41+k) says can reach t take part. steps = route length s->t from f58888 (0 if s == t), avail = points - steps. If avail > 0, f5861C(t, n, avail) marks the reachable territories in 0x107EE4[]; t itself is unmarked. Candidates u are reachable territories whose canonical c = 0xC803C[u] is either held by n alone with tokens < f78D08(c, n) (population limit), or empty with no city (0xE2C18+3c+2 bit 0 clear) and byte 0xF488C[n] == 0. They are bubble-sorted, highest first, by the signed priority byte 0xEED84[160n + u]. Leg 1 (s->t): the best route of f58888(s, t, n, steps), or the first route in mode 1, or [t, 0xFF] if s == t. Routes are scored by the tokens they can pick up (f78D08 surplus; in mode 1 a f7C838 conflict trial when other nations are present). The best route is copied to the local [ebp-0x90]. Leg 2 (t->candidate): for each candidate, f58888(t, cand, n, avail); score = free room along the path (a local 160-byte visited map); the best route goes to [ebp-0x88]. The amount is capped at *cnt. Execution: on leg 1 at each territory, load up to 5 tokens: f57CE8(c, n, 1, m), ship +0x4D+k += m, AI move record type 3; then for each hop a move record type 10, points +0x41+k - 1, int16 +0x45+2k = next + 1. On leg 2 at each territory, unload min(room, aboard): f57E28, +0x4D+k -= m, record type 4, *cnt -= m, landed += m; then the hops as type 10. Move records are 6 bytes at 0x1079B8 + 6i (count [0x107D3C]): +0 from, +1 to, +2 count, +3 ship k, +4 type (3 load, 4 unload, 10 ship move), +5 = 0x2B on leg 1, 0x2C on leg 2.
0x4ac50.globals: reads area records 0xE31B8+69(c+1): +1 count, +1+n marker, +0x0E+n tokens, +0x24+n movable; 0xE2C18+3c (+2 bits 0/1); 0xC803C canonical; nation 0xF14CC+199n: +0x40 ships, +0x41+k points, +0x45+2k location, +0x4D+k aboard (all written); 0xEED84[n][160] priority; 0xF488C[n]; 0x108820[] route records and count [0x109E00] (via f58888); 0x107EE4[160] reach (via f5861C); writes the ship move list 0x1079B8.. / [0x107D3C]
0x4ac50.calls: f57E28, f57CE8, f5843C*, f58888* x4, f5861C*, f78D08* (population limit of t for n: bits 3..5 of territory byte 0xE1639+35t, +1 with Agriculture (+0x27) when n is alone there) x12, f7C838* (conflict trial: copies area record t+1, adds k tokens of n, runs 0x5B588 silently with [0xBB3F8] = 0 between the World/Move stack helpers 0x7A778/0x7A7B0, restores the record, returns int8 0xF547C[n] = n's losses; *out = nations left) x2, f7D5D0* (memset) x1
0x4ac50.risks: 1216 instructions of nested loops over the shared global route buffer 0x108820 (16-byte records, at most 350; f58888 does not bound-check [0x109E00]). The candidate list is a 160-int stack array. The move list 0x1079B8 holds 150 six-byte records with no bound check on [0x107D3C]. The signed byte compare in the bubble sort (jle on al/bl) must be kept. Byte vs dword reads of the same fields: ship location is read as int16 sar 16 here but written as a word = next+1 (the high byte is cleared). G: in mode > 1, the original *cnt is removed from t at exit even when some of those tokens were loaded onto ships; that could leave counts negative, so translate it literally. Several 6-byte rep movs copies of the route records. Watcom keeps the registers across calls, which the C translation does not need to model.

0x4bbdc.purpose: AI nation n (eax) pulls its tokens out of contested territories it would lose. For each territory in n's list (int8 nation +0x60 entries at +0x61+j, territory + 1): t = entry - 1. f7C7C4(t, n) is called and its result never used. t qualifies when area record t+1 has count > 1 and marker +1+n == n, f7C838(t, n, 0, &x) == n's tokens there (n would lose all), movable +0x24+n > 0 and byte +0x3B == 0. Up to 0x1F0 candidates go into a local list. Pass 1: f48028(&cnt, list, t, n, 0x17) finds a refuge. If it returns one, all movable tokens go to its first entry: land-move record type 0x29 and f57CA4(t, dest, n, 1, k); t is marked done (-1). Pass 2 (mode 0x0C): for neighbours u with exactly 2 nations, m = f4CC5C(u, n, 0); tokens move one at a time while movable > 0 and m > 0. Pass 3 (mode 0x18): the rest move one at a time to the first neighbour. Land-move records are 4 bytes at 0x107694 + 4i (count [0x1079B4]): +0 from, +1 to, +2 count, +3 type.
0x4bbdc.globals: reads nation +0x60/+0x61..; area +1, +1+n, +0x0E+n, +0x24+n, +0x3B; writes land move list 0x107694 / [0x1079B4]; area records via f57CA4
0x4bbdc.calls: f7C7C4* (result unused), f7C838*, f48028* x3 (neighbour finder, 5th argument on the stack), f57CA4 x3, f4CC5C
0x4bbdc.risks: 2 KB stack frame: the 0x1F0-entry list and the neighbour list are locals handed to f48028 by pointer. No bound check on [0x1079B4]. The f7C7C4 call must stay, for its side effects (G).

0x4c074.purpose: AI nation n (eax) attacks neighbouring land held by one other nation. The list of n's territories (+0x61..) is copied into the global 0xF7CA0[] with count [0xF7C9C]. For each territory t with flags 0xE2C18+3t+2 bits 0/1 clear, n alone there, movable > 0 and tokens > f78D08(t, n): surplus = tokens - limit. For each land neighbour u (list [0xF8E7C+4t]: int16 count, then entries) held by one nation that is not n: m = f7C760(u) (the first nation 1..11 with marker == itself); diff = Metalworking(m) - Metalworking(n) (int8 +0x26); e = m's tokens at u. The supporting neighbours w of u (n alone there, flag bit 1 clear, tokens > limit) are collected into 0xF7CA0 again; S = their summed surplus. f7C838(u, n, S, &x) trial. Go ahead if both sides lose something (0xF547C[m] + 0xF547C[n] > 0) and m's losses >= n's, or else if limit(u) == 1. Then a dice roll from the pre-rolled table: v = int16 0x112A94[(u % 4) + 3][n - 1] / 300 (0..99). The attack happens only if v < 100 - 10*AI level + 10*int8 nation +0x9B. AI level = bits 2..3 of byte 0xE1625: (word [0xE1624] << 4) >> 14. need = 1 if limit(u) == 1 and the trial was unfavourable; such a move is skipped when byte 0xF06C0[n] > 0xF06C0[m]. Otherwise need = e + diff + (e + diff < S). Then single tokens move from each w (movable > 0, tokens > limit) to u, as land-move records type 0x11, count 1.
0x4c074.globals: area records (+1, +1+n, +0x0E+n, +0x24+n); 0xE2C18 flags; 0xE1639+35t population limit bits 3..5; 0xF8E7C land adjacency; nation +0x26 Metalworking, +0x9B; 0xE1624 word (AI level bits); 0x112A94 int16[30][10] AI random table (from f7BCD4); 0xF06C0[n] bytes; 0xF547C losses (from f7C838); writes 0xF7C9C / 0xF7CA0 (the scratch list the nation choice also uses), 0x107694 / [0x1079B4]
0x4c074.risks: BUG(1995) candidate (D): the outer loop walks n's territory list in the global 0xF7CA0/[0xF7C9C], and the inner neighbour gathering resets [0xF7C9C] = 0 and overwrites the same array. After the first attack candidate the outer loop iterates over the support list instead; a literal translation must keep the shared global. Randomness comes only through the table 0x112A94, filled with game_rand in phase TAXATION by f7BCD4. Signed idiv (u % 4) and the 16-bit word shifts for the level must be exact.

0x4c6e4.purpose: AI nation n (eax) reinforces threatened territories by one token. For t 0..0x9C whose AI flag byte 0xF3581[314(n-1) + 2t] has bit 0x02: L0 = f7C838(t, n, 0, &x). Skip if n's tokens at t > L0 (safe). L1 = f7C838(t, n, 1, &x); skip if L1 > L0 or tokens + 1 < L1. Act only if territory byte 0xE1639+35t has bit 0x40 or byte 0xF0044[160n + t] has bit 0x02. f48028(&cnt, list, t, n, 0x0A) and f48D44(&cnt, list, n, t, 1) build the source list. The first source with tokens > f78D08 gives one token: f57CA4(src, t, n, 1, 1) and land-move record type 0x1A. If none, f48028(..., 0x12) + f48D44, and the first source with movable > 0 gives one. At most one move per t.
0x4c6e4.globals: 0xF3581 (int16[157] per nation, bit 0x02: G AI target flags), 0xF0044[n][160] bit 0x02, territory byte 0xE1639+35t bit 0x40 (G), area +0x0E+n, +0x24+n; writes 0x107694 / [0x1079B4]
0x4c6e4.risks: Local 0xB0-int list passed by pointer to f48028/f48D44 (which take a 5th argument on the stack). Loop bound 0x9D (157), not 160.

0x4c9b8.purpose: AI nation n (eax) goes for target territories marked x (edx). Runs only if int8 nation +0x98 (G: tokens on the board) >= 14. Collects territories t-1 for records t = 1..0x9D whose byte +0x3B+n == x, sorts them with f48D44(&cnt, list, n, 0, 5), then for each target: r = -1. The first time per round ([0x107D40] == 0) a target with a city (flag bit 0) and no nations: r = f4CEE4(t, n, &tmp), [0x107D40] = 1. Otherwise for a target without a city: f4CC5C(t, n, 4) when count <= 1, or when count > 1 and n is already there. If r != -1: f7A940 and 0x7AA1C (push the World State and Move stacks), then 0x3580C(r, t, n, 1, r) plans the move. A non-zero return means it failed: f7AC60 and 0x7AE14(0) restore, and [0x107D40] = 0. Zero means success: 0x7AD24 and 0x7AD7C drop the saved copies, and area byte +0x3B of t = n's tokens there.
0x4c9b8.globals: nation +0x98; area +1, +1+n, +0x0E+n, +0x3B, +0x3B+n (per-nation AI marks); 0xE2C18 flag bit 0; [0x107D40] once-per-round flag
0x4c9b8.calls: f48D44*, f4CC5C*, f4CEE4*, f7A940, 0x7AA1C, 0x3580C (stack argument), 0x7AD24, 0x7AD7C, f7AC60, 0x7AE14
0x4c9b8.risks: Speculative planning through the World State Stack (f7A940/f7AC60) and the Move Stack (0x7AA1C/0x7AD7C/0x7AE14). The push/pop pairs must match exactly or the stack-overflow messages fire. The 0xA8-entry list is a stack array.

0x4cc5c.purpose: Tokens nation n needs to take territory t. Args eax = t, edx = n, ebx = mode; returns need or -1. m = the strongest other nation at t (k = 0..11, k != n-1, max tokens +0x0E+(k+1)); big = 2 if m >= 10 (pirates or barbarians), else 1. No enemy tokens: returns 1 if t is empty, else -1. base = population limit (territory byte +1 bits 3..5) - 1, at least 1. If byte 0xF06C0[m] < 0xF06C0[n] or big: need = e + base - own + (Metalworking[m] - Metalworking[n]), where e = m's tokens and own = n's tokens at t. Else returns -1 if mode == 3 or if 0x7CAB4(n) == 0. Otherwise f48028(&cnt, list, t, m, 0x0C): with no neighbours the same formula, else need = e + min(f4D110(t, &cnt, list, m, 0), 2) + base - own + the Metalworking diff.
0x4cc5c.globals: area +0x0E+k tokens, +1 count; territory 0xE1639+35t; byte 0xF06C0[n]; nation +0x26 Metalworking
0x4cc5c.risks: Signed byte compare on 0xF06C0. Several exits through different epilogues (returns at 0x4CEC7 and 0x4CEDB). Local 0xAC-int list.

0x4cee4.purpose: Tokens n needs to take the city at t. Args eax = t, edx = n, ebx = int *out. City owner m = byte 0xE2C18+3t (+0); big = 2 if m > 9. E = int8 +0x2A (Engineering) of m minus that of n; e = m's tokens at t (+0x0E+m). If 0xF06C0[m] < 0xF06C0[n] or big: need = e + 7 + E, *out = need. Else f48028(&cnt, list, t, m, 0x0C) and r = f4D29C(t, m) (m's sea reinforcement). If cnt + r == 0: same formula, *out = need. Else *out = 7 + E (without e), s = f4D110(t, &cnt, list, m, 0), extra = 0 if s + r == 0, else s + r - 1 + (Metalworking[m] && !Metalworking[n]). Returns e + 7 + extra + E. The 7 is the city's worth in tokens.
0x4cee4.risks: *out gets different meanings on different paths (with or without e). Dword-sar-24 reads of the advance bytes (0xF14F3+199m sar 24 = +0x2A) next to byte reads (0xF14F2 = +0x26): offsets are easy to misread.

0x4d110.purpose: Land reinforcement potential of nation m near t. Args eax = t, edx = int *cnt, ebx = list, ecx = m, stack k (ret 4). Calls f4892C(t, &cnt2, list2, *cnt, [list, m, 0x0B]) to get a second-ring list. Then over the given list and over list2: for each territory u with count != 0, s = m's tokens at u - k. If s > 0 and (territory u byte +1 bit 0x40 is clear or s <= 4), sum += s. Returns sum.
0x4d110.risks: Mixed register and stack arguments (callee-pops ret 4; f4892C takes three stack arguments). The 0xA8-int local list2.

0x4d29c.purpose: How many tokens nation m (edx) can bring to t (eax) by sea. Pushes the World State and Move stacks, 0x460C0(m), [0xF5908] = 0 around 0x46BB8(m). For each ship k < +0x40 whose f5843C(s, t, m, points) == 1: f58888(s, t, m, points) builds routes; 0xF8418 and 0xF84B8 (160 each) and 0xF8194 (640) are memset to 0xFF. Each route i gets byte +8 = 0x374E0(i, t, m, 999, [1]) (tokens it can collect). Fewer than 20 routes: a descending bubble sort on +8 with 16-byte swaps; otherwise qsort(0x108820, count, 16, compare 0x3530C). best[k] = int8 record 0 +8. Then f7AC60 and 0x7AE14(0) restore the stacks. Returns max(best[k], 0).
0x4d29c.globals: nation +0x40/+0x41+k/+0x45+2k; [0xF5908]; 0x108820 route records (+8 written), [0x109E00]; 0xF8418, 0xF84B8, 0xF8194 AI scratch
0x4d29c.calls: f7A940, 0x7AA1C, 0x460C0, 0x46BB8, f5843C*, f58888*, f7D5D0 x4 (memset), 0x374E0 (stack argument), qsort (0x8C331) with comparator 0x3530C, f7AC60, 0x7AE14
0x4d29c.risks: Watcom qsort is not stable. For equal keys the port must reproduce 0x8C331's exact algorithm, or AI choices differ. 0x3530C is a function pointer (address-taken). best[] is a 4-int stack array indexed by ship (overflows if +0x40 > 4). It reads record 0 +8 even when no route exists (0xFF from the memset = -1). The routes are evaluated inside a speculative World State push/pop.

0x4d518.purpose: Plays back and applies AI nation n's planned land moves. Args eax = n, edx = show. If show and Show AI Movement (byte 0xF097C bit 0x40): sprintf "%s is moving." (0xB4734, nation name 0xC768C[n]); f3A990; the message area's y and h are temporarily set to 0x14C/0x7B for f3A9F4 and then restored; f3CBBC. If [0x1079B4] > 0: byte 0x108804 = 1 (token mode); with show, f4D82C sorts and merges the list. Per record: from 0xFF is skipped; from 0xC8 sets 0xE2C18+3*to+2 |= 2 (a marker record, no move); from 0xC9 is skipped. Otherwise c = +2; c > 75 sets flags a = b = 1 and c -= 75, c > 50 sets a = 1 and c -= 50. With show and Show AI: f3F670, f3F624(from, 0xF), f3DA60(from), f459E4(n), f3CBBC. Colour of from = 5 if n's movable there == c, else 0xF. Colour of to = 0xE if a && !b, else 5/0xF by movable at to. Then f5A084(5, n, from, 1, [from, colour_from, to, colour_to, c, show]). After the list: if no ship moves and show and Show AI, f3D9FC(n), f3CBBC, f78A20(500). Ship moves go to f4DACC(n, show). Without Speedup AI Movement (bit 0 of 0xF097D) there is a 300 ms pause before and after.
0x4d518.globals: land move list 0x107694 / [0x1079B4]; ship move count [0x107D3C]; byte 0x108804 (1 tokens / 2 ships); toggles 0xF097C bit 0x40, 0xF097D bit 0; message area 0xBB3FA..0xBB400 (int16); 0xE2C1A flag bit 1; area +0x24+n
0x4d518.calls: sprintf 0x7DB3D, f3A990, f3A9F4, f3CBBC x3, f4D82C*, f3F670, f3F624, f3DA60, f459E4, f5A084*, f3D9FC, f78A20 x3, f4DACC*
0x4d518.waits_for_input: timed only (f78A20: 500 and 300 ms, plus f5A084's blinks); no click
0x4d518.risks: When show == 0 the colour locals [ebp-0x18]/[ebp-0x14] are passed to f5A084 uninitialised (f5A084 ignores them then). Magic encodings in the move list: from 0xC8/0xC9, count > 50/75. The 16-bit word test (word [0xF097C] << 7 >> 15) is bit 0 of 0xF097D.

0x4d82c.purpose: Reorders the AI land move list 0x107694 for display. Writes 0xFF as from of record [count] (a sentinel), copies the list to a local array, and rebuilds it with the records whose count +2 < 50 first and then those >= 50. Over the first part (m records) two bubble passes: by to (+1) ascending, then by from (+0) ascending (unsigned compares, swapping whole dwords). Then it merges runs with the same from/to: for i < m-1 with from <= 0xA0, j advances while record j+1 has the same from and to, and record j+1's from is set to 0xFF. If j != i, record i's count += j - i.
0x4d82c.risks: Local copy of at most 205 records (0x334 bytes) with no bound check. The merge adds j - i (one token per record assumed), not the merged counts. The merge scan can run past m into the >= 50 records and erase one with the same from/to (G, 1995 quirk); it is stopped only by the sentinel at [count]. 0x4DAAC..0x4DACB after its ret is 0x4DACC's jump table (data inside code).

0x4dacc.purpose: Plays back AI nation n's ship move list. Args eax = n, edx = show. Byte 0x108804 = 2. For each record i < [0x107D3C] at 0x1079B8 + 6i, a switch on type +4 - 3 through the 8-entry jump table 0x4DAAC. 3 (load): area[from+1] +0x2D+n = ship +3; f5A4BC(5, n, from, count +2, [show]). 4 (unload): area[to+1] +0x2D+n = ship; f5A750(5, n, to, count, [show]). 5 (unload all): the same with count = the ship's aboard (+0x4D + the selected index at f3E8FC(to)). 6..9: nothing. 10 (ship move): area[from+1] +0x2D+n = ship; colour = 0xF if any of n's ships at from has points > 0, else 5; f5A2C4(5, n, from, from, [colour, to, show]). Ends with byte 0x108804 = 1.
0x4dacc.globals: ship move list 0x1079B8 / [0x107D3C]; area +0x2D+n (selected ship, written); nation +0x40, +0x41+k, +0x45+2k, +0x4D+k; 0x108804
0x4dacc.risks: Jump table at 0x4DAAC (8 dwords, before the function); types outside 3..10 are ignored (ja). Callee-pops stack arguments. The 6-byte record index is built as lea 3i, *2.

0x5055c.purpose: Play-by-email end of turn: write the state for the next player and quit to DOS. mkdir("PBEM_OUT"), f53A00 (delete pbem_out\*.hst). r = -0x5F (return to host) unless int16 [0xF4090] == 1, in which case r = f53EA8(0xEE20C) asks whom to send to. Return to host: name "%s.hst" (if [0x1087D4] != 0, the player of int16 [0xF5476] is nation byte 0xE1622, or int16 [0xF40B4] != 0) else "PBEM_OUT\%s.hst" from 0xEE20C. fopen "wb", save via 0x5E9B0 with description "%s to Host file", fclose, crc = f7BBF0(name), fopen "ab" and append the 4-byte CRC. Send direct: finds the next player in the order list int16 0xF06B0[] after the current one (strnicmp of 0xEE20C's first 4 letters against the codes 0xC7664) that has nation +0x9C != 0 and an entry in the trade records 0x111122+16j (j < int16 [0x112548]). The file is 0xEE220 with its first 4 letters replaced by that nation's code, "PBEM_OUT\%s" or "%s", description "%s to xxx file"; byte 0xE1622 = next nation; strcpy to 0xF5230. Then remove(0xEE220), f508FC(r, name, next), remove savgamea.dat and savgameb.dat, f39F50(-1), [0xF5500] = 0, f44CAC (quit).
0x5055c.globals: 0xEE20C / 0xEE220 PBEM names; 0xE1622 nation; 0xF06AE/0xF06B0 order; 0xF4104+32p player records; 0xF5472..0xF5476; 0xF40B4; 0x1087D4; 0x111122 trade records; [0x112548]; nation +0x9C; writes 0xF5230, 0xF5500
0x5055c.calls: mkdir, f53A00*, f53EA8*, sprintf 0x7DB3D x7, fopen 0x7D8C8 x3, 0x5E9B0 (write save) x2, fclose 0x7D95E x3, f7BBF0 x2, strnicmp, fwrite, remove x3, f508FC*, 0x39F50, f44CAC
0x5055c.waits_for_input: through f53EA8 and f508FC (f78BA4 click waits)
0x5055c.risks: PBEM only (dropped in the port by Erik's ruling). Never returns (quits). Uninitialised read: the current index [ebp-0x30] is set only when strnicmp matches. If no next player is found, [ebp-0x20] = -1 indexes 0xC7664[-1] (a garbage pointer). The string copies are unrolled 2-byte strcpy loops.

0x508fc.purpose:
Instructions after a PBEM file was written. Args eax = r, edx = file name, ebx = next nation. Background 0x15 (f3CD6C) into the back buffer, colour 13, font 2. Return-to-host for the host/local case: "The file %s.HST has been written.  When" / "the other players have returned their files, put" / "them in the %s directory." (0xF56F4) and "This message has also been written to SENDHOST.TXT" (font 1); the same goes to sendhost.txt with fprintf. Remote player: "Email the file %s.HST located in" / "the PBEM_OUT sub-directory to the person" / "hosting this PBEM game." plus the SENDHOST note; the file gets the formatted first line and "
sub-directory to the person hosting this PBEM game.
". Direct send: "Email the following file located in the" / "PBEM_OUT sub-directory:", then the file name at (0x5A, y) and "to %s" (player name 0xF4106+32p) at (0xDC, y), "This list has also been written to SENDHOST.TXT"; the file gets "%s to %s
". CONTINUE (0x2A of dialog 0xBB800) is moved to (0x109, y), f3B05C, f3CC14, then the click wait.

0x54824.purpose: The game loop (main 0x118C9). Repeats while done == 0. Top of each turn: in phases 15/16 with digital sound ([0xF625C]), stops sample [0xF6278] (AIL_active_sample_count([0xF6274]) > 0 -> AIL_end_sample), sets its loop count to 1, and frees the WAV named at 0xF6118 (0x7CB9D([0xF6260], f7D2E8(name)), name[0] = 0). Round label: sprintf(0x109E7C, "%d", int16 [0xF40FC]) on button 0x101 of 0xF596C. Then 0x7C960(). switch (byte [0xF4102]) through the 21-entry jump table 0x547D0; each case usually: f553C0 (phase music), the phase routine, the next phase number, 0x5E7B4 (empty stub), 0x5E8EC(phase) autosave "AutoSaved after %s - R%d", PBEM export f5055C when needed, then 0x22B00 (elimination check). 0 TAXATION: f7BCD4 (AI random table), 0x66050. 1 POPULATION EXPANSION: 0x673A8. 2 CENSUS: 0x13D44. 3 SHIP MAINTENANCE: 0x60AE0, 0x60BD8. 4 SHIP CONSTRUCTION: 0x60AE0, DoShipContruction 0x61940. 5 MOVEMENT: snapshots area 0xE31B8 -> 0xE8888 and 0xE2C18 -> 0xE2FD8 (0x1E0 bytes); f55574; then area -> 0xE5D20, 0xE2C18 -> 0xE2DF8, nations 0xF14CC -> 0xF1FB0 (0xAE2); [0xEDF58] = 1, [0xEDF5C] = round (for REPLAY); next phase 6 with PBEM, else 7; PBEM: 0x6E53C, f5055C. 6 VIEW MOVEMENT (PBEM): f59298, 0xE1624 &= ~1. 7 CONFLICT: 0x5AAA4(1). 8 CITY CONSTRUCTION: int16 [0xF408E] = 0, 0x32214. 9 REMOVE SURPLUS: 0x5C238(1). 10 CITY SUPPORT: int16 [0x109E20] = 0, 0x5C62C; int16 [0xF5476] = 1. 11 ACQUIRE GOODS: int16 [0xF5478] = 0, DrawTradingCards 0x6BD98; byte [0x110F74] = 0. 12 DECLARE OFFERS: if f55500() (two or more nations have the minimum goods): [0xF4230] = 1, 0x6F270, bytes 0xF09D4[0..9] = 0. Otherwise, when [0xF4230] is set, "Lack of nations with sufficient trade goods (%d min) cancels this round of trading." (0x7983C), and phase 15. 13 COUNTER OFFERS: 0x723DC. 14 ACCEPT TRADES: 0x734E4. Then, unless int16 [0xF4090] is set, the Trading Wrapup (f763FC) if trades occurred, and a count of nations with byte 0xF09D4[n] == 1 holding >= min goods (computers: max(min, 6)). Another session (phase 12, int16 [0xF5476]++) if count >= (byte 0xE1625 bit 0x10 ? 2 : ([0xF40EC] + 1)/2) and sessions < byte 0xE1623 & 0x0F. PBEM shows "%s nations have indicated their desire\nto have Trade Session %d" (0xC08AC words). Otherwise phase 15. 15 CALAMITIES: 0x1E0A0 with int16 0xF7AFC/0xF7AFE cleared around it; PBEM copies nine 25-byte records 0xF07B4 -> 0xF0898 and clears their counts. 16 MONOTHEISM CONVERT: 0x21914. 17 CITY SUPPORT: 0x5C62C. 18 ACQUIRE CIVILIZATION: 0x162D0; [0xF09E4] = any nation with Roadbuilding (+0x28); 0x1A3A0 Tool Acquisition Wrapup unless PBEM. 19 DISCARD EXCESS: 0x6E770. 20 SHOW AST: system("copy savgamea.dat savgameb.dat >NUL:"), f55258; PBEM: 0x1A3A0. done = f136B0(3) (AST alteration, 1 = someone won); if not done, phase 0 and autosave(20). Over 20: only 0x22B00. After the loop: 0x14294 (Final Civilization Standings), f55304, remove("savgameb.dat"), [0xF5500] = 0, f44CAC (quit).

0x55574.purpose: MOVEMENT phase. The message area is set to (169, 334, 300, 34). For t < 157: clear flag bit 1 of 0xE2C18+3t+2, and without a city (bit 0) zero +0 and +1. Allocates TempTerr (0x2B65) and Tempnation (199) with malloc 0x822B5 (and the no-op tracer f78B24). Movement order int16 0xF06B0[] with count [0xF06AE]: the census order 0xF069A[] (count 0xF0698), nations without Military (+0x35) first, then those with it. Player buttons f783B8, f7A8D0, [0xF09E4] = any nation with Roadbuilding. Background 3, f7876C, dialogs 0xC4A3C (MOVE TOKENS 0x26, 1-5 0xC4..0xC8, MOVE SHIPS 0x27, FIND UNMOVED 0x29, UNDO MOVE 0x28, FINISHED 0x2A, RESTART 0x41) and 0xC4E28 (EMBARK, DISEMBARK, DISEMBARK ALL, NEXT SHIP and their short twins 0x2B..0x32) are appended with f7853C; f5D14C(0, 1); token mode; int16 [0xF09E0] = 1. Per nation n in order (only own nation with PBEM; nations with +0x9A != 0 otherwise): [0xF40F8] = n; snapshot of the area records and n's record into TempTerr/Tempnation (RESTART restores them); PBEM own nation shows "NOTE: Tax assessments, ...". AI (+0x9A == 2): saves the seed [0xCAC5C], pushes the World State, shows "%s considers movement." (0x79270), disables the dialog, pushes again, runs 0x353C4(n), pops (trial), runs 0x461BC(n) (the real AI moves via 0x4AC50.., 0x4D518), shows "Movement for %s complete.", then adds REPLAY (0xC9) / CONTINUE (0x2A) from 0xC59EC and waits. REPLAY (-0x5E) restores the seed and pops the World State, then plays the same moves again. CONTINUE (-1) runs 0x7AD24. Human: movable +0x24+n = tokens where marked (boxes colour 0xF); MOVE SHIPS is disabled without ships; ship points = 4 + Clothmaking (+0x25); start territory 0xC4990[n], else f577B0. Click loop while f5790C(n): f775F0, poll fg_mousepos, f3D434(x, y, 0xF596C). -1 FINISHED: "There are still tokens left on your ships..." if f57AFC, else PBEM bookkeeping and f57254 confirmation. -2/-3: boxes redrawn. -0x63 RESTART: f57160. -0x79 FIND UNMOVED: f57810. -4 UNDO: from = [0x108808]. A territory click checks with f57BD8 and gives "You have no tokens in that territory." / "There are no tokens with movement points left in that territory." / "There are no ships in that territory." Tokens: the first click selects the source (f576F8, f5D14C, f572CC, colour 0xE). The second click moves int16 [0xF09E0] tokens if f582CC (land adjacency), f57CE8 + f57E28, and records undo data 0x108808..0x108818. Up to 1 + Roadbuilding (+0x28) moves from one source chain through own land without a foreign city (f574B0, 400 ms pause), else "You may not move your token into this territory." Ships: "Ship #%d has no movement points remaining". f58330 checks the move (-2 "You may not move your ship into this territory.", -3 "...into the open sea as its last move."), f580CC, points - 1. When nothing is left: "You have no more tokens (or ships) to move.  Press FINISHED." and buttons disabled. PBEM records 10-byte moves into [0xF09B4] (realloc, per nation [0xF0984+4n], count int16 0xF09BA+2n) and restores the area/own nation records at the end. Cleanup: remove the dialogs, f7ABD0, free the temp blocks.

If f577B0 returns -1 (no tokens), f3F624(-1, 0xF) writes 0xFFB5F and f3DA60(-1) reads 0xC803C[-1]. malloc(10000) (0x822B5) for the PBEM store is called with edx/ebx left over from earlier code; harmless, malloc reads only eax (D 0x822B5).
