0x577b0.purpose: First territory with movable tokens of nation n: for r 1..0x9C, returns r - 1 when area byte +0x24+n of record r != 0; else -1.
0x577b0.risks: Returns -1, which the caller uses as a territory index unchecked.

0x57810.purpose: FIND UNMOVED for nation n. Token mode (byte 0x108804 == 1): from record [0x109E18] + 1 to 0x9D, the next record r with movable +0x24+n != 0; stores [0x109E18] = r and returns r - 1. At the end it resets [0x109E18] = 0 and searches again. Ship mode: from k = [0x109E1C] + 1 to 3, the next ship whose location low byte != 0 and points +0x41+k > 0; [0x109E1C] = k, returns location - 1. At the end it resets to -1 and searches again.
0x57810.risks: Infinite loop if nothing qualifies (it restarts the scan for ever). The callers only reach it while f5790C is true, but that test also counts ships with tokens aboard and no points, which this scan does not find.

0x5790c.purpose: Anything left to move for nation n: f57940(n) || f5799C(n).

0x57940.purpose: 1 if any area record r 1..0x9D has movable tokens of n (+0x24+n), else 0.

0x5799c.purpose: 1 if any ship k < +0x40 of nation n has points +0x41+k > 0 or tokens aboard +0x4D+k != 0, else 0.

0x57a90.purpose: 1 if one of nation n's ships k < +0x40 is at territory t: int16 +0x45+2k (the full word) == t + 1.
0x57a90.risks: Compares the full 16-bit word, while other code masks the low byte. A literal port must keep the difference.

0x57afc.purpose: 1 if any of nation n's ships has tokens aboard (+0x4D+k != 0).

0x57bd8.purpose: Clicked territory t valid for nation n in the current mode. Tokens (0x108804 == 1): area record t+1 has count != 0 and one of the markers +2..+0x0A equals n. Ships (== 2): one of ships 0..3 (always 4, not +0x40) has location low byte == t + 1. Returns 1/0.
0x57bd8.risks: The ship test scans all four slots regardless of the ship count.

0x57ca4.purpose: Move k tokens of n from a to b: f57CE8(a, n, flag, k) then f57E28(b, n, k). Args eax = a, edx = b, ebx = n, ecx = flag, stack k (ret 4).
0x57ca4.risks: k is a stack argument; callee pops 4 bytes.

0x582cc.purpose: Land adjacency: 1 if u is in t's land list ([0xF8E7C+4t]: int16 count, then int16 entries), else -2.

0x58330.purpose: Can nation n's selected ship at t move to u (eax = t, edx = u, ebx = n). k = area[t+1] +0x2D+n. With points +0x41+k > 1, u must be in the coast list [0xF90FC+4t], or with Astronomy (+0x2B) in the sea list [0xF937C+4t]. On the last point only the coast list counts, and the default result becomes -3 with Astronomy ("open sea as its last move"). Returns 1 if found, else -2 or -3.

0x5843c.purpose: Is there a sea route between a and b shorter than k points for nation n? k == 0 returns 0. Swaps so that a <= b, then f58568 (table 2) with Astronomy (+0x2B), else f584B4 (table 1).

0x584b4.purpose: Route check in N.RL table 1: linear scan of the [0xFFD44] 8-byte records at 0xFFD48 (+0 from, +1 to, +4 first route index) for from == a and to == b. Then counts the non-0xFF bytes of the 4-byte route at [0x10740C] + 4*first; 1 if that count < k, else 0.
0x584b4.risks: Only the first route of the pair is measured. The block pointer [0x10740C] is a port heap handle (load_heap_ptr).

0x58568.purpose: The same as f584B4 for table 2 (Astronomy): [0x101DC8] records at 0x101DCC (+4 index at 0x101DD0).

0x5861c.purpose: Territories reachable from t by nation n with k points. memset(0x107EE4, 0, 0x280) (int32[160]). For every route-table record (table 2 with Astronomy, else 1) with t as an endpoint whose first route has fewer than k intermediate territories, marks the other endpoint: reach[other] = 1.
0x5861c.risks: Branch layout jumps into the middle of the loops (shared tail at 0x586E8/0x587FB).

0x58888.purpose: All usable routes a->b for nation n with k points. Args eax = a, edx = b, ebx = n, ecx = k. k == 0 gives [0x109E00] = 0. Swaps so that a <= b and remembers whether it did. memset(0x108820, 0xFF, 0x15E0), then f58DCC (Astronomy) or f58A74. If swapped, each record's 6 path bytes are reversed (0<->5, 1<->4, 2<->3) and shifted left while byte 0 is 0xFF. Then each record's +6 = k - (index of the first 0xFF from byte 2, at most 6, - 1), the points left at the end. Records are 16 bytes: +0..+5 path, +6 points left, +8 (used by f4D29C).
0x58888.risks: Global route buffer shared by many AI routines (re-entrancy: callers keep copies in locals).

0x58a74.purpose: Fills 0x108820 with N.RL table 1 routes from a to b for nation n within k points. Args eax = a, edx = b, ebx = n, ecx = k. Starts at the first-record index int16 0x107410[a] and finds the record with from == a and to == b. Each route j < int16 +2 is the 4 bytes at [0x10740C] + 4(first + j). The record gets +0 = a, then the intermediate territories u. A u where n has no tokens (+0x0E+n) and 0xC80DC[u] == 8 (an ordinary territory, not one of the eight open-sea areas 0..7) blocks the route: block[u]++ in a local int16[160]. Then b follows the copied bytes. A route with length >= k ends the scan; an unblocked one is kept ([0x109E00]++). If nothing was kept, the territory u with the fewest blocks is unblocked (block[u] = 0) and the scan is redone, now blocking on block[u] != 0. This repeats until a route is kept or no counter remains.
0x58a74.globals: 0xFFD44/0xFFD48 table 1, 0x107410 index, [0x10740C] block, 0xC80DC territory type, area +0x0E+n; writes 0x108820, [0x109E00]
0x58a74.risks: If the first index 0x107410[a] is -1, the scan starts at record -1 (0xFFD40, the count field). No bound on [0x109E00] (350 records). Rejected routes leave their bytes in the slot the next route overwrites; a shorter later route would keep stale bytes. G: harmless if routes are sorted by length. The int16 reads are dword sar 16 (+2 count).

0x58dcc.purpose: Identical to f58A74 but on N.RL table 2 (Astronomy): records 0x101DC8/0x101DCC, index 0x107550[a]. The code differs only in those addresses.
0x58dcc.risks: As f58A74. One C function with a table parameter reproduces both exactly.

0x59298.purpose: PBEMViewer: replays the other players' recorded moves. Builds the movement order (non-Military first) as f55574 does, then f783B8. Allocates copies of the area records (0x2B65) and 12 nation records (0xAE2), f78B0C("PBEMViewer") (no-op), and appends dialog 0xC5600 (REPLAY/CONTINUE). Background 3, f7876C, f5D14C(0, 0), f3C720(0xF596C), f3B05C. Saves the phase byte, sets it to 5, hides the mouse. Per nation in order: movable tokens = tokens, ship points = 4 + Clothmaking, status panel. Then its stored 10-byte moves ([0xF0984+4n], count int16 0xF09BA+2n: +0 origin, +1 move number, +2 from, +3 colour, +4 movable, +5 to, +6 colour, +7 movable at to, +8 type, +9 count) are replayed through the 12-entry jump table 0x59268 on type 1..12. 1: f5A084(saved phase, n, origin, move# == 1, [from, colour, to, colour, count, 1]). 2: f5A2C4. 3: f5A4BC. 4/5: f5A750. 6: inline token-move blink with f57CE8/f57E28. 7: f5A600. 8, 9, 11: f5A8FC. 10: nothing. 12: ship selection with f576F8/f426D0/f3E89C. At the end: phase byte restored, the dialog back, f3D9FC/f459E4 for own nation 0xE1622, f78BA4 loop. REPLAY (-0x5E) restores the records from the copies and replays; CONTINUE (-1) removes the dialog and frees the copies.

0x5a084.purpose: Animates and applies one land move. Args al = phase byte, edx = n, ebx = territory to highlight, ecx = flag; stack [from, colour_from, to, colour_to, k, show], ret 0x18. If show and (PBEM or Show AI Movement): f3F670, f3F624(ebx, 0xF), phase byte 0xF4102 = al, f5D14C(n, from) if n is human (+0x9A == 3), phase byte = 5 (not the saved value), f3CBBC. Then from's token box blinks 0xE/5 with f3DA60 centring and 100 ms waits ([0xC65B8]): five extra blinks without Speedup, and a last wait of [0xC65B0] (500) or [0xC65BC] (300 with Speedup). Then f57CE8(from, n, flag == 1, k) and f57E28(to, n, k). With show: from box colour_from, to box 0xE/5/0xE/colour_to, each followed by f3D52C(0, 0) and a 100 ms wait, and the final 500/300 ms wait.
0x5a084.risks: Leaves the phase byte at 5 regardless of what it was (0x59298 restores its own copy at the end). Callee-pops 6 stack arguments; 8-bit first argument.

0x5a2c4.purpose: Animates and applies one ship move. Args al = phase byte, edx = n, ebx = territory to highlight, ecx = from; stack [colour, to, show], ret 0xC. With show and (PBEM or Show AI): highlight, the phase byte trick, f5D14C(n, from) for humans, phase byte = 5, f3CBBC, from's ship box (f3F70C) blinks as in f5A084. Then f580CC(from, to, n), the selected ship at to (area[to+1] +0x2D+n) loses a point (+0x41+k - 1), f576F8(from). With show: from box = colour, to box 0xE, f3DA60(to), f3CBBC, final 500/300 ms wait.

0x5a2c4.risks: Like f5A084 it does not restore the phase byte. Callee-pops 3 stack arguments.

0x5a4bc.category: movement replay (AI ship playback 0x4DACC and the PBEM viewer)
0x5a4bc.purpose: Replays an EMBARK step (first coast) in the PBEM movement viewer. Args: al = phase byte to show, edx = nation n, ebx = index i (into 0xC803C), ecx = count k, [esp+4] = show. t2 = f3E8FC(i). k times: f57CE8(0xC803C[i], n, 1, 1) (one token off the land, movable too) and nation n byte +0x4D+s ++ with s = area[t2+1] +0x2D+n (tokens aboard the selected ship of t2). If show and (PBEM bit 0x80 of 0xE1624 or option bit 0x40 of 0xF097C): byte 0xF4102 = al, f3F698(t2, area[t2+1]+0x24+n == 0 ? 5 : 0x0F), f5D14C([0xF40F8], t2) if nation +0x9A == 3, 0xF4102 = 5 (MOVEMENT, hard-coded), f3DA60(t2), f3CBBC, f78A20(word 0xF097C bit 8 ? [0xC65BC]=300 : [0xC65B0]=500 ms). ret 4.

0x5aaa4.purpose: Conflict resolution. eax = show (1 from the game loop 0x54B56, 0 from AI simulations). show: message area (169,340,300,20), nation list int16 0xF06AE/0xF06B0[] = nations 1..9 with +0x9A != 0, f783B8(0xF596C,[0xF5940]), memset(0x109E24,0,81). Scans area records r = 1..157: contested if more than one nation (+1 > 1), or one nation next to a city (tstate[r-1]+2 bit0) whose owner (tstate+0) has no tokens there; listed (local int[60], 0xFF-filled) if tokens of nations 1..11 exceed the population limit (bits 3..5 of terrflag byte 0xE1639+35t) or it is such a city. If any: show sets [0xF40F8] = first nation (PBEM: byte 0xE1622). Two passes (0: no city, 1: city): per entry, if show: background 3 to back buffer, f7876C, append dialog 0xC5214, disable button 7 if >1 human (0xE1620), f3B05C, f3CBBC; clears 0x109E08..0x109E0A and 0xF547C[14], 0xF548C[14]; f5C110(rec) (conflict matrix); highlight; city: f5B224(rec) else if 2+ nations f5B588(r). If show: 'lost territory' marks: a = f5C1CC(t) when the pre-movement copy 0xE8888 had one nation there: area[r]+0x3B+a / +0x3B+b flags (b = f7C760(t)), also for a city that existed before movement (0xE2FD8 copy) but not now; f3DA60, f7844C, f5CDE8(0, 'CONFLICT RESOLUTION - UNITS REMOVED'), f78664(0xC5214). If byte 0x109E08 (plunder pending): f5BA0C(show) with [0xF40F8] saved/restored. After both passes, show: hostility nation(i+1) byte +0xA9+j: +1 (max 5) where 0x109E24[9i+j]==1, else -3 (min 0). If nothing was contested and show: f79270(100, first nation, -200, '' (empty string 0xB5C52), 0). Always f3C314(0xF596C, 7).

With show=0 (AI simulation) it still mutates state outside the World State Stack: 0x109E24, 0x109E08.., 0xF547C/0xF548C, and redraws button 7 (f3C314) into the back buffer. Local list of 60 ints but up to 157 territories could qualify (overflow if >60 conflicts). The 'nothing happened' message is an empty string. Two-pass ordering and 0xFF fill must be kept exactly.

0x5b224.purpose: Attack on a city in area record rec (r = rec+0, t = r-1). owner = tstate[t]+0. If 2+ nations: f5B588(r) first. None left: 0x109E08 = 0. First nation k+1 present: if it is the owner: 0x109E08 = 0, return. Else attacker a. Thresholds by Engineering (nation +0x2A): owner has it and a not: (replace 7, need 8); owner not and a has: (5, 6); else (6, 7). a's tokens < need: attack fails, 0x109E08 = 0, 0xF547C[a] += tokens, a stock +0x99 += tokens, board +0x98 -= tokens, f57CE8(t, a, 0, tokens). Else: replace = min(replace, owner stock +0x99) unless owner == 10 (PIRATE); f78F04(t, owner) removes the city; 0xF548C[owner]++; f57E28(t, owner, replace); owner stock -= replace, board += replace; f5B588(r). If a is a computer (+0x9A == 2) and has >= 6 tokens there, or Architecture (+0x31) and >= 3: tstate[t]+2 |= 2, +0 = a, +1 = turn byte 0xF40FC (G: marks the site for the AI). Then if a still has tokens and a != 11 (BARBARIAN): plunder pending 0x109E08 = 1, 0x109E09 = a, 0x109E0A = owner, int16 0x109E0C = r; else 0x109E08 = 0.

0x5b588.purpose: Resolves a token conflict in area record r (territory r-1). Builds local pairs {count, nation} for nations 1..11 with tokens (count +50 with Metalworking +0x26), total = all tokens. PBEM only (0xE1624 bit 0x80): Military (+0x35) nations make later non-Military ones lose tokens. If count > 1: bubble-sort pairs by count ascending; limit = population limit (terrflag bits 3..5); loop while (no city and total > limit and nations > 1) or (city and nations > 1): for the group of pairs with the current smallest count, each loses 1 token (f57CE8(t, n, 0, 1)); if byte 0xBB3F8 != 0 the token goes back to stock (board -1, stock +1); 0xF547C[n]++; total--; next group, wrapping to 0. Afterwards PIRATE (nation 10) tokens there (+0x18) are all removed: 0xF5486 += them, f57CE8(t, 10, 0, all).
0x5b588.globals: area +1, +0x0E+n, +0x18; tstate +2 bit0; terrflag 0xE1639+35t; nation +0x26 Metalworking, +0x35 Military, +0x98, +0x99; 0xBB3F8 (G: 1 = real resolution, 0 = AI trial; written at 0x39D79/0x4975E); 0xF547C[14]; 0xE1624

Local stack pair array (11 x 2 bytes) with a second copy for compaction. Loop termination relies on f581C4 (via f57CE8) lowering +1. Removal order (groups of equal count, wrap) is specific; keep literal.

0x5ba0c.purpose: eax = show. Then background 3 to back buffer, f7876C. amount = min(a stock +0x99, 3). amount > 0: if a is human (+0x9A == 3, or the local PBEM player): only when show: [0xF40F8] = a, arrows 0xF51AC/0xF51B4 at (296,385)/(330,385), 'UNITS TO' 'TRANSFER', '%s, you may transfer %s%d unit%s from stock to your treasury.' 0x62840.purpose: Returns the chosen option index or -1. Off if int16 0xBB3F0 == 0. f63950(n) sites; budget counters [0x110148] = 4 - ships, 0x11014C = f63AF0 (treasury-only ships), 0x110150 = f63B7C (1+1), 0x110154 = f63C6C (2 levy); '%s considers building ships. (%d,?,?)'. f7A940 x2, f7A610, clock 0x10F2C8, f353C4 + f461BC baseline, base = (int16)f7B044(n), f7AF28, f639E8, recount. Then up to 150 options: f63D10(n) generates combinations (sites 0x110174, treasury 0x11016C, levy 0x110170, count 0x110178); applies them to the state (ships, area +0x1B+n/+0x2D+n, tokens, treasury, stock), stores them in 0x10F6B8 [150][18]; countdown messages '(%d,?,?)' / '(0,%d,%d)' with f79270(-560, n, -200); f461BC timed (0x10F2CC, 0x10F2C0 sum, 0x10F2C4 count, 0x10F2DC); capacity byte +0x11 = ships*mp minus sail steps of the move list; levy options checked against landing moves; score = f7B044 or -100 (unused new ship, or not better than base; site then excluded in 0x10F220); f7AF28. f7AC60; bubble sorts by count asc, capacity desc, score desc; drop options <= base; pick = rand * ties >> 15. f7AD24, f7AC60; busy wait to 0x10F2C8 + 75 ticks.
0x62840.globals: 0xBB3F0; 0x10F30C/0x10F310 sites; 0x10F220[160] excluded sites; 0x110144..0x110178; 0x10F6B8 options; 0x10F2C0..0x10F2EC time/statistics; 0x108190; move list 0x1079B8/0x107D3C; terrflag 0xE163A bit 0x01; nation +0x25, +0x3E, +0x40, +0x45, +0x98, +0x99
0x62840.calls: f63950, f63AF0, f63B7C, f63C6C, sprintf, f79270, f7A940, f7A610, clock, f353C4, f461BC, f7B044, f7AF28, f639E8, memset, f63D10, f7AC60, game_rand, f7AD24
0x62840.waits_for_input: clock busy wait; messages via f79270
0x62840.risks: One game_rand per decision (only if options survive). Timing-dependent search: f6332C prunes by measured clock() times, so results depend on host speed (G: must be made deterministic with a virtual clock). The debug countdown text is shown to the player. In the levy check it compares the move's ship index with j (new ship j) rather than ships+j (G).

0x6332c.purpose: eax = total ship slots. budget = int16 0xBB3E8 (100) * 9500 / 100. avail = sites not excluded; 0x10F2E8 = C(avail) from 0xC7618 (triangular numbers); avg = 0x10F2CC / 0x10F2DC (min 1); elapsed = clock() - 0x10F2C8. If avg*0x10F2E8 + elapsed > budget: (avail > 3) compute a site limit from the remaining time (0xC7618 thresholds, min 3); if limit <= avail: sort options by capacity then score and exclude (0x10F220) the first site of options from 'limit' on, 0x10F2E8 = C(limit). Else: sort the same way; 0x10F2E0 = stage > 2 ? min(avail, 4) : 0; if the next stage would overrun pick 0x10F2E0 from 0x10F2F4 thresholds; 0x10F2EC = 0x10F2F4[0x10F2E0].
0x6332c.risks: Behaviour depends on wall-clock timings (clock()): not reproducible across machines; needs a deterministic clock in the port. Unsigned divisions. Early return leaves a local limit unused.

0x63950.purpose: 0x10F30C = 0; for t < 160 coastal (terrflag bit 0x02) with nation n's tokens > 1: 0x10F310[count++] = t.

0x639e8.category: AI: coastal targets of leading nations
0x639e8.purpose: eax n, edx int *count, ebx int *list. th = int8 0xF06C0[n]. For t < 157 with terrflag 0xE1639 bit 0x40 and 0xE1638 bit 0x02 and exactly one nation present: for k 0..8 with int8 0xF06C1[k] > th and nation k+1 tokens there: list[count++] = t.
0x639e8.globals: 0xF06C0[] (G: per-nation rank, e.g. census order); terrflag; area +1, +0x0E+n
0x639e8.risks: Writes through caller stack pointers; the list has no bound check; meaning of 0xF06C0 G.

0x63af0.purpose: Counts ships to pay 2 each from treasury +0x3E while [0x110148] > 0 and treasury > 1 and (treasury < lim or treasury - 2 > lim), lim = (0xE1624 & 0x20) ? 8 : 18; each takes one from 0x110148.

0x63b7c.purpose: v = treasury - 2*[0x11014C]; if slots remain and n has some territory (records 1..157) with >= 2 tokens and v > 0 (the lim test is always true then): returns 1 and takes a slot; else 0.
0x63b7c.risks: Single if, not a loop (at most 1).

0x63c6c.purpose: If slots remain and 0x11014C == 0 and 0x110150 == 0 and n has a territory with >= 3 tokens: returns 1 (takes a slot), else 0.

0x63d10.purpose: Returns 1 with the next combination in 0x110178 (count), 0x110174[] sites, 0x11016C[] treasury (2-type), 0x110170[] levy (type); 0 when done. Stage 0x110158: 0 = one ship (type 0 if treasury ships, else 1 or 2), 1 = pairs, 2 = triples; site indexes 0x11015C/0x110160/0x110164 enumerate i<j<k over 0x10F310, skipping excluded sites 0x10F220 (stage 0 does not check) and sites where n's tokens <= type. On a stage change: counters -1, 0x110168 = 2, stage++; entering stage 1: if byte 0xF488C[n] != 0, re-admit excluded sites with >1 token and int8 0xEED84[160n+t] >= 0 (and zero the matching option score), then f6332C(total); entering stage 2: exclude the first site of options 0x10F2E0..0x10F2F0. Stops when stage+1 > total.
0x63d10.risks: Stateful generator in globals across calls; three nearly identical nested enumerations; signed byte compares; translate as is (not as a clean combinations loop) to keep the order.

0x643c8.category: AI: gather tokens at planned city sites
0x643c8.purpose: If byte 0xF488C[n] == 1 return. f7A940, f7AA1C. For t 1..156 in play, coastal, tstate +2 bit 0x02 owned by n with movable tokens there: f48028(&cnt, buf, t, n, 15) reachable land, f48D44(&cnt, buf, n, t, 1); move up to 'movable' tokens one by one from listed territories with >1 tokens (f57CA4(s, t, n, 1, 1)), appending move records {s, t, 1, 0x10} to 0x107694/[0x1079B4]; record (t, moved) locally and word area[t+1]+0x39 = moved. None: f7AC60, f7AE14, f648C8(n, 0). Else f7A940, f7AA1C, f648C8(n, 0x10); differences against the stacked +0x39; if any: pop/peek both stacks, redo the gathering with the reduced need, f648C8(n, 0x10), drop both; else drop both stacks twice.
0x643c8.globals: 0xF488C; 0xEE16C in play; terrflag; tstate +0/+2; area +0x24+n (movable), +0x0E+n, +0x39 (int16); move list 0x107694/0x1079B4; World State Stack 0xF5240 copies; Move List Stack 0x112A1C..
0x643c8.calls: f7A940, f7AA1C, f48028, f48D44, f57CA4, f7AC60, f7AE14, f648C8, f7AF28, f7AFB8, f7AD24, f7AD7C
0x643c8.risks: Two parallel stacks (world state, move list) with branch-specific push/pop/peek/drop sequences; reads the stacked copy directly ([0xF5240 + 4*depth] + 69(r-1) + 0x37). Large stack buffers (0x2CC and 0x7CC). Loop starts at t = 1.

0x648c8.purpose: eax n, edx flags (0 or 0x10). If 0xF488C[n] == 1 return. For each ship k with full movement (+0x41+k == 4 + Clothmaking): t = ship territory; target = f64BB8(k, mp, n); if > 0: f58888(t, target, n, mp) (routes 0x108820), plan = f65010(n, flags); else -1. For the chosen 16-byte route: for j 0..5 (0xFF = none): delta int8 +8+j < 0: f57CE8(0xC803C[tj], n, 1, -d) and record {+0 tj, +2 -d, +3 k, +4 3 (embark), +5 6}; > 0: f57E28 and record {+1 tj, +2 d, +3 k, +4 4 (disembark), +5 6}; then a sail step to tj+1: record {+0 tj, +1 next, +3 k, +4 10, +5 6}, +0x41+k--, word +0x45+2k = next+1.
0x648c8.calls: f64BB8, f58888 (unported route builder), f65010, f57E28, f57CE8
0x648c8.risks: Move record fields differ by type (+0 vs +1 for the territory); keep exact byte offsets.

0x64bb8.purpose: eax k, edx mp, ebx n -> territory or -1. t = ship territory; f5861C(t, n, mp) (reach table int32 0x107EE4[160]); candidates u with reach 1, not land-adjacent to t (matrix 0xF95FC[157t+u]), empty and no city. For each: f58888(t, u, n, mp) routes; per route counts free landing territories (not marked, not terrflag 0xE163A bit 0x01, byte 0xF4234[160(n-1)+tt] == 0) vs n's loadable tokens; best by (landings, tokens) with int8 0xEED84[160n+u] > 0 to win outright; exact ties broken by the AI random table: int16 0x112A94[row 12 + (count++ % 8)][n] / 300 < 50.
0x64bb8.globals: 0x107EE4; 0xF95FC land matrix; area +1, +0x0E+n; tstate +2; terrflag; 0xF4234 [9][160]; 0xEED84 [..][160]; 0x112A94 AI random table (game_rand-made); routes 0x108820, count 0x109E00
0x64bb8.risks: Uses the precomputed random table, not game_rand (so the seed is not advanced here). Land matrix row t may be 157..159 (out of the 157x157 matrix) and u up to 159. 160-byte stack arrays reused per route.

0x65010.purpose: eax n, edx flags -> route index or -1. 0x10818C = max(.., route count); memset(0xF8418, -1, 160) keep-cache; f7A940, f7AA1C. Per route r (0x108820+16r): along its territories decide how many tokens to keep (f495C0 + f49790, cached in 0xF8418; 0xF3580 bit 0x80 and terrflag bit 0x04 rules; flags 0x10 uses area +0x39 needs at marked sites), embarkable tokens (min 5, min landing capacity of empty non-city territories = pop limit + Agriculture), embark passes (contested first, then over-limit, then any) with f57CE8 and backups of touched area records in a stack array (73-byte entries) and 0xF8194[t]; unload pass with f57E28 (from the last landing back); score int16 +0x0E = f7B044(n), or -300 if nothing to carry; restore backups. f7AC60, f7AE14. Sort routes by score: bubble if < 20 routes, else qsort(0x108820, n, 16, 0x65C4C) (descending int16 +0x0E). Ties on byte +6 and score: pick from int16 0x112AA6+2n of the AI random table. Returns pick if its score >= 0.
0x65010.globals: 0x108820 routes, 0x109E00, 0x10818C; 0xF8418[160]; 0xF8194[160]; 0xF3580; terrflag; tstate; area +1, +0x0E+n, +0x24+n, +0x39; nation +0x25, +0x27; 0x112A94 table; World State Stack top copy
0x65010.calls: memset, f7A940, f7AA1C, f495C0, f49790 (unported AI evaluators), f57CE8, f57E28, f7B044, f7AC60, f7AE14, qsort (comparator 0x65C4C)
0x65010.risks: qsort with a function pointer comparator (Watcom qsort's own order for equal keys must be reproduced, not libc qsort). Unload loop could spin if no landing accepts a token. 0x630-byte stack backup array of 73-byte records. Writes the stacked state copy directly.

0x65cb0.purpose: f7A940; simulates f5AAA4(0) and f5C238(0); occupied[] = territories of n's ships; for each ship k with moves left: f5861C reach, candidate territories reachable in 1 with n's marker and not AI-marked (tstate bit 0x02), sorted by n's tokens; target = best; if not the current: f58888 route, then sail records {+0 tj, +1 next, +3 k, +4 10, +5 0x2A}, moves--, word +0x45+2k updated. f7AC60 (state restored; the move list keeps the plan).
0x65cb0.globals: nation +0x40, +0x41, +0x45; 0x107EE4; area +1+n, +0x0E+n; tstate +2; routes 0x108820; move list 0x1079B8/0x107D3C
0x65cb0.calls: f7A940, f5AAA4, f5C238, memset, f5861C, f58888, f7AC60
0x65cb0.risks: f5AAA4(0)/f5C238(0) inside a push/pop still change globals outside the stack (0x109E24, 0xF547C, 0xF5934, button 7 redraw). game_rand cannot be reached because 0x5BA0C draws only when shown.

0x66050.purpose: Message area; int32 0x11017C[n] = 0; nation list; f783B8. If any nation has cities: background 3, f7876C, f3B05C, f459E4/f3D9FC(first), start = clock(). For n 1..9 in play with cities ([0xF40F8] = n): with Coinage (+0x2C): human (or PBEM local) f66488(n); computer: rate = f667B0(n), and if changed (not PBEM) '%s sets its Tax Rate to %d.' with 2000 ms. Tax = cities * rate (+0x3F; 2 without Coinage); stock >= tax: treasury += tax, stock -= tax; else revolt flag 0x11017C[n] = 1. Revolts: Democracy (+0x34): 'Democrary spares %s from a Tax Revolt.' 3000 ms; else f7844C, f6685C(n, cities - stock/rate). Wait until start + 500/[0xBB3F4]/10 ticks. Nobody with cities: f79270(100, first, -200, '' (0xB892B), 0).
0x66050.calls: f783B8, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, f7876C, f3B05C, f459E4, f3CBBC, f3D9FC, clock, f667B0 (unported AI rate), f3A990, sprintf, f3A9F4, f78A20, f66488, f3A924, f7844C, f6685C (unported tax revolt)
0x66050.waits_for_input: human rate via f66488 (f78BA4); timed messages; final clock wait
0x66050.risks: Division by zero in stock/rate if rate is 0. Byte arithmetic on treasury/stock. Text slip 'Democrary'. The 'any cities' scan stops at the first nation with cities.

0x66488.category: UI: human sets the tax rate
0x66488.purpose: int32 0xFFD40 = -50 (help state); [0xF40F8] = n; f7844C. PBEM non-local: return. Background 3, f7876C. max = min(stock / cities, 3). max == 0: '%s, a tax revolt is unavoidable.\nThe tax rate has been set to 1 to minimize the effect.' (f3AB7C), rate = 1, 4000 ms. Else dialog 0xC817C, arrows (296,385)/(330,385), 'TAX' 'RATE', '%s, set your tax rate.'; v = min(rate, max); loop: box with v, f3CBBC, f78BA4(0xF596C, 0): -12 up to max, -11 down to 1, -1: rate = v, f78664(0xC817C).
0x66488.calls: f7844C, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, f7876C, f3A924, sprintf, f3AB7C, f3F670, f459E4, f3D9FC, f3B05C, f3CBBC, f78A20, f7853C, fg_vbopen, f3AF8C, fg_setcolor, f3A3A0, f3A044, fg_vbclose, f3A9F4, f3C9D0, itoa, f3A0B0, f78BA4, f78664
0x66488.waits_for_input: f78BA4(0xF596C, 0) until -1; 4000 ms in the forced case

0x667b0.purpose: AI tax-rate choice for nation n (eax). rec = 0xF14CC+199n; c = int8 +0x51 (cities, read as dword [rec+0x4E] sar 24), s = int8 +0x99 (tokens in stock, [rec+0x96] sar 24). If 2c > s: rate 1. Else rate 3 if turn int16 [0xF40FC] (dword [0xF40FA] sar 16) >= 9 and s >= 25 and c <= 6, otherwise 2; then while rate > 1 and c*rate > s: rate--. Returns rate in eax (signed compares throughout). No screen, no text.
0x667b0.risks: Unusual prologue (push 0x1C, __CHK, push ebx, push edx, push ebp). Fields read as dword..sar 24, so the byte is +3 from the displacement; keep signed int8 semantics.

0x6685c.purpose: Tax Revolt of nation n (eax) losing k cities (edx). Sets int32 [0xFFD40] = 2 (help topic 'taxrevlt'). Builds a local list of int16 pairs {nation, score} of the other nations m (1..9) with byte +0x9A != 0, m != n and dword [0x11017C+4m] == 0; score = 5*(9 - int8 +0x51) + int8 +0x99 (movsx 16-bit); bubble-sorts it descending by score (signed 16-bit). Message sprintf("%s suffers a Tax Revolt!", name[0xC768C+4n]) shown with 0x79270(-500 = wait for CONTINUE, n, -200 = home view, buf, 0), then f3A990, f3CBBC. Then for each listed m while k > 0: if m has < 9 cities: take = min(9 - cities(m), k); if m's +0x9A == 3 (human) and not PBEM (byte [0xE1624] & 0x80 clear): 0x2468C(m, n, take, 2) (ChooseCitiesToLoseToPirates reused: the human picks the annexed cities), else 0x66B54(m, n, take); k -= take. If k > 0 remains: "%s's revolting cities can no longer be absorbed by the other nations." via 0x79270(-500, n, -200, buf, 0), then human (+0x9A==3, not PBEM) 0x66D8C(n, k) else 0x66C2C(n, k). Finally x = cities(n) * int8 +0x3F (tax rate): byte +0x3E (treasury) += x, byte +0x99 (stock) -= x.
0x6685c.globals: writes [0xFFD40]=2; reads dword [0x11017C+4m] (written by 0x66050), [0xE1624]&0x80, nation +0x51,+0x99,+0x9A,+0x3F; writes nation +0x3E, +0x99; names 0xC768C; 204-byte stack text buffer [ebp-0xCC]
0x6685c.waits_for_input: yes: inside 0x79270(-500,...) twice (CONTINUE click via f78BA4(0xF596C,0), or 250/1000 ms when unattended f7BA64); indirectly in 0x2468C / 0x66D8C for humans
0x6685c.risks: Local pair array [ebp-0x68] read through misaligned dword..sar 16 ([ebp+4i-0x6A]); list sized for 9. Bubble sort compares int16. Byte arithmetic on treasury/stock may wrap (no clamp). PBEM branch (0x80 flag) changes who chooses.

0x66b54.purpose: Computer nation m (eax) annexes k (ebx) revolting cities of nation n (edx). Loop while k > 0: t = 0x20C70(m, n) - 1 (unported; G: AI pick of n's city territory, returns territory+1); f3F670, f3F624(t, 15) (highlight), f3DA60(t) (centre), f78A20(500); byte area[t+1] + 0x3B + n = 1 (0xE31F3 + 69(t+1) + n); 0x78F04(t, n) (remove n's city at t); 0x78E74(t, m) (give m a city at t); k--; sprintf("%s annexes a city in %s.", name[m], territory name [0xC77D8+4t]); 0x79270(2000 ms, n, t, buf, 0).
0x66b54.globals: writes area record +0x3B+n (G: per-nation 'lost by revolt' flag); via 0x78F04/0x78E74: 0xE2C18 territory state, nation city list +0x51/+0x52..; territory names 0xC77D8
0x66b54.calls: 0x20C70, f3F670, f3F624, f3DA60, f78A20, 0x78F04 (remove city), 0x78E74 (add city), sprintf, 0x79270
0x66b54.waits_for_input: no (timed: 500 ms + 2000 ms per city via 0x79270)
0x66b54.risks: If 0x20C70 finds no city it returns 0 -> t = -1 and area/TSTATE index -1 (no guard). 116-byte stack text buffer.

0x66c2c.purpose: Computer nation n (eax) removes k (edx) of its own cities that nobody could absorb. Two passes j = 0, 1; in each, i runs from cities-1 down to 0 while k > 0: t1 = byte rec+0x52+i (territory+1); found = (t1-1 is one of the four int32 at 0xC0618 + 16n + 4q, q 0..3; G: the nation's home/start territories); a city is removed only when found == (j != 0), so pass 0 removes the cities outside that list first. Removal: f3F670, f3F624(t1-1, 15), f3DA60(t1-1), f78A20(500), 0x78F04(t1-1, n), k--, sprintf("%s removes a city in %s", name[n], [0xC77D4+4*t1]), 0x79270(2500, n, t1-1, buf, 0).
0x66c2c.risks: Inner loop computes edx (rec+i) before the q<4 test and reuses it after (fine, but keep the same index). Text lacks the final period (other message has one).

0x66d8c.purpose: ChooseMultipleCitiesToRemove: human nation n (eax) removes k (edx) cities. Snapshots for RESTART: heap blocks via 0x822B5: [0xEED74] = 0x2B65 bytes (area records 0..160), [0xEED7C] = 0x1E0 (0xE2C18 territory states), [0xEED78] = 0x954 (nation records 1..11 at their offsets). Debug name to no-op logger 0x78B0C. Screen: f3CD6C(3), [0xEE168]=3, full fg_vbcopy background->back; sprites 0xF51AC (0xFB,0x195) and 0xF51B4 (0x178,0x195); "LEFT TO" right-aligned at (0x12F,0x185), "REMOVE" at (0x150,0x185); f3AB7C("%s, select cities to be removed"); f7876C; dialog 0xC8568 (arrows 0x39/0x3A, RESTART 0x41, REMOVE 0x3F, FINISHED 0x2A) appended to 0xF596C (f7853C), f3B05C; choice list by 0x28CFC(n, 2, 0) into 0xF7CA0/[0xF7C9C]. Loop: box (0x109,0x195,0x6E,0x13) with the selected territory name, box (0x136,0x181) with the number left (itoa); highlight; FINISHED enabled only when left <= 0, REMOVE only when left > 0; on change f459E4(n) and f3DA60(sel) (or f3D52C(0,0) if the list is empty); r = f78BA4(0xF596C, 1): -100 loop; r >= 0 (map click on a listed territory) select; -9/-0xA prev/next; -0x65 (REMOVE): 0x78F04(list[sel], n), left--, then the entry is deleted from 0xF7CA0, count--, f79A9C(&sel), 0x28CFC(n,2,0); -0x63 (RESTART): "Restart %s Tax Revolt?" (adjective table 0xC76C4) confirmed through 0x795A8 (== -0x61) when option bit 0xF097C&0x08 is set, then copies the three snapshots back, left = k, list rebuilt; -1 (FINISHED) exits: f78664(0xC8568), free the three blocks and zero their pointers.
0x66d8c.globals: heap fields [0xEED74],[0xEED78],[0xEED7C]; areas 0xE31B8, 0xE2C18, nations 1..11; choice list 0xF7CA0/[0xF7C9C]; dialogs 0xC8568, 0xF596C; [0xEE168]; options [0xF097C]
0x66d8c.calls: malloc 0x822B5, 0x78B0C, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, fg_vbopen, f3AF8C, fg_setcolor, f3A3A0, f3A044, fg_vbclose, sprintf, f3AB7C, f7876C, f7853C, f3B05C, 0x28CFC, f3C9D0, f3A0B0, itoa, f3F670, f3F624, f3C3D0, f3C314, f459E4, f3DA60, f3D52C, f3CBBC, f78BA4, 0x78F04, 0x795A8 (yes/no box), f79A9C, f78664, free
0x66d8c.waits_for_input: yes: f78BA4(0xF596C, map=1) click loop (buttons and map territories); 0x795A8 yes/no for restart
0x66d8c.risks: 0x822B5 called with edx/ebx (tag, caller name) left over from other code (uninitialised tags). Heap pointers stored in 32-bit data fields (port handles). If k exceeds the cities left, REMOVE stays enabled with an empty list and reads 0xF7CA0[0] stale. 248-byte stack text buffer; restart copies must use the same 69-byte/3-byte/199-byte strides.

0x673a8.purpose: POPULATION EXPANSION phase driver. Message area 0xBB3FA..0xBB400 = (0xA9,0x154,0x12C,0x23); player list int16 [0xF06AE] count + [0xF06B0..] of nations with +0x9A != 0; f783B8(0xF596C, [0xF5940]); screen f3CD6C(3), background->back, f7876C, f3B05C(0xF596C), f459E4(first), f3CBBC, f3D9FC(first); start = clock(). For n = 1..9: [0xF40F8] = n, byte [0xF488C+n] = 0; handled if (not PBEM and +0x9A != 0) or (PBEM and n == byte [0xE1622]). need = sum over n's area list (count int8 +0x60, area indexes +0x61..) of min(tokens,2) with tokens = int8 area+0x0E+n. If stock (+0x99) >= need: automatic: for each area: tokens 1 -> 2, 2 -> 4 (marker area+1+n = n written), > 2 -> +2; +0x98 (on board) += added, +0x99 -= added. Else: f7844C(0xF596C,[0xF5940]); if stock <= 0: "%s, you have no stock for expansion." via 0x79270(-500, n, -200, ...); elif +0x9A == 3: 0x67758(n) (ManualPopExpansion); elif +0x9A == 2: 0x680DC(n, need). After the loop: PBEM -> byte [0xF40FE] = 1; then busy-wait until clock() >= start + (1000/[0xBB3F4])/10 (inline copy of f78A20(1000), unsigned compare).
0x673a8.calls: f783B8, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, f7876C, f3B05C, f459E4, f3CBBC, f3D9FC, clock, 0x7844C (highlight current nation's player button), sprintf, 0x79270, 0x67758, 0x680DC
0x673a8.waits_for_input: only through callees (0x79270 CONTINUE, ManualPopExpansion); own final 1 s busy wait
0x673a8.risks: Area tokens read as dword [0xE31C3 + 69a + n] sar 24 with n from [0xF40F8] (a global, not the loop variable). Token bytes can exceed 127 only theoretically. PBEM branch. Inline clock wait not via f78A20 (keep the /C divisor).

0x67758.purpose: ManualPopExpansion: human nation n (eax) without enough stock places tokens by hand. word [0xBB400] = 0x15 (restored to 0x23 at exit). Snapshots areas/territory states/nations as 0x66D8C. Allowance per area t 1..160: byte area+0x24+n = 0 if n has no tokens there, 1 if one token, 2 if more (recomputed on restart). Screen: background, sprites 0xF51AC/0xF51B4 at y 0x186, "LEFT IN" / "STOCK" at y 0x176, f3A9F4("%s, you have insufficient stock for full expansion. Choose territories to be expanded."), f7876C, dialog 0xC8954 (arrows, DISTRIBUTE ALL 0xDB, ADD ONE 0xDC, ADD MAX 0xDD, RESTART 0x41, FINISHED 0x2A) appended to 0xF596C, f7844C, list 0x28CFC(n, 3, 0). Loop draws the selected territory name and the stock count; 0xDB/0xDC/0xDD enabled while stock > 0, FINISHED only when stock == 0. r = f78BA4(0xF596C, 1): >= 0 select; -9/-0xA prev/next; -0x77 ADD ONE: tokens+1, allowance-1, stock-1, board+1, entry removed when allowance hits 0; -0x78 ADD MAX: same until stock or allowance is 0, entry removed; -0x76 DISTRIBUTE ALL: round-robin one token per listed area until stock is 0 (then the selected entry is removed); -0x63 RESTART ("Restart %s Population Expansion?", 0x795A8 if 0xF097C&0x08): snapshots back, allowances recomputed, list rebuilt; -1 exits (f78664(0xC8954), free blocks).
0x67758.globals: [0xBB400]; heap [0xEED74],[0xEED78],[0xEED7C]; area +0x0E+n tokens, +0x24+n allowance; nation +0x98, +0x99; 0xF7CA0/[0xF7C9C]; dialogs 0xC8954, 0xF596C; [0xF097C]
0x67758.calls: 0x822B5, 0x78B0C, f3CD6C, fg_vbcopy, fg_vbopen, f3AF8C, fg_setcolor, f3A3A0, f3A044, fg_vbclose, sprintf, f3A9F4, f7876C, f7853C, f3B05C, 0x7844C, 0x28CFC, f3C9D0, f3A0B0, itoa, f3F670, f3F624, f3C3D0, f3C314, f459E4, f3DA60, f3D52C, f3CBBC, f78BA4, 0x795A8, f79A9C, f78664, free
0x67758.waits_for_input: yes: f78BA4(0xF596C, 1) loop (buttons + map clicks), 0x795A8 confirmation
0x67758.risks: DISTRIBUTE ALL loops forever if stock > 0 while every listed allowance is 0 (only safe because stock < need on entry and the list matches the area list). Loop counter for the allowance init is taken from edx after the no-op 0x78B0C (relies on edx preserved). ebx=0x23 set before f78664 and stored after (callee-saved). Uninitialised malloc tags as 0x66D8C.

0x680dc.purpose: Computer nation n (eax) with need (edx) > stock chooses where to place its tokens. f7A8D0 (WSS alloc); "%s cannot fully populate and is considering where to place its tokens." via 0x79270(-550 = no wait, n, -200, ...); start = clock(). Stock 0: byte [0xF488C+n] = 1, done. If 100*stock/need < 80: [0xF488C+n] = 1 (G: short-of-stock flag read by 0x6DE04). alloc int32[160] (stack, memset 0x280). f7A940 (WSS push), then simulates full expansion on the board (1 token +1, >=2 tokens +2, +0x98 updated, alloc[t] += added); excess = added - stock. 0x461BC(n) and 0x5AAA4(0) (G: AI evaluation and conflict resolution on the simulated board). Cuts: per area of n's list not flagged 0xE2C18[t].+2 & 2, if tokens > 0x78D08(t, n) (population limit, +1 with Agriculture) cut = 1 (setg, not the difference) while excess and alloc; then entries of the table 0x107694 ([0x1079B4] dwords: byte0 territory <= 0xA0, byte2 amount, byte3 type) of type 7, then type 0x11; then areas with bit 8, then bit 7, of int16 0xF3580[(n-1)*157 + t]. f7AC60 (WSS pop, board restored). If excess remains: list 0xF7CA0 = n's areas-1, 0x48D44(0xF7C9C, 0xF7CA0, n, 0, 1) (G: rank), round-robin decrement of alloc. Finally for t 0..159 with alloc[t] > 0 and stock > 0: f57E28(t, n, alloc[t]), +0x98 += alloc, +0x99 -= alloc. f7ABD0 (WSS free). Busy-wait until clock() >= start + 1000/10 (not scaled by [0xBB3F4]).
0x680dc.calls: f7A8D0, sprintf, 0x79270, clock, memset 0x7D5D0, f7A940, 0x461BC, 0x5AAA4, 0x78D08, f7AC60, 0x48D44, f57E28, f7ABD0
0x680dc.waits_for_input: no (fixed 1 s clock wait, unscaled by /C)
0x680dc.risks: alloc indexed by byte0 of 0x107694 entries up to 160 -> alloc[160] writes past the 160-int array into the text buffer. setg gives a cut of 1 per area (likely meant tokens - limit; keep for --original). The list loop after 0x5AAA4 uses n's (possibly changed) area list inside the WSS window. Round-robin can spin if all alloc are 0 with excess > 0. Callees 0x461BC/0x5AAA4 run on a simulated board inside WSS push/pop: any random draws there would not be undone (seed not in the WSS).

0x68730.purpose: AI nation n (eax) declares its trade offer: 0x68FDC(n) (worst tradable calamity held), 0x68788(n) (ranked hand), 0x68B44(n) (wanted cards); if [0x1105AC+4n] (number of wanted cards) != 0: 0x68C90(n) builds the offer, else byte +0x9C (offer slot 0) = 0.
0x68730.callers: 0x6F270 (DECLARE OFFERS, computer nations with >= max(min goods, 6) cards)
0x68730.risks: game_rand only through 0x68C90 (and 0x6937C, f76F70 inside it).

0x68788.purpose: Builds AI nation n's ranked list of held commodities. 0x68A64(n, byte +0xBB) fills 0x1105A0[0..8]. If int16 [0xF5476] (session) == 1: for card i 18..1 held by n: skip if [0xF590C+4n] >= 7 and stack (i-1)/2 >= 7; s = (i-1)/2; if s-1 <= cities: [0x1105D4+4n] = s, stop (G: highest stack worth asking for). Then memset(0x1101AC, 0, 0x120), [0x1103EC] = 0 (count), [0x1103F0] = 0; for i 18..1 with c = int8 rec+i != 0 and 0x1105A0[(i-1)/2] != 0: entry e (16 bytes at 0x1101AC+16e): +0 id i, +8 c; Mining check: i in 0xBDD3C[1..5] {4,12,11,16,18}; value +4: i 1/2: c*c*((i+1)>>1); with Mining (+0x29) and listed: (c+2)^2*((i+1)>>1), +0xC = c+1; else (c+1)^2*((i+1)>>1), +0xC = c. Bubble sort descending by +4.
0x68788.globals: writes 0x1101AC table (18 x 16 bytes), [0x1103EC], [0x1103F0], [0x1105D4+4n]; reads 0x1105A0, [0xF5476], [0xF590C+4n], nation cards +1..+0x12, +0x29, +0x51, 0xBDD3C
0x68788.risks: Mining flag [ebp-0x24] is reset only when an entry is added; inner search reads 0xBDD3C via dword sar 24. Values computed in 32-bit; the 16-byte records are swapped with movsd (keep layout).

0x68a64.purpose: memset(0x1105A0, 0, 9); for every other nation m (1..9, +0x9A != 0, m != n=eax) and every card i 18..1 m holds: unless [0xF590C+4m] is not -1 and >= 7 and stack (i-1)/2 >= 7, memset(0x1105A0, 1, s+1) with s = (i-1)/2. So 0x1105A0[s] = 1 when some other nation holds a card of stack >= s. Second argument edx (byte +0xBB from callers) is stored and never used.
0x68a64.risks: Unused parameter; keep the call signature.

0x68b44.purpose: Chooses how many and which cards AI nation n (eax) asks for. K = int32 0xC8DA0[[0x1103EC]] (table {5,0,1,1,1,2,3,3,4,4,4,5,..}); memset(rec+0x9C+5, 0, 5) (offset byte 0xCA9A2). If count < 8: sum of +8 over entries K..count-1, +1 if [0x110600] < 0; if sum < 3: K--. Cap K at 3 if [0x110600] < -1 or f7CAB4(n) != 0 (no negative relation in 0xF52E0) or int16 [0x112C98+2n]/300 < 25. [0x1105AC+4n] = K; if K: offer slots rec+0x9C+5+j = entry j's card id for j < K; [0x11059C] = K.
0x68b44.risks: int16 0x112C98 has no direct writer in the code (G: always 0 unless filled by a block copy). Offsets into the offer come from bytes of the 0xCA99C.. constant table read as dword sar 24: read them from obj2.

0x68c90.purpose: Builds AI nation n's declared offer at rec+0x9C (13 bytes; slots: 0..1 true cards, 2 stated third card, 5..9 wanted, 10 actual third card; offsets from bytes 0xCA9A1/0xCA9AD/0xCA9AF). r = game_rand()*100>>15; truth = (byte +0xBC == 1) ? r >= 66 : r < 66. [0x1106B0+4n] = 0. If [0x110600] >= 0 (no bad calamity): m = 3, and if int16 [0xF5476] == (byte [0xE1623] & 0xF) (last session): second game_rand, if r2 < 80 - 20*AI level (bits 2-3 of byte 0xE1625) then [0x1106B0+4n] = 1. Else m = 2, truth = 0. Fills from the ranked list starting at entry [0x11059C]: card ids written at slot j++ while m > 0; after slot 1 j jumps to 10, and without truth and with no calamity slot 10 gets the lowest entry's id (0x11019C+16*count) and m drops twice. If slot 10 is empty: flag = 1, slot 10 = calamity id [0x110604]. 0x6937C(n, &truth, 1, 0, flag). If K > 1: f76F70(K, rec+0x9C+5) shuffles the wanted cards. If !flag and truth: sorts {slot0, slot1, slot10} descending and writes slot0, slot1, slot10 and slot 2 = smallest.
0x68c90.risks: 1 game_rand always, a 2nd in the last session when no bad calamity, K more inside f76F70 when K > 1, plus those of 0x6937C: order must be exact. Constant offsets read unaligned from 0xCA99C..; the word [0xE1624]<<4>>14 bit extraction. Writes past slot 10 possible when j continues (slot 11, 12) — keep byte-exact.

0x68fdc.purpose: [0x110600] = 0, [0x110604] = 0; for each calamity card held by nation n (count byte +0x13, ids +0x14..): v = 0x690AC(id, n); if v < [0x110600]: [0x110604] = id, [0x110600] = v. Leaves the most harmful calamity (score < 0) and its id.
0x68fdc.risks: Followed in the binary by the 12-entry jump table of 0x690AC (0x6907C..0x690AB) inside the code object.

0x690ac.purpose: Harm score (<= 0) of calamity card c (eax) for nation n (edx), switch through the jump table at 0x6907C for c 0x13..0x1E (default 0). 0x13 Volcano 0; 0x14 Treachery -5; 0x15 Famine 0; 0x16 Superstition -1 with Enlightenment (+0x39), else -5 with Deism (+0x38), -10 with Mysticism (+0x37), else -15; 0x17 Civil War 0; 0x18 Slave Revolt -15, -5 more with Mining (+0x29), +5 with Enlightenment; 0x19 Flood 0; 0x1A Barbarian Hordes -12; 0x1B Epidemic -16, +8 Medicine (+0x2D), -5 Roadbuilding (+0x28); 0x1C Civil Disorder v = cities-3, -1 each for Music, Drama&Poetry, Law, Democracy (+0x30,+0x2F,+0x33,+0x34), +1 Roadbuilding, Military (+0x28,+0x35), v>=0, result -5v or -1 if 0; 0x1D Iconoclasm v = 4 -Law -Philosophy (+0x36) -3*Theology (+0x3B) +Monotheism (+0x3A) +Roadbuilding, same -5v/-1; 0x1E Piracy -10.
0x690ac.risks: Jump table (12 dwords in the code object, fixups). Several cases share targets (0x69133 is also the tail of case 0x16, 0x69154 of case 0x16 and 0x1E). Unusual prologue.

0x6937c.purpose: Chooses the stated (possibly bluffed) third card. Args: n (eax), int *truth (edx), count (ebx), k (ecx, candidate index into 0x110400), flag (stack). If *truth: in DECLARE OFFERS (byte [0xF4102] == 0xC) slot 2 = slot 10 and return; in counter offers the record 0x111118+16*int16[0x112548]: if its +5 byte is 1 or 2, *truth = 0 and continue, else +2 = +5 and return. Otherwise top = highest s with 0x1105A0[s] (capped by [0x1105D4+4n]), id range 2*top+2 down to 1; for j < count: a = (counter phase and [0x110408+28k] >= 0); r = game_rand()*100>>15 >= 66; candidate id is rejected if it is one of n's wanted cards (declare phase), or (counter phase, a) the partner m=[0x110400+28k] does not want it, or (r) it equals one of the two true cards, or (counter phase) it is one of m's three offered cards; fallbacks restart the scan without each restriction when it reaches 1. The chosen id goes to slot 2 (declare) or record +2+j (counter). If flag == 0 and the stated card's stack is lower than the actual third card's, recursive call 0x6937C(n, &one, 1, k, 0) (states the truth).
0x6937c.globals: nation +0x9C..; 0x111118 records / int16 [0x112548]; 0x110400 candidate table (28-byte records); 0x1105A0, [0x1105D4+4n], [0x1105AC+4n]; byte [0xF4102] (phase); offset bytes 0xCA9AC..0xCA9B0
0x6937c.risks: One game_rand per j iteration (callers pass count 1 or [0x1103F8+28k]-2) plus the recursive call's. Recursion. Uninitialised local [ebp-0x3C] if count <= 0. ret 4 (one stack arg). Dense flag interplay: translate branch by branch.

0x698a4.purpose: AI nation n (eax) evaluates every declared offer and makes counter offers. Returns at once if [0x1105AC+4n] == 0. 0x68FDC, 0x68788, K as in 0x68B44 (cap 3), [0x11059C] = K. Copies the [0x112560] declared-offer records (21 bytes) from 0x110ECC to 0x110608; 0x6AD70(n, 0) clears impossible cards. For each offer i of another nation m (record +0x12): candidate k at 0x1103F4+28k: +0 matches (offered cards n wants), +4 = 3, +8 = f6DD98(0) - f6DD98(n) with the three cards added to scratch nation record 0 (copy of n), +0x18 expected value (average of f195D8(0)-f195D8(n) leaving out each card in turn, or only slot 2 if byte 0xE1625 & 0x20), value = expected + (gain - expected)*trust/100 with trust = int8 n+0xB1+m clamped 0..100, +0xC m, +0x10 i. Sorts candidates by +8 then by +0 descending. For each candidate: [0x1105FC] = 0x6B928(n, m); threshold from the average value (>= 0xC8D40[AI level]), calamity, relation bytes n+0xA8+m and n+0xBD+m (x30), m's calamity harm (0x690AC on slot 10), leader [0xF52D4] (-3/20), human partner, +500 if 0x1105D4[n] < lowest stack m wants; if value > threshold: 0x6A5FC(n, k, &out, c < -1) builds a counter record; if its first card != 0 and the re-evaluated gain passes, record +0xD = m, +0xE = n, int16 [0x112548]++. If out and more than 3 were added: keeps the 3 best by int32 0xF52E0[n][m] (via a stack copy of all records) and compacts.
0x698a4.globals: 0x110ECC/[0x112560] declared offers, 0x110608 copy, 0x1103F4 candidates (28 bytes) /[0x1104B8], 0x111118 counter records /int16 [0x112548], [0x1105FC], [0x110600], nation record 0 (scratch), nation +0x9C.., +0xA8+m, +0xB1+m, +0xBD+m, 0xC8D40, 0xC8DA0, 0xF52E0, [0xF52D4], byte 0xE1625
0x698a4.risks: Overwrites nation record 0 as a scratch hand repeatedly (must match byte for byte at the end). Stack buffer [ebp-0x5EC] receives 16*[0x112548] bytes: room for 56 records only (overflow if more). repne movsd/movsb used as rep. Long arithmetic chain with signed idiv by 20/100/300; game_rand only through 0x6A5FC/0x6937C. 0x6B928 indexes the score history transposed (see 0x6B928).

0x6a5fc.purpose: Fills counter-offer record R = 0x111118+16*int16[0x112548] (memset 8) for AI n (eax) and candidate k (edx; partner m = [0x110400+28k]); *out (ebx) = 0; m3 = 3; if [0x110600] < -1 or c (ecx): m3 = 2, *out = 1 (include the calamity). matches = n's ranked entries that m wants (m+0x9C+5..). r = game_rand()*100>>15; truth = (byte n+0xBC == 1) ? r >= 75 : r < 75; *out forces truth 0. Returns if matches + !truth == 0. Pass 1: entries from [0x11059C] that m wants, pass 2: entries m neither wants nor offered (m+0x9C+0..2); card ids to R[j++] (j 2 -> 5), lowest card at R[5] without truth; if m3 still > 0: R[0] = 0, return. If *out: R[j++] = [0x110604]. 0x6937C(n, &truth, [0x1103F8+28k]-2, k, *out). If none of R[0..4] is wanted by m: R[0] = 0. If !*out and truth: sorts R[0], R[1], R[5] by score (id, doubled when m wants it) and writes R[0], R[1], R[5] and R[2] = R[5].
0x6a5fc.globals: 0x111118 / int16 [0x112548]; 0x110400 candidates; 0x1101AC ranked list, [0x1103EC], [0x11059C]; [0x110600]/[0x110604]; nation +0x9C.., +0xBC; offset bytes 0xCA99F.., 0xCA9AA..0xCA9B0
0x6a5fc.risks: Packed 5-byte stack records {u8 card; int32 score} read through misaligned dword..sar 24 ([ebp-0x73+5q]). One game_rand + 0x6937C's. Relies on exact offsets from the 0xCA99C.. byte table.

0x6ad70.purpose: Removes impossible cards from the copied declared offers 0x110608 (21-byte records, count [0x112560]) as seen by AI n (eax). For each nation m in play: 0x68A64(m, byte n+0xBB) and keeps 0x1105A0[0..8] in a local [10][9] table. held_all[i] = (n's count of card i == int32 0xC8D58[i], the stack's card count for i). For each offer slot q < 5 with card c: offering nation m = record +0x12; slot cleared if local[m][(c-1)/2] == 0 or held_all[c].
0x6ad70.risks: Clears calamity ids too if their (c-1)/2 >= 9 (index past the 9-entry row into the next nation's row). Unused 2nd arg to 0x68A64.

0x6af34.purpose: Same filter as 0x6AD70 for the counter offers addressed to AI n (eax): reads the 20-byte records at 0x111498 (count int16 [0x112568], cards +0..+4, nation +0xE) but clears the slot in the 21-byte table 0x110608 (index 21i+q).
0x6af34.risks: BUG(1995) candidate (G): reads one table and clears another with a different stride, so the filter has no effect on 0x111498 and corrupts 0x110608 slots; keep for --original.

0x6b0ec.purpose: AI nation n (eax) answers the counter offers made to it (0x111498, 20-byte records, count int16 [0x112568]). hascal = slot 10 (n+0xA6) >= 0x13. 0x68FDC(n), 0x6AF34(n). Stack copy of n's record minus its three offered cards (slots 0, 1, 10, decremented without checks); f194E4(n). Per record i: matches with n's wanted cards; scratch record 0 = copy + the three offered cards: 0x1104BC+28i = f195D8(0)-f195D8(n); expected via leaving out each card (or slot 2 with byte 0xE1625&0x20); 0x1104C0 = expected + diff*trust/100 (trust n+0xB1+record+0xD); if hascal: += max(0, 0x6B928(n, [0x1104C8+28i]))/2; 0x1104C4 = i, 0x1104C8 = record +0xE, 0x1104D4 = matches. Threshold per record (avg >= 0xC8D4C[level], calamity, [0x1106B0+4n]*40/20, relations n+0xA8+m, n+0xBD+m, harm of slot 10 for m, leader [0xF52D4], human partner); 0x1104CC = value - threshold; sort descending; the first record with >= 0 is accepted: 0x75074(record index).
0x6b0ec.globals: 0x111498 / int16 [0x112568]; 0x1104BC.. table (28-byte records); nation +0x9C, +0x9D, +0xA6, +0xA8+m, +0xB1+m, +0xBD+m; record 0 scratch; [0x110600], [0x1105FC], [0x1106B0+4n], [0xF52D4], 0xC8D4C, byte 0xE1625
0x6b0ec.risks: Uninitialised read: 0x6B928 is called with [0x1104C8+28i] before that field is written for i (stale from an earlier call, or BSS 0). Decrementing card counts of slot ids 0 hits byte 0 of the copy. Accepts at most one counter offer.

0x6b928.purpose: Score gap: a = int16 [0xEE9F0 + 90*(turn-1) + 2*x] for x = eax and edx (turn = int16 [0xF40FC]); returns 0 if score(eax) > score(edx), else (score(edx) - score(eax))/50.
0x6b928.risks: Index is [turn-1][nation] while f136B0 writes [nation][turn] (90-byte rows per nation): transposed (G: BUG(1995)); for turn > 10 it reads past the 0x384-byte table. Unusual prologue.

0x6bd98.purpose: DrawTradingCards. Nations in play ordered by cities ascending (ties by number) into 0xF06B0 (count = [0xF40EC]); if no nation has cities: 0x79270(100, first, -200, "" (0xB8BF4), 0) and return. 0x553C0 (music). PBEM: snapshots stacks (0xF06D0, 0xE1 bytes -> [0xEED80]) and nations (0x7C6 bytes -> [0xEED78]). f783B8(0x1106D8, [0xF5960]); hand sizes byte [0x110AD0+p] = f76F14; [0x110AC4] = 1 + bit 6 of 0xE1624 (cards per stack); [0xEE168] = 10 (+1 with 8 players); 0x6CB8C. Per nation in order: byte +0x3C = 0, [0xF40F8] = n, [0xF590C+4n] = -1. No cities: just its row. Human (or PBEM local): disable 0x8B, 0x2A (0x3C530), 0x6CF50, 0x6CDA0(p), title with the name, 0x6FFC4, 0x6D010 (hand face down at x 7 or 0xD1, y 0x196, w 0x1F4/0x172), 0x6FBDC(n,1) (REVEAL GOODS), enable 0x8A, 0x6D0C4 (face up), 0x6FE68 POINTS, [0x110ACC]=0, PBEM session-1 9-city case 0x6E158; loop r = f78BA4(0x1106D8, 0): -0x32 0x6D178 (acquire), -0x33 0x6D564 (buy), -1 FINISHED: draws the row counters (acquired [0x110AC8], bought [0x110ACC], hand). Computer: f3C940([0xF8E78]), 0x6DBAC (acquire face down), 0x6D010, f78A20(1500); not PBEM: repeat 0x6DE04(n) while it buys and treasury >= 6; PBEM: pre-declared -0x61 buys from stack 8 (-18 treasury, +18 stock) or shows '0'/'?' placeholders; f3C8C4. End: 0x6CDA0(-1); PBEM without local human: waits for FINISHED; PBEM with int16 [0xF5478]: restores stacks and nations (keeping +0x3C), frees blocks.
0x6bd98.globals: 0xF06AE/0xF06B0, [0xF40EC], [0xF40F8], 0xF590C[n], 0x110AC4, 0x110AC8, 0x110ACC, 0x110AD0[], [0xEE168], dialog 0x1106D8 (built by 0x7784C at load), [0xF8E78], heap [0xEED78]/[0xEED80], int16 [0xF5476], [0xF5478], int16 [0xF0684+2n] (PBEM buy codes), stacks 0xF06D0, nation +0x3C,+0x3E,+0x51,+0x99,+0x9A

0x6de04.purpose: Computer nation n (eax) decides whether to buy a card; returns (s<<8)+1 if it bought from stack s-1 (1-based s), else 0. Buy variant (byte [0xE1624] & 0x20): cities <= 3 and treasury >= 6: s = 3 if it holds >= 2 of card 6 or 5, 2 for cards 4/3, 1 for cards 2/1; else cities <= 5 and treasury >= 10: s = 5 (cards 10/9), 4 (8/7); else treasury >= 18 and stock < 18: s = 6..9 for pairs 12/11, 14/13, 16/15, 18/17; s = 0 if stack s-1 is empty. Without variant: if treasury >= 18: f194E4(n); s = 9 if stock < 2*cities; else if byte [0xF488C+n]: s = 9 when 0x17EDC(n,-1,0) == 0, or when a second identical call != 0 and the hand (f76F14) <= 8; else s = 9 if it holds no Gold (card 18) or no Ivory (17) ... precisely: Gold >= 1 and Ivory >= 1 -> 9; else 9 if cities == 9 and stock < 25. Purchase if s > 0 and treasury >= 2s: card = 0x76E50(s-1, n); then [0xF590C+4n] = s-1, treasury -= 2s, stock += 2s.
0x6de04.risks: Card counts read as dword [rec+k] sar 24 (byte rec+k+3) mixed with movsx bytes: map each to the right card id. With s == 0 the emptiness test reads stack index -1 (0xF06B5..). Two identical 0x17EDC calls (keep both: side effects?).

Waits for FINISHED (f78BA4(0x110ADC,0) until -1) or unattended 250/1000 ms.

0x70074.purpose: Puts card c (al) into the first empty slot of the current group k = int32 [0x112558] and draws it. Mode int32 [0x110EC8] == 1 (counter-offer): the slots are the bytes of row int16 [0x112548] of the counter-offer table 0x111118 (16-byte rows), from start2[k] for count[k]; mode 0 (own offer of nation edx): the bytes nation +0x9C+start1[k].. (0xF1568 + 199n + 3). The first slot holding 0 gets c; cardtiny c (0xF4C1C + 8c) is drawn at the slot's (x, y) (int16 0x111524 + 8s, 0x111526 + 8s) into the back buffer [0xF52C8], then again on the screen with the mouse hidden. Returns 1 if placed, 0 if the group is full.

0x70294.purpose: Clears the current group k = [0x112558] of the offer being composed (code -0x25 and the clear-all loop of 0x7109C) and redraws its empty slots. For each slot of the group: byte = 0; then f71D30(slot) (background -> back buffer), the empty-slot card cardtiny 32 + (edx == 1) (0xF4D1C, or 0xF4D24 highlighted) on the back buffer, f71E34(slot) (to the screen) and the card again on the screen with the mouse hidden. When k == 1 (bluff) it also clears the bluff-replacement slot: mode 1 group 4 (row byte +5), mode 0 group 3 (nation +0xA6), drawn with plain cardtiny 32. Finally nation n (eax) is copied over record 0 (0xF14CC, 199 bytes) and f707A0(n) rebuilds the scratch hand.

0x70984.purpose: Removes card c (eax) from nation record 0 (the scratch hand): c <= 18 decrements commodity count +c; a calamity is searched in +0x14.. (count +0x13), the lists +0x14 (ids) and +0x1C (who gave it) are shifted down over it, the count decremented and the freed last entries set to 0 / 0xFF. Same body as 0x75CA8 fixed to record 0.

0x70a6c.purpose: Switches the current slot group of the offer composer. New group k' = -0x11 - code (codes -0x11..-0x15 -> 0..4), kept in [0x112554]; nothing happens if k' == [0x112558]. Mode 0 calls f6FA54, mode 1 f6FB2C (G: erase the old heading); the empty slots of the old group are redrawn plain (cardtiny 32, 0xF4D1C) and those of the new group highlighted (cardtiny 33, 0xF4D24); [0x112558] = k'. Then mode 0 (own offer, dialog 0x111594) through a jump table: -0x11 'Truly stated' above slot 0, -0x12 'Bluff' above slot 2, -0x13 'You want to trade for...' at (0x92, 0xBC), -0x14 'Replace your bluffs with...' at (0x181, 0x6C); mode 1 (counter-offer, dialog 0x111D6C) by compares: -0x11 'Truly stated', -0x12 'Bluff', -0x15 'Replace your bluffs with...' above slot 5. Each case: f707A0(n), buttons 0x75/0x76 enabled/disabled as a pair (f3C314/f3C3D0), f6F95C(0 or 1), colour 15, the heading (f3A044); every path ends with fg_vbclose and f3CC14.

Then auto-advance: group 0 full -> -0x12 (Bluff); group 3 -> f6FDC8 and, if slot +0xA6 is filled, -0x13 (want); else f6FDC8 redraws. -0x1C: a click in the commodity chart at x 0x235 (two columns 40 px apart, rows 47 px from y 0x18): card 2*row + column; placed directly in the want group (k % 3 == 2), or in other groups only while (filled bluff slots + 2) < f76F14(n); a filled bluff slot advances to -0x14 (mode 0) or -0x15 (mode 1).

0x71768.purpose: Checks the offer when DONE (-1) is clicked. Mode 0 (own offer, nation n +0x9C slots): a = filled truthful slots (must be 2), b = filled bluff slots, c = filled want slots; incomplete if a != 2, b == 0 or c == 0, unless all three are 0 (no offer at all is accepted): 'Your offer is incomplete.\n' (strcpy); then d = filled bluff-replacement slots; d < b appends 'You must declare a bluff replacement.'. Mode 1 (counter-offer row int16 [0x112548]): truthful slots +0..+1, bluff +2, replacement +5; the incomplete text via sprintf + strcat. On error f71B68(text) and the result is -15; on success int32 [0x1105AC + 4n] = c and -1. Mode 1 with success and a, d non-zero: row +0xD = the answered offer's nation (record [0x11256C], byte 0x110EDE + 21r), +0xE = n, +0xF = record +0x13, and the record's +0x14 = n (G: n has countered it).

0x72fc4.purpose: Draws the 'Respond To Offer - Session %d' screen: offer index [0x11256C] = (-0x26 - code) + scroll [0x11255C]; mode [0x110EC8] = 1 (counter-offer); background 15 ([0xEE168] = 0xF). The commodity chart: cardtiny 1..18 at (0x235 + 40*(i&1), 0x18 + 47*(i>>1)). The offer's 2 truthful cards at (0x6D + 39j, 0x75) and its bluffs (with the 0x2000 shift), its 5 wanted cards at (0x153 + 39j, 0x75). The slot rectangles for the reply are written: slots 0..1 at (0x6D + 39j, 0xF2), bluff slots 2.. at (0xC7 + 39j, 0xF2), replacement slots 5.. at (0x166 + 39j, 0xF2), each 32 x 46 (int16 0x111524 + 8s), the hand rectangle slot 13 = (7, 0x196, 0x1F4, 0x2E), each drawn empty (cardtiny 32). n's hand f71FB0(7, 0x196, 0x1F4, n); title, n's name, '%s offers for trade...' (the offerer) at (0x6D, 0x61), '... and wants ...' at (0x153, 0x61); f6FB2C; f6FE68(0x203, 0x19F, n, 0); button 0x103 enabled iff trades exist; f3B05C(0x111D6C); f3CC14.
0x72fc4.globals: reads offer records 0x110ECC (21 bytes each, count [0x112560], built by f726DC: +0x00..+0x0C the nation's +0x9C..+0xA8 (shuffled), +0x0D..+0x11 a second shuffle, +0x12 nation, +0x13, +0x14), [0x11255C], int16 [0x112542], word [0xE1624], int16 [0xF5476], byte [0x110F74]; writes [0x11256C], [0x110EC8], [0xEE168], slot rects 0x111524..0x111592
0x72fc4.calls: f3A044 (ported) x2, f3A18C (ported) x2, f3AF8C (ported) x6, f3B05C (ported), f3BFBC (ported), f3CC14 (ported), f3CD6C (ported), f6FB2C, f6FE68, f71FB0 (ported), sprintf x2, fg_vbcopy, fg_setcolor, fg_vbopen, fg_vbclose
0x72fc4.risks: Writes the slot-rectangle table that the other composer routines read; a literal port must keep it at its address. Two local text buffers via sprintf.

0x734e4.purpose: The ACCEPT TRADES step (game loop 0x54824). Nothing if [0x112560] == 0. In session 1 (int16 [0xF5476] == 1) every computer nation's 9 bytes +0xBE..+0xC6 are cleared (G: who passed it a calamity). f783B8(0x112158, [0xF5958]). Every counter-offer row: its first 3 cards copied to +8..+0xA and, unless variant bit 0x20 of [0xE1625] (G: 'real goods in trade are known'), shuffled (f76F70, random). int16 [0x112542] = 1, [0x112558] = 0, [0x110EC8] = 0, [0xEE168] = 2. For each player p in turn order (0xF06B0, count [0xF40EC]): n = [0xF40F8]; skipped when its offer slot +0x9C is empty; scroll [0x112564] = 0. Human (PBEM: viewer only): f73D4C(n), f7401C(n, 0) unless there is one human, f6FBDC(n, 1), f7401C(n, 1), then the loop: -0x2C / -0x2B scroll +3 / -3; player buttons -0x36..-0x3D: the shown nation becomes that player's (f73D4C + f7401C); -0x2F..-0x31 (no PBEM) f75074(scroll - 0x2F - code) accepts that response; PBEM: -0x2F..-0x31 and -0x97..-0xAB set preferences via f7399C(index, 0..7); -1 next player. Computer: f73D4C, f7401C(n, 0); unless int16 [0xF40C2] the dialog is disabled and f78A20(2000); f6B0EC(n) (AI accepts); dialog restored.
0x734e4.calls: f3C7A0 (ported), f3C940 (ported), f3CD6C (ported), f6B0EC, f6FBDC, f7399C x6, f73D4C x3, f7401C x6, f75074, f76F70 (ported), f783B8 (ported), f78A20 (ported), f78BA4 (ported), memset
0x734e4.waits_for_input: f78BA4(0x112158, 0) loop per human until -1; f78A20(2000) busy wait for each computer unless [0xF40C2]
0x734e4.risks: Indirect game_rand through f76F70 (row shuffles) and f6B0EC (AI). A player button replaces the local nation [ebp-0x30] used by the following f73D4C/f7401C calls but not [0xF40F8], so after viewing another player the list on screen and the one f75074 indexes belong to that player (G: possible 1995 bug, check in DOSBox-X). Seven near-identical range compares for the PBEM preference buttons (ids in groups of three). PBEM branches to drop.

0x7399c.purpose: Sets the acceptance preference of response (scroll [0x112564] + index) to k (edx, 0..7): with k > 0 it first clears k from every other response's +0x13 (0x1114AB + 20i), then stores k. Redraws the three visible rows' radio buttons on dialog 0x112158: id 0x87 + row (f3B914 / f3B728) and the seven preference ids 0xEC + 3j + row (j < count, checked when the preference is j + 1). Button 0x2A becomes 'ACCEPT PREFERRED ORDER' ([0xF4100] = 1) when any preference is set, else 'REJECT ALL OFFERS' ([0xF4100] = 0); f3B05C, f3CC14.
0x7399c.globals: reads/writes 0x1114AB + 20i (preference); reads [0x112564], int16 [0x112568]; writes int16 [0xF4100]; dialog 0x112158
0x7399c.calls: f3B05C (ported), f3B728, f3B914 x8, f3C284 (ported) x2, f3CC14 (ported)
0x7399c.risks: Only reached with PBEM (bit 0x80 of [0xE1624]); dropped with PBEM. Seven unrolled blocks, one per preference column.

0x73d4c.purpose: Builds nation n's response list: response list 0x111498 (20-byte records, count int16 [0x112568]: +0..+0xF a copy of a counter-offer row, +0x10 int16 the gain, +0x12 row index, +0x13 PBEM preference 0..7). memset(0x111498, 0, 0x8C), count 0; v0 = f194E4(n) + f195D8(n) (G: the Goods Held value of n's hand). For each counter-offer row whose +0xD is n: a record = the 16-byte row, +0x12 = row index, +0x13 = 0; nation n is copied to record 0, n's own offer cards are taken out (f75CA8 on +0x9C, +0x9D and the replacements +0xA6..+0xA8), the row's 5 cards +8..+0xC added (f75D84), and +0x10 = f194E4(0) + f195D8(0) - v0. Finally a bubble sort by the gain, largest first (20-byte swaps through a stack temporary).
0x73d4c.globals: reads nation n (+0x99..+0xA8, cards), rows 0x111118 (+0xD), int16 [0x112548]; writes response list 0x111498 (20-byte records, count int16 [0x112568]: +0..+0xF a copy of a counter-offer row, +0x10 int16 the gain, +0x12 row index, +0x13 PBEM preference 0..7), nation record 0, and whatever f194E4/f195D8 write (0xF68B0..)
0x73d4c.calls: f194E4 (ported) x2, f195D8 (ported) x2, f75CA8 x5, f75D84, memset
0x73d4c.risks: Evaluates with the shuffled copy +8.. of the responder's cards (bluffs included, G). memset size 0x8C = 7 records with no count check (more than 7 rows answering one offer would overflow into 0x111524, the slot rectangles: G). Bubble sort with signed int16 compare (jle) - keep the stable order for equal gains.

0x7401c.purpose: Draws the 'Accept Trades - Session %d' screen for nation n (eax), mode edx. Read-only view (ro = 1) if n is a computer or mode 0, else ro = (n != [0xF40F8]). Background 13, f74D54 resets the row buttons, hand rectangle (7, 0x196, 0x23A, 0x2E); hand face down (card backs) if ro or mode 0, else f707A0(n) (hand minus the offer) + f6FE68 and 'Does not' / 'include initial offer' at (7, 0x180/0x18A). The initial offer: n's own truthful cards (0xCF + 39j, 0x58) and replacements (0x133 + 39j) when !ro (or a computer with int16 [0xF40C2]); else the public shuffled offer record (0x110ED9..) with the bluff shift. Up to three responses from scroll [0x112564]: the responder's cards, token and name (+0xE), '%+d' gain unless ro, row buttons 0x87 + row enabled, PBEM preference radios 0xEC + 3j + row; 'N O N E' if none. Button 0x2A: 'REJECT ALL OFFERS' ([0xF4100] = 0) if rows are shown and no preference set, PBEM with a preference 'ACCEPT PREFERRED ORDER' ([0xF4100] = 1), else 'CONTINUE' (two copies). Texts: title, n's name, 'Bluffs replaced by...' (0x133, 0x4C), 'Truly Stated' (0xCF, 0x4C), 'You initially offered...' (0xD9, 0x3A), PBEM 'Trade Acceptance Order Preference', 'If Not Lying' above the gains, 'Offers...' when ro, 'The responses to %s offer...' with 'your' or the adjective 0xC76C4[n] ('African'...). f3B05C(0x112158), f75000 (scroll buttons), button 0x2A enabled iff !ro, f3CC14.
0x7401c.globals: reads response list 0x111498 (20-byte records, count int16 [0x112568]: +0..+0xF a copy of a counter-offer row, +0x10 int16 the gain, +0x12 row index, +0x13 PBEM preference 0..7), offer records 0x110ECC (21 bytes each, count [0x112560], built by f726DC: +0x00..+0x0C the nation's +0x9C..+0xA8 (shuffled), +0x0D..+0x11 a second shuffle, +0x12 nation, +0x13, +0x14), nation n (+0x9A, +0x9C..+0xA8), [0xF40F8], int16 [0xF40C2], word [0xE1624], [0x112564], [0xF595C], int16 [0xF5476], 0xC768C[], 0xC76C4[]; writes int16 [0x112542] = 1, int16 [0x112546] (rows shown), [0xEE168], [0x11254C], int16 [0xF4100], hand rect 0x11158C..0x111592, dialog 0x112158 (count int16 = [0xF595C])
0x7401c.calls: f39F90 (ported) x2, f3A044 (ported) x7, f3A0B0 (ported) x4, f3A18C (ported) x2, f3AF8C (ported) x7, f3B05C (ported), f3B914 x8, f3BFBC (ported) x8, f3C0D8 (ported) x8, f3C284 (ported) x3, f3C314 (ported), f3C3D0 (ported), f3CC14 (ported), f3CD6C (ported), f6FE68, f707A0, f74D54, f75000, f76F14 (ported), sprintf x3, fg_vbcopy, fg_setcolor x3, fg_vbopen x2, fg_vbclose
0x7401c.risks: 3384 bytes of straight-line drawing with PBEM branches (radios, preference texts, x offsets 0xA1/0xB5 and 0x95/0xA9 chosen by bit 0x80) and seven unrolled preference blocks. Text built with sprintf into a 0xA0 stack buffer. 'Truly Stated' here vs 'Truly stated' in 0x70A6C.

0x74d54.purpose: Resets the three response rows' buttons on dialog 0x112158: id 0x87 + row disabled with style 2 (f3C0D8); with PBEM the label 'REJECT' at x 0x17A, width 0x32, f3C1F4(id, 1); without PBEM 'ACCEPT OFFER' at x 0x198, width 0x6E, f3C1F4(id, 0) and the seven preference radios 0xEC + 3j + row get style 2; then all seven preference ids are disabled (f3BFBC 0).
0x74d54.globals: dialog 0x112158 records (labels, x, width, style, enabled); reads byte [0xE1624] (0x80)
0x74d54.calls: f3BB48 (ported) x2, f3BD80 (ported) x2, f3BFBC (ported) x8, f3C0D8 (ported) x8, f3C1F4 x2, f3C284 (ported) x2
0x74d54.risks: PBEM branch; f3C1F4 is unported (UI kit). Loop re-enters the middle of its body through a jmp (Watcom layout).

0x75000.purpose: Enables or disables the scroll buttons of dialog 0x112158: 0x85 (up) iff [0x112564] > 0, 0x86 (down) iff [0x112564] + 3 < int16 [0x112568].

0x75074.purpose: Carries out accepted response i (eax) of the list 0x111498: A = the offerer (+0xD), B = the responder (+0xE), r = the row (+0x12). Pre-trade copies of both nation records go to the stack (199 bytes each). Trade t = byte [0x110F74]: A's cards = the offer record's +0x0D..+0x11 (found by its +0x12 == A) -> 0x110F75 + 5t, B's = row +8..+0xC -> 0x111015 + 5t, nations -> 0x1110B5[t] / 0x1110D5[t], session byte [0xF5476] -> 0x1110F5[t]; count + 1. f75A1C(A, r) fills the detail block 0x112570; if A gives a calamity (byte [0x112572] > 18): A's +0xBD+B = 1 and every other computer m with m's +0xBD+A set has it moved to m's +0xBD+B (G: who passed calamities); the same for B ([0x11257B]). f75C08 swaps the cards, f6E460(A), f6E460(B), f75DF0 withdraws the offer, f75EB4 / f75F08 drop the other offers and counter-offers of A and B. A human A gets f75520(0, A, B, &preA); B human (no PBEM) f75520(1, B, A, &preB); both computers: f75FB4(A) (Trade Summary). A computer's trust in the other, byte +0xB1 + other, += int8 table 0xCA994[4*level] (20/15/10 by bits 10..11 (0x0C00) of word [0xE1624], G: the AI level) times the other's honesty byte (+1 / -1, [0x112581] / [0x112578]), clamped to -15..100.
0x75074.globals: reads response list 0x111498 (20-byte records, count int16 [0x112568]: +0..+0xF a copy of a counter-offer row, +0x10 int16 the gain, +0x12 row index, +0x13 PBEM preference 0..7), offer records 0x110ECC (21 bytes each, count [0x112560], built by f726DC: +0x00..+0x0C the nation's +0x9C..+0xA8 (shuffled), +0x0D..+0x11 a second shuffle, +0x12 nation, +0x13, +0x14), counter-offer rows 0x111118 + 16r (count int16 [0x112548]: +0..+1 truthful cards, +2..+4 bluffs, +5..+7 replacements, +8..+0xC shuffled copy (0x734E4), +0xD the answered offer's nation, +0xE the responder, +0xF); writes trades 0x110F74 (count), 0x110F75[32][5], 0x111015[32][5], 0x1110B5[32], 0x1110D5[32], 0x1110F5[32]; nations +0xB1+m (trust), +0xBD+m; detail block 0x112570..0x112581; reads word [0xE1624], byte [0xF5476], nations +0x3D, +0x9A
0x75074.waits_for_input: through f75520 / f75FB4 (CONTINUE or the unattended timer)
0x75074.risks: Two 199-byte nation copies on the stack (0x1B8-byte frame) passed by pointer to f75520: a port has to give them stable addresses or pass C pointers. No bound on 32 trades (byte count, 5t indexing into fixed arrays). The level table 0xCA994 has 3 entries; level 3 would read 0xCA9A0 (the slot table, 0). The search for the offer record falls through with index = count if none matches (D).

0x75520.purpose: The 'Trade Details' screen for one side of a trade: side eax (0/1), nation n (edx), partner (ebx), ecx = pointer to n's 199-byte pre-trade record (a caller's stack copy, or 0xF2A94 + 199n). Background 14; title and n's name; side 1 first f3CC14 and f6FBDC(n, 0) (G: hand the screen to the second player). 'Pre-Trade': the record is copied over nation record 0 and drawn with f71FB0(0x37, 0x3C, 0x1CC, 0) and f6FE68(0x203, 0x46, 0, 1). 'You traded' (right-aligned at 0xBE): the side's truthful cards and replacements at (0xC8 + 39j, 0x78), ' to %s'; 'You received' with the other side's cards at y 0xC8; '%s was bluffing with' and the other side's declared bluffs at y 0x104 (empty slots = cardtiny 32). 'Post-Trade' with n's current hand f71FB0(0x37, 0x154, 0x1CC, n) and f6FE68(0x203, 0x154, n, 1). CONTINUE 0xBB800 moved to (0x109, 0x1AE).
0x75520.globals: reads detail block 0x112570 (2 x 9 bytes, side s at 0x112570 + 9s: +0..+1 truthful cards, +2..+4 the cards really given in place of the bluffs (replacements), +5..+7 the declared bluffs, +8 int8 1 = honest / -1 = bluffed), nation n, 0xC768C[]; writes [0xEE168], nation record 0 (from the pre-trade copy); dialog 0xBB800 position; reads int16 [0xF40BA]
0x75520.calls: f39F90 (ported), f3A044 (ported) x2, f3A18C (ported) x2, f3A3A0 (ported) x4, f3AF8C (ported) x5, f3B05C (ported), f3BB48 (ported), f3BC64 (ported), f3CC14 (ported) x2, f3CD6C (ported), f6FBDC, f6FE68 x2, f71FB0 (ported) x2, f78A20 (ported), f78BA4 (ported), f7BA64 (ported), sprintf x3, fg_vbcopy, fg_setcolor x2, fg_vbopen x3, fg_vbclose x3
0x75520.waits_for_input: f78BA4(0xBB800, 0) until -1, or when f7BA64 says unattended f78A20(250, or 1000 with [0xF40BA])
0x75520.risks: Takes a pointer to a caller's stack buffer (0x75074's local copies) and copies it into the nation table; the PBEM caller passes 0xF2A94 + 199n. The 'bluffing with' row shows the other side's declared bluffs even when it did not bluff (G: same cards).

0x75a1c.purpose: Fills the trade detail block: memset(0x112570, 0, 0x12); side 0 from the offerer's record (eax): +0x9C, +0x9D, the replacements +0xA6..+0xA8 (start1[3]) to +2..+4, the bluffs +0x9E..+0xA0 (start1[1]) to +5..+7, +8 = 1, or -1 if any of +2..+4 differs from +5..+7; side 1 from counter-offer row r (edx): +0, +1, +5..+7 to +2..+4, +2..+4 to +5..+7, honesty in 0x112581.
0x75a1c.globals: writes detail block 0x112570 (2 x 9 bytes, side s at 0x112570 + 9s: +0..+1 truthful cards, +2..+4 the cards really given in place of the bluffs (replacements), +5..+7 the declared bluffs, +8 int8 1 = honest / -1 = bluffed); reads nation +0x9C..+0xA8, row 0x111118 + 16r, bytes 0xCA9A1/0xCA9A3
0x75a1c.risks: The honesty loops compare from index 2 to 4 of the 0x112570 array against 0x112573.. (+3), i.e. replacements vs bluffs: keep the byte offsets exactly.

0x75bd4.purpose: Tradable-card test: returns byte [0xC95C5 + c] for c > 18 (1 for the tradable calamities 0x14, 0x16, 0x18, 0x1A..0x1E, 0 for 0x13, 0x15, 0x17, 0x19), 0 for commodities.

0x75c08.purpose: Swaps the cards of a trade: for j < 5 removes side 0's card 0x112570[j] from record A (eax) and side 1's 0x112579[j] from record B (edx) (f75CA8), then for j < 5 adds side 1's card to A (f75D84(card, A, B)) and side 0's to B.
0x75c08.globals: reads detail block 0x112570..0x11257D; writes the two nation records' cards
0x75c08.risks: Record pointers in, not nation numbers (callers pass 0xF14CC + 199n).

0x75ca8.purpose: Removes card c (al, 0 ignored) from the nation record at edx: c <= 18 decrements +c; a calamity is found in +0x14.. (count +0x13), the lists +0x14 / +0x1C shifted down, count - 1, last entries 0 / 0xFF.
0x75ca8.risks: Uninitialised start index [ebp-0x8] if the calamity is not held (D).

0x75d84.purpose: Adds card c (al, 0 ignored) to the nation record at edx: c <= 18 increments +c; a calamity is appended at +0x14 + count with the giver's nation (byte +0x3D of the record at ebx) at +0x1C + count, count + 1.
0x75d84.globals: nation record (pointer): +0x01..+0x12, +0x13, +0x14..+0x23; reads +0x3D of the giver

0x75df0.purpose: Withdraws nation n's offer: memset(nation +0x9C + byte [0xCA9A0], 0, 13), then deletes every counter-offer row whose +0xD (the answered offer) is n, compacting the 16-byte rows and decrementing int16 [0x112548].
0x75df0.globals: writes nation n +0x9C..+0xA8, rows 0x111118 and int16 [0x112548]
0x75df0.risks: The row loop re-tests the same index after a deletion via dec/inc of the counter (Watcom loop shape).

0x75eb4.purpose: After a trade between A (eax) and B (edx): f75DF0 for each of them whose offer slot +0x9C is still set.

0x75f08.purpose: After a trade between A and B: deletes every counter-offer row made by A or B (row +0xE), compacting the rows and decrementing int16 [0x112548].

0x75fb4.purpose: The 'Trade Summary - Session %d' screen shown to the humans after a trade between two computers: background 14, title with int16 [0xF5476]; only the last trade t = [0x110F74] - 1 at y 0xDC: '<-->' (font 2), A's token and name at x 0xF5..., A's 5 cards, B's token, name and 5 cards (0x110F75 / 0x111015 + 5t, 0x1110B5 / 0x1110D5); CONTINUE 0xBB800 at (0x109, 0x1AE).
0x75fb4.globals: reads trades 0x110F74.., token sprites 0xF4ACC + 8n, 0xC768C[], int16 [0xF5476], int16 [0xF40BA]; writes [0xEE168]
0x75fb4.calls: f39F90 (ported) x2, f3A0B0 (ported) x3, f3A18C (ported), f3AF8C (ported) x4, f3B05C (ported), f3BB48 (ported), f3BC64 (ported), f3CC14 (ported), f3CD6C (ported), f78A20 (ported), f78BA4 (ported), f7BA64 (ported), sprintf, fg_vbcopy, fg_setcolor, fg_vbopen, fg_vbclose
0x75fb4.waits_for_input: f78BA4(0xBB800, 0) until -1, or the unattended timer (250 / 1000 ms)
0x75fb4.risks: The argument (nation A) is stored and never used.

0x762e0.purpose: PBEM: shows the viewer [0xE1622] the details of its trades of this round. Only when int16 [0xF4100] == 1 and int8 [0xF4877 + viewer] >= 0: 18 bytes from 0xF47D4 + 18*(viewer - 1) into the detail block 0x112570, then for every trade t with the viewer as A or B: f75520(side, viewer, partner, 0xF2A94 + 199*viewer). Finally int16 [0xF4100] = 0.
0x762e0.globals: reads byte [0xE1622], int16 [0xF4100], 0xF4877[], 0xF47D4 (18-byte records), trades 0x110F74.., 0xF2A94 + 199n (G: saved pre-trade nation copies); writes 0x112570.., int16 [0xF4100]
0x762e0.risks: PBEM only (in a hot-seat game [0xF4100] is never 1): drop with PBEM. All trades shown with the same detail block.

0x76e50.purpose: Draws the top card of trade-card stack s (eax) for nation n (edx): if int16 [0xF06D0 + 25s] != 0 it is decremented and the card is byte [0xF06D6 + 25s + count]; a calamity (> 18) is appended to n's +0x14 + count (count +0x13 + 1, the giver byte +0x1C not written), a commodity increments n's +c. Returns the card, 0 for an empty stack.
0x76e50.globals: stacks 0xF06D0 + 25s (int16 count, cards from +6); nation n +0x01..+0x14
0x76e50.callers: f5195C (0x53007, 0x53048); DrawTradingCards 0x6BD98 (0x6C671); f6D178 (0x6D29F, 0x6D41F); f6D564 (0x6D5F3, 0x6D8F8); f6DBAC (0x6DCB8); f6DE04 (0x6E10E)
0x76e50.risks: Leaves +0x1C + count (the giver) as it was. No bound on 8 calamity entries. eax read by the 9 callers.

0x7701c.purpose: Deterministic shuffle of n (eax) bytes at edx for AI slot k (ebx) using the AI random table 0x112A94 (int16[30][10], made by f7BCD4 with game_rand): copies to a 188-byte local, then repeatedly takes index table[j mod 30][k] / (30000 / min(n, 30000)) (n - 1 if that is >= n), writes that element out and closes the gap.
0x7701c.risks: No game_rand here (the table was filled earlier). Stack local of 0xBC bytes: n > 188 overflows (D). Signed idiv twice per pick.

0x771f8.purpose: Puts card c (eax) on its discard pile: stack s = (c - 1) / 2 for commodities, byte [0xCA9C1 + c] for calamities (0x13..0x1E -> 1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,5,6,7,8); appends c at 0xF07BA + 25s + count, int16 [0xF07B4 + 25s] + 1.
